notes: Queue for the QA loop. Statuses: open | in_progress | done | blocked | regressed. cycle.py takes the highest severity open item; triage.py appends what the automated pass found.

items.title: Ribbon clips its primary action at 1280px (Compile cut off)
items.why: At a 1280x800 window the Build group's Compile button is clipped by the viewport edge, so the most important action is half-invisible. Word keeps every group reachable at narrow widths.
items.hint: Reproduce with `node qa/smoke.mjs` (it records ribbon overflow observations and qa/shots/03-ribbon-*.png). Fix in CSS first: the ribbon should not overflow the window — allow groups to shrink the wide labels to icons or scroll horizontally inside .ribbon-content. Do not reorder or remove commands.
items.note: first fix was insufficient; real fix: .app-shell explicit minmax(0,1fr) column

items.title: Word-standard editing shortcuts missing (Ctrl+K link, Ctrl+Shift+7/8 lists, Ctrl+1/2/5 spacing, Tab indent)
items.why: The smoke pass confirmed these keys do nothing. Anyone coming from Word hits them in the first minute.
items.hint: App.tsx has a keydown effect that only handles Ctrl+S and Ctrl+Enter — extend that pattern. Ctrl+K should open the existing link dialog, Ctrl+Shift+7/8 toggle ordered/bullet lists through Tiptap commands, Ctrl+1/2/5 apply the existing line-spacing styles, Tab/Shift+Tab indent or outdent the current list/paragraph instead of leaving the editor. Every shortcut must keep working inside the LaTeX source textarea without hijacking it.

items.title: No Find & Replace (Ctrl+F / Ctrl+H)
items.why: Searching a manuscript is table stakes; there is no find UI anywhere in the app.
items.hint: Add a small non-modal find bar anchored top-right of the editor column (not a modal). Ctrl+F opens it and prefills with the current selection, Enter/Shift+Enter walk matches, Escape closes and returns focus to the page. Ctrl+H reveals the replace field with Replace / Replace all. Use the Tiptap editor's own document search (ProseMirror positions) so matches highlight in the visual editor; in source mode search the textarea. Keep the LaTeX round trip untouched.

items.title: No discoverable Visual / Source / Split switcher in the editor chrome
items.why: The status bar prints the current mode as static text and nothing in the ribbon switches modes, so the split view is effectively hidden.
items.hint: App.tsx already has setMode(nextMode) and an EditorMode of visual|source|split. Make the status-bar mode segment a segmented control (Visual / Source / Split) and add a matching View-tab group in the ribbon. Keyboard: Ctrl+Alt+1/2/3.

items.title: Browser demo workspace does not survive a reload (everything is lost)
items.why: In browser mode the app adopts demoWorkspace() and the top bar still says 'Saved locally', but nothing is persisted. Reloading loses the document — the label is a lie and it blocks multi-turn testing.
items.hint: When !isDesktop, persist the workspace to localStorage on the existing autosave debounce and restore it on boot (recent documents list too). Keep the desktop path unchanged. Do not fake file-system success.

items.title: Zoom has no keyboard or gesture path and no fit-width
items.why: Status bar zoom buttons are the only way to zoom; Word users expect Ctrl+wheel and a fit-width option.
items.hint: Ctrl/Cmd+wheel over the page area changes zoom in the existing 70-150 range; Ctrl+0 resets to 100%; add a small fit-width button next to the zoom percentage. Do not let browser page zoom interfere (preventDefault on the wheel handler).

items.title: Start screen footer is hardcoded 'Sentence 0.1' while the app is 0.2.0
items.why: Version is triple-tracked in package.json, Cargo.toml and tauri.conf.json; the UI shows a fourth, stale number.
items.hint: Inject the version at build time (define in vite.config.ts from package.json) and render it, so bumping package.json cannot drift.

items.title: No print path (Ctrl+P) with paper-accurate styles
items.why: Word's most-used output besides save is print; the app can only export through the desktop Tectonic build.
items.hint: Ctrl+P calls window.print(). Add an @media print block that hides ribbon, sidebar and status bar, removes page shadows and background chrome, and prints the page sheet at its true width. Verify with a headless PDF print in the smoke script (page.pdf()) that the ribbon does not appear.

items.title: Nested lists are destroyed when LaTeX source is applied
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (functional): expected The edited source re-imports as a two-level nested list: 'renamed parent' with an indented 'keep child' item, and the LaTeX stays a nested itemize environment.
items.hint:
Repro: In a new document, clear the editor (Ctrl+A, Backspace). Click Home > Bulleted list, type 'keep parent', press Enter, press Tab, type 'keep child'. Click View > LaTeX, change 'keep parent' to 'renamed parent' in the LaTeX source textarea, click 'Apply source', then click View > Visual. (The same happens if you apply hand-authored LaTeX containing a nested \begin{enumerate} inside a \begin{itemize}.)
Actual: The visual editor shows a flat two-item bulleted list whose item texts literally contain '\begin{itemize}' and '\end{itemize}' ('renamed parent \begin{itemize}' / 'keep child \end{itemize}'). Switching back to LaTeX shows the environment commands escaped as '\textbackslash{}begin\{itemize\}' and '\textbackslash{}end\{itemize\}' instead of a nested environment. Applying hand-authored mixed itemize/enumerate likewise flattens all items into the outer list type and leaves '\begin{enumerate}' / '\end{enumerate}' as visible text. No console errors were emitted.
items.source: explore:lists:nested lists are destroyed when latex source is applied

items.title: $...$ inline math from LaTeX source is silently turned into escaped plain text
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (functional): expected `$E=mc^2$` is parsed as an editable inline math node, and the re-exported source still contains the math expression.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. Type `Inline `, Insert tab > Inline equation with `E=mc^2`, type ` tail`, Insert tab > Equation block with `a^2+b^2=c^2`. View > LaTeX: the source has `Inline \(E=mc^2\) tail` and an `equation*` block. Change only that inline expression to `Inline $E=mc^2$ tail`, click Apply source, then View > Visual, then View > LaTeX again.
Actual: No inline math node remains: the visual paragraph reads `Inline $E=mc^2$ tail` as literal text (the display equation survives). Re-exporting writes `Inline \$E=mc\textasciicircum{}2\$ tail`, so the math is corrupted on round-trip.
items.source: explore:math:$...$ inline math from latex source is silently turned into escaped plain text

items.title: Numbered equation environment from LaTeX source is not recognized and is escaped as text
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (functional): expected The numbered equation is imported as an editable display math node and re-exported as an equation environment.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project with inline math `E=mc^2` and an equation block `a^2+b^2=c^2` via the Insert tab. View > LaTeX, change `\begin{equation*}` / `\end{equation*}` to `\begin{equation}` / `\end{equation}`, click Apply source, then View > Visual and View > LaTeX again.
Actual: The display math node disappears and the visual document shows the raw lines `\begin{equation}`, `a^2+b^2=c^2`, `\end{equation}` as text. Re-exported source contains `\textbackslash{}begin\{equation\}` and `a\textasciicircum{}2+b\textasciicircum{}2=c\textasciicircum{}2`, destroying the equation.
items.source: explore:math:numbered equation environment from latex source is not recognized and is escaped as text

items.title: Undefined control sequence in math is accepted: no error flag and Insert stays enabled
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (functional): expected An undefined command is flagged as invalid (as `\frac{` is), the Insert button is disabled, and an error message is shown instead of writing uncompilable LaTeX into the document.
items.hint:
Repro: Insert tab > Inline equation, type `\badcommand{x}` in the LaTeX source field, inspect the preview and the Insert button, then click Insert and switch View > LaTeX.
Actual: KaTeX renders the command in red (`mstyle mathcolor="#cc0000"`), but the preview has no `.math-preview-invalid`/`.katex-error` class and Insert is enabled. After insertion the document contains `\(\badcommand{x}\)` in the generated source with no error reported to the user. By contrast `\frac{`, `x^{` and `\begin{` correctly show `.katex-error` and disable Insert.

items.title: Clicking a math node, cancelling the edit dialog, then pressing Backspace does not delete it

items.title: Applying LaTeX containing \texttt wipes the entire visual document
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (functional): expected The new paragraph renders in the visual editor and stays in the exported LaTeX alongside the existing body.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project and switch View > LaTeX. Append the line `Code: \texttt{CODE MARKER}` before `\end{document}`, click Apply source, then View > Visual. Switch back to View > LaTeX to read the generated source.
Actual: The visual editor is empty (innerHTML 122 chars, placeholder only): both headings, all paragraphs and the quote disappear, the toast says 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.', and the re-exported source contains only front matter through `\keywords{...}` with no body. The app's unmodified exported source triggers the same wipe because it contains `\texttt{meaning = structure + language}`; an in-page check of /src/lib/latex.ts shows that command is parsed into a text node with mark type `inlineCode`.
items.source: explore:source-editor:applying latex containing \texttt wipes the entire visual document

items.title: Malformed LaTeX with a missing \end{document} is applied silently and clears the document
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (functional): expected The app reports the invalid LaTeX and keeps the previous document; the sentinel and original body remain.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. View > LaTeX: replace `\texttt{meaning = structure + language}` with plain text and add `SENTINEL BEFORE BREAK` before `\end{document}`, click Apply source, then View > Visual and confirm the sentinel is visible. Return to View > LaTeX, delete only the `\end{document}` line, click Apply source, then View > Visual.
Actual: Apply source is enabled, the toast says 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.', and no alert or error text appears. The visual editor is empty (innerHTML 122 chars), the status bar reads 0 words, and re-exported LaTeX has only front matter - the sentinel and all body content are gone.
items.source: explore:source-editor:malformed latex with a missing \end{document} is applied silently and clears the document

items.title: Unbalanced table environment is stored as escaped text with no error
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (functional): expected The unbalanced environment is reported as invalid LaTeX and the previous document is preserved.

Repro: Create a project. View > LaTeX, replace `\texttt{meaning = structure + language}` with plain text, append `\section{Unbalanced section}`, `\begin{table}[htbp]` and `SENTINEL UNBALANCED` before `\end{document}` (no `\end{table}`), click Apply source, then View > Visual and View > LaTeX.
Actual: Apply source succeeds with the success toast and no error message. The visual editor shows the raw lines `\section{Unbalanced section}`, `\begin{table}[htbp]` and `SENTINEL UNBALANCED` as plain text, and the re-exported source escapes them as `\textbackslash{}section\{Unbalanced section\}` and `\textbackslash{}begin\{table\}[htbp]`, corrupting the LaTeX.
items.source: explore:source-editor:unbalanced table environment is stored as escaped text with no error

items.title: Source edits in Split mode are not applied when switching to Visual

items.title: Status bar page count ignores page breaks and visual document length
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (functional): expected The status bar page count should reflect the visible document length and increase when explicit page breaks are added (the two breaks grow the sheet by ~2,567px).
items.hint:
Repro: Run `node qa/probes/long-document.mjs`. After it builds 50 headings and ~6,050 words the status bar reads '13 pages' while the `.paper-sheet` is 17,440px tall (scrollHeight 17,550px). Then, in the same document, place the caret at the end and click Insert > Page break twice, typing text between and after the breaks; the sheet grows to 20,007px, the LaTeX gains two `\newpage` commands, but the status bar still reads '13 pages'.
Actual: With 6,050 words the status bar reads 13 pages for a 17,440px sheet; after two explicit page breaks (verified as two `\newpage` lines in the LaTeX source) the sheet is 20,007px tall and the status bar still reads 13 pages. Word count itself stays correct (6,050 -> 6,072 after the added text).
items.source: explore:long-document:status bar page count ignores page breaks and visual document length

items.title: Browser document is lost on reload while the UI reports it as saved
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (functional): expected Once the indicator reads 'Saved locally' (and especially after a Save click reports 'Saved to disk.'), reloading should restore the edited document. If nothing is persisted, the indicator and toast should not claim a successful save.
items.hint:
Repro: On http://localhost:1420 click 'Create a project'. Type ` PERSIST-RELOAD-MARKER-7Q` at the end of the document and wait ~1.6s until the top-bar sublabel under the project name reads 'Saved locally' (View > LaTeX shows the marker in the exported source). Click the Save button and note the toast. Reload the page, then click 'Create a project' again on the Start screen and inspect the visual editor and View > LaTeX source. Run the same reload immediately after typing, before the autosave debounce fires.
Actual: The Save click shows the toast 'Saved to disk.' and the sublabel becomes 'Saved locally', but reload returns to the Start screen with no recent documents. After creating a project again the marker is absent from both the visual editor and the exported LaTeX; the original demo body is back. localStorage before reload contains only `sentence.gitAuthor` - no document snapshot is written. Reloading immediately after typing (sublabel 'Editing') also loses the text and shows no beforeunload confirmation (0 dialogs observed).
items.source: explore:persistence:browser document is lost on reload while the ui reports it as saved
items.note: duplicate of qa-005 (browser workspace does not survive reload)

items.title: Opening or returning to Visual view flips an unchanged document to 'Editing'

Actual: The sublabel changes to 'Editing' even though the editor's innerText is unchanged (probe comparison true); it returns to 'Saved locally' only after another ~1.1s autosave. Immediately after project creation the sublabel also reads 'Editing'.
items.source: explore:persistence:opening or returning to visual view flips an unchanged document to 'editing'
items.note: verified fixed by bf241b6: Visual -> LaTeX -> Visual with no edit leaves the top bar at 'Saved locally' and the document at 92 words (was flipping to 'Editing')

items.title: Deleted table is resurrected on source/visual switch

Repro: Create a new project, Insert tab > Insert table, click the centre cell and type `victim`. Switch View > LaTeX (the source contains a tabular with `victim`), switch back to View > Visual, click the centre cell again, then Insert tab > Delete table. The table disappears. Actual: Immediately after the click the editor shows only an empty paragraph, but View > LaTeX still shows `\begin{tabular}{lll}` with `victim`, and switching back to View > Visual restores the full 3x3 table with `victim`. The Delete table button then becomes disabled again even though the table is visible, and typing after the round trip leaves the restored table in the document.
items.source: explore:tables:deleted table is resurrected on source/visual switch

items.title: Single-column LaTeX tabular becomes escaped plain text instead of a table
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (functional): expected An editable one-column table with the three rows, and re-exported LaTeX keeps the table environment.
items.hint:
Repro: Insert a 3x3 table, switch View > LaTeX, replace the table block with `\begin{table}[htbp]`, `\centering`, `\begin{tabular}{l}`, `\hline`, rows `Only \\`, `a \\`, `b \\`, `\hline`, `\end{tabular}`, `\end{table}`, click Apply source, then View > Visual.
Actual: No table exists. The body shows the raw LaTeX as one paragraph (`\begin{table}[htbp] \centering \begin{tabular}{l} ...`). The next LaTeX export escapes it as `\textbackslash{}begin\{table\}[htbp]` etc., corrupting the document source.
items.source: explore:tables:single-column latex tabular becomes escaped plain text instead of a table

items.title: Text in a second paragraph of a table cell is dropped from LaTeX
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (functional): expected Both lines from the cell appear in the tabular row (for example `first line\par second line` or `first line second line &  &  \\`).
items.hint:
Repro: Insert a 3x3 table, click the top-left cell, type `first line`, press Enter, type `second line`, then switch View > LaTeX.
Actual: The visual cell shows two paragraphs (`first line` and `second line`), but the exported tabular row contains only `first line &  &  \\`; `second line` is absent from the source.
items.source: explore:tables:text in a second paragraph of a table cell is dropped from latex

items.title: No visual controls to add or remove table rows or columns
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (functional): expected The visual editor offers a way to insert and delete a row or column near the cursor.
items.hint:
Repro: Insert a 3x3 table with a header row, click the centre body cell, inspect the buttons on every ribbon tab (Home, Insert, Layout, References, Review, Paper, View, Git), right-click the cell, and try Alt+Enter, Alt+Insert, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+Shift+Equal and Ctrl+Shift+Backspace.
Actual: The only table controls anywhere are Insert table and Delete table. Right-clicking a cell opens no menu, none of the tried shortcuts changes the table, and Tab at the end of the last row only appends a row (3x3 becomes 4x3). Rows/columns can only be changed by hand-editing LaTeX source; there is no way to remove a single row or column visually.
items.source: explore:tables:no visual controls to add or remove table rows or columns

items.title: Math dialog accepts unknown LaTeX commands that KaTeX renders as errors
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (functional): expected Invalid/unknown LaTeX should be flagged as an error and the Insert button should be disabled, as it is for malformed input like `\frac{`.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Open the app and create a new project.
2. On the Insert tab, click 'Inline equation'.
3. In the LaTeX source textarea, enter `\badcommand{x}`.
4. Observe the preview and the Insert button state.
Actual: The preview renders the command in red error styling but the dialog reports no katex-error/invalid state (`hasKatexError: false`, no `math-preview-invalid` class) and the Insert button remains enabled. The same input can be inserted into the document.
items.source: explore:math:math dialog accepts unknown latex commands that katex renders as errors

items.title: Math node cannot be removed with Backspace/Delete after closing its edit dialog
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (ux): expected After dismissing the edit dialog, the math node should be selectable/removable by keyboard, or there should be an obvious delete affordance.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a new project.
2. Insert an inline equation with value `x+1` (Insert > Inline equation, type `x+1`, click Insert).
3. Click the inserted math node in the editor; the edit dialog opens.
4. Press Escape to close the dialog.
5. Press Backspace (or Delete).
Actual: After Escape closes the dialog, pressing Backspace or Delete does not remove the math node; the node remains in the document. The probe observed the node still present after both Backspace and Delete following dialog dismissal.
items.source: explore:math:math node cannot be removed with backspace/delete after closing its edit dialog

items.title: Rejecting an older tracked revision discards later edits and resurrects previously rejected text
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected Rejecting the EARLY revision should undo only ' EARLY' and leave ' LATE' intact; the previously rejected ' delta-two' must stay rejected.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. In a fresh document type 'Baseline revision text'. 2. Review tab > Track changes (button becomes 'Tracking on'). 3. Type ' delta-one', wait 2s, click Accept on the pending card. 4. Type ' delta-two', wait 2s, click Reject on its card; editor now reads 'Baseline revision text delta-one'. 5. Type ' EARLY', wait 2s, then type ' LATE', wait 2s. Two pending cards appear (newest first: LATE, then EARLY). 6. Click Reject on the second (older, EARLY) card. 7. Read the editor text and switch to View > LaTeX to read document.tex.
Actual: Editor text changed from 'Baseline revision text delta-one EARLY LATE' to 'Baseline revision text delta-one delta-two'; both EARLY and LATE were lost and the earlier rejected 'delta-two' came back. The exported LaTeX body showed the same 'Baseline revision text delta-one delta-two'. After the click only the LATE card remained, still claiming after='Baseline revision text delta-one EARLY LATE'.
items.source: explore:review:rejecting an older tracked revision discards later edits and resurrects previously rejected text

items.title: No UI to add a reply to a comment thread
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected A comment thread offers a way to add a reply, as implied by the review comment workflow and the reply pane in the thread model.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Type text, select it, Review tab > New comment, enter a body, click Comment. 2. In the Review sidebar click the comment thread, then double-click its body. 3. Inspect every control and input inside the thread and sidebar panel.
Actual: Thread exposes only two icon buttons (titles 'Resolve comment' and 'Delete comment'); inputs=[] and no reply/respond text appears before or after clicking or double-clicking. Thread reply count stays 0 and the probe's replyMatches list is empty.
items.source: explore:review:no ui to add a reply to a comment thread

items.title: Deleting a comment leaves an orphaned highlight in the document
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected Deleting a thread removes its comment mark from the document, so the highlight disappears and cannot reference a missing thread.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Add a comment to selected text (e.g. 'Quoted sentence for review') and submit it. 2. In the Review sidebar click the 'Delete comment' icon on the thread. 3. Count [data-comment-id] elements in the editor and click the remaining highlighted text.
Actual: Thread count dropped 1 -> 0 but highlight count stayed 1 with the same mark id (e.g. '12db0404-998a-4630-9649-63aa56a2b36e') and class 'comment-highlight'. Clicking that orphan highlight switched the sidebar to Review/Comments yet showed zero threads ('Select text and choose New comment...' empty state).
items.source: explore:review:deleting a comment leaves an orphaned highlight in the document

items.title: Rejecting a tracked revision leaves a stale baseline for the next revision
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected The next revision's before text should reflect the document after the rejection ('Baseline revision text delta-one'), not text that was just rejected.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Type 'Baseline revision text', turn on Track changes, type ' delta-one', wait 2s and Accept it. 2. Type ' delta-two', wait 2s, click Reject; editor returns to 'Baseline revision text delta-one'. 3. With tracking still on type ' EARLY', wait 2s, type ' LATE', wait 2s. 4. Read the 'before' text of the second (EARLY) revision card in the Review panel.
Actual: The EARLY card showed before='Baseline revision text delta-one delta-two' even though 'delta-two' had been rejected and was absent from the editor; probe flag staleBaselineEvidence=true.
items.source: explore:review:rejecting a tracked revision leaves a stale baseline for the next revision

items.title: Re-clicking the active LaTeX mode button silently discards unapplied source edits
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (functional): expected Re-selecting the already active mode is a no-op, so ZXRECLICK remains in the textarea, or the app warns before discarding unapplied source edits.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project (New document), click View > LaTeX. At the end of the LaTeX source textarea type ZXRECLICK with the keyboard and do NOT click Apply source. Click the View ribbon tab, then click the LaTeX button again while LaTeX mode is already active, and read the textarea.
Actual: The textarea is regenerated from the visual document and ZXRECLICK is gone with no warning. The probe confirmed the marker is still present after clicking only the View tab (afterViewTabOnly=true) and disappears immediately after the LaTeX button click (before=true, after=false).
items.source: explore:source-editor:re-clicking the active latex mode button silently discards unapplied source edits

items.title: Ctrl+Z in the source textarea undoes one character at a time instead of the typed token
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (ux): expected One Ctrl+Z removes the just-typed token, as in a native textarea; the probe's native textarea control went from "ZXUNDO" to "" with one Ctrl+Z.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project, click View > LaTeX, click at the end of the source textarea and type ZXUNDO as normal keystrokes. Press Ctrl+Z once and read the textarea tail.
Actual: Only the final character is removed: the tail reads ZXUND. Seven Ctrl+Z presses total are needed to restore the text before typing, and Ctrl+Shift+Z restores one character at a time. The source document itself is never damaged by the undos.
items.source: explore:source-editor:ctrl+z in the source textarea undoes one character at a time instead of the typed token

items.title: Edits inside the autosave debounce are lost on reload with no warning
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (functional): expected Recent edits are flushed or the app warns before navigating away, so the typed marker survives the reload.
items.hint:
Repro: In the browser app, type a unique marker such as 'persist-beta-X' at the end of the document, then immediately reload the page while the document heading still says 'Editing' (the probe reloads about 300 ms after typing, before the 1100 ms autosave timer). Inspect document.body innerText and the localStorage key sentence.workspace before and after the reload.
Actual: Before reload the marker is visible in the editor, the heading says 'Editing', and sentence.workspace does not contain the marker. The reload completes with no prompt; afterwards the marker is absent from both the editor and storage, while text autosaved earlier is still present.
items.source: explore:persistence:edits inside the autosave debounce are lost on reload with no warning

items.title: Undo appears enabled but is a no-op after reload
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (ux): expected Undo is disabled when no undo history exists, or an enabled Undo performs a visible change.
items.hint:
Repro: In the browser app, type a marker, wait 1.5 s until the heading says 'Saved locally', then reload. Press Ctrl+Z with focus in the editor, then click the 'Undo (Ctrl+Z)' ribbon button; compare document.body innerText before and after each action and read the button's disabled property.
Actual: After reload the Undo button reports disabled=false. document.body innerText length is 1452 before Ctrl+Z, 1452 after Ctrl+Z, and 1452 after clicking Undo; the marker remains in the document. No visible change occurs from either action.
items.source: explore:persistence:undo appears enabled but is a no-op after reload

items.title: A restored source-edited document is marked dirty and silently rewritten
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (functional): expected A saved document that is restored without user input stays 'Saved locally' and its stored model is not rewritten.
items.hint:
Repro: In the browser app, type text and wait for 'Saved locally'. Switch View > LaTeX, insert a plain sentence before \end{document}, wait 1.5 s for autosave, then reload. Observe the heading immediately after reload, wait another 1.5 s without editing, and re-read localStorage sentence.workspace.
Actual: Immediately after reload the heading says 'Editing' and the saved check icon disappears despite no user edit. After another 1.5 s, autosave rewrites the stored document JSON from 1302 to 1471 characters while text, node types, and marks are unchanged, and the heading returns to 'Saved locally'. Opening a fresh document shows the same pattern without input: stored document grows from 1174 to 1316 characters after 1.5 s idle.
items.source: explore:persistence:a restored source-edited document is marked dirty and silently rewritten

items.title: Settings button is not activated by Enter when focused
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected The Settings panel/dialog opens (same effect as clicking the Settings button).
items.hint:
Repro: Open the editor (browser/dev build). Tab to focus the Settings (gear) button in the top bar (aria-label "Settings"). Press Enter.
Actual: Pressing Enter while the Settings button is focused does not open the Settings UI in the observed run (no modal/dialog opened).
items.source: explore:keyboard:settings button is not activated by enter when focused

items.title: A second page-furniture command replaces the previously inserted page break or contents block
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (functional): expected Each ribbon command inserts its own block: two page breaks should yield two \newpage commands and two contents blocks should yield two \tableofcontents commands.
items.hint:
Repro: In the demo document click at the end of the last paragraph, click Insert > Page break, then immediately click References > Table of contents without clicking back into the editor. Then, from a paragraph, click References > Table of contents followed immediately by Insert > Page break. Compare the [data-page-break] and [data-toc] counts in the visual DOM and the 
ewpage / 	ableofcontents counts in View > LaTeX.
Actual: After the first break the DOM had 2 [data-page-break] and 1 [data-toc]; after the Contents click it had 1 break and 2 TOCs and the LaTeX had 
ewpage count 1 and 	ableofcontents count 2, i.e. the newly inserted break was overwritten. In the reverse order there were 1 break and 4 TOCs before the Page break click and 2 breaks and 3 TOCs after it, with 
ewpage count 2 and 	ableofcontents count 3: the last inserted TOC was overwritten. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs steps 8 and 10: out.repeated.afterSecondBreak={breaks:2,tocs:1} vs out.repeated.dom.breaks=1, out.repeated.dom.tocs=2, out.repeated.latex.newpageCount=1; out.tocThenBreak.afterTocOnly={breaks:1,tocs:4} vs out.tocThenBreak.dom.breaks=2, out.tocThenBreak.dom.tocs=3.
items.source: explore:insert-media:a second page-furniture command replaces the previously inserted page break or contents block

items.title: Inserting an image at a caret inside a paragraph splits the sentence into two paragraphs
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (functional): expected The image is inserted inline or as a separate block without cutting an existing sentence into two paragraphs.
items.hint:
Repro: At the end of a paragraph type 'SPLIT BEFORE. SPLIT AFTER.', press Home then ArrowRight 13 times so the caret sits just after the first sentence, then supply a PNG to the hidden file input (the stubbed browser picker path) via Insert > Image. Inspect View > Visual DOM and View > LaTeX. Actual: The visual DOM becomes

SPLIT BEFORE.

SPLIT AFTER.

and the exported LaTeX places a \begin{figure}...\includegraphics[width=0.8\linewidth]{assets/images/mid-paragraph.png}...\end{figure} block between 'SPLIT BEFORE.' and ' SPLIT AFTER.', turning one sentence into two paragraphs. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs step 3: out.imageMidParagraph.dom.html and out.imageMidParagraph.latex.bodyTail.
items.source: explore:insert-media:inserting an image at a caret inside a paragraph splits the sentence into two paragraphs

items.title: Select-all + list toggle does not convert a list to paragraphs; it adds an empty item
items.why:
Exploratory pass on lists (functional): expected Both items become plain paragraphs (

one

two

) and the generated LaTeX contains no list environment and no empty \item.
items.hint:
Repro: Clear the editor, type 'one', click the 'Bulleted list' ribbon button, press Enter, type 'two'. Press Ctrl+A (getSelection() is 'one two '), then click 'Bulleted list' again. Switch to Source and read the LaTeX textarea. Repeating with 'Numbered list' gives the same result. Actual: The editor stays a list and gains a third empty item:
  • one
  • two

. LaTeX is ' egin{itemize} \item one \item two \item \end{itemize}'. With Numbered list the LaTeX is ' egin{enumerate} \item x \item y \item \end{enumerate}'.
items.source: explore:lists:select-all + list toggle does not convert a list to paragraphs; it adds an empty item

items.title: Ordered list start number is dropped from LaTeX
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (content): expected The exported LaTeX should reproduce the visual list numbering starting at 3 (for example with \setcounter{enumi}{2}), so the PDF shows '3. apple'.
items.hint:
Repro: Clear the editor and type '3. apple' in a paragraph so the ordered-list input rule fires. Switch to Source and read the LaTeX textarea. Actual: The visual editor has

  1. apple

, but the LaTeX is '\begin{enumerate}\n\item apple\n\end{enumerate}', which renders the item as '1. apple'.
items.source: explore:lists:ordered list start number is dropped from latex

items.title: Table editing: a contextual table toolbar
items.why: Word users edit tables constantly. Tiptap ships table commands; the app exposes only 'insert 3x3', so a table cannot be reshaped after creation.
items.hint: When the cursor is inside a table, show a small toolbar above it (or in the ribbon) with: add row above/below, delete row, add column left/right, delete column, toggle header row, merge/split cells, cell alignment, delete table. Use the existing Tiptap table extension commands through the editor. Add a caption field that emits \caption{...} in LaTeX.
items.source: roadmap:table editing: a contextual table toolbar

items.title: Spell check that respects the LaTeX source
items.why: Every word processor has it. A manuscript editor without spell check sends people to another app to proofread.
items.hint: Use the WebView's native spellchecker on the ProseMirror surface (spellcheck attribute + lang) rather than shipping a dictionary; verify it does not underline LaTeX commands in source mode (turn spellcheck off in the .tex textarea). Add a Review-tab 'Spelling' toggle that persists in settings.
items.source: roadmap:spell check that respects the latex source

items.title: Real pagination in the visual editor
items.why: The visual page is a single long sheet and the status bar guesses page count. Without page breaks WYSIWYG means nothing for a print-first tool.
items.hint: Measure the rendered block positions against the configured page height and draw page-break rules (a repeating background or absolutely positioned separators) so the user sees where pages split; derive the page count from the same measurement instead of word count. Use the settings' paperSize/margins/fontSize to compute the content height. Keep it CSS/measurement only — no full layout engine.
items.source: roadmap:real pagination in the visual editor

items.title: Unknown LaTeX commands pass math validation and can be inserted
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (functional): expected Input that KaTeX itself renders as a red error should be flagged as invalid, so Insert/Update is disabled as it is for malformed input like `\frac{`, preventing uncompilable LaTeX entering the document.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a new project and click the Insert tab.
2. Click 'Inline equation', type `\badcommand{x}` in the LaTeX source textarea.
3. Observe the preview: the command is rendered in red via `mstyle mathcolor="#cc0000"`, but the dialog reports no error (no `katex-error`, no `math-preview-invalid`) and the Insert button is enabled.
4. Click Insert.
5. Switch to View > LaTeX and read document.tex: it contains `\(\badcommand{x}\)`. The same happens with `\unknown{}`.
Actual: `\badcommand{x}` and `\unknown{}` leave the Insert button enabled and are inserted into the document and exported to LaTeX. By contrast `\frac{`, `x^{`, `\begin{` and `}{` correctly show `.math-preview-invalid` and disable Insert.
items.source: explore:math:unknown latex commands pass math validation and can be inserted

items.title: Dismissing a math edit dialog with Cancel/Escape drops editor focus; typing and Backspace are swallowed
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (ux): expected After the edit dialog closes, keyboard focus should return to the editor so the user can keep typing or delete the clicked math node with Backspace/Delete.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a new project, use Insert > Inline equation to insert `x+1`.
2. Click the inserted math node (the 'Edit inline equation' dialog opens).
3. Press Escape or click Cancel.
4. Check `document.activeElement`: it is `BODY`, not the editor.
5. Press Backspace, or type `YY`, then switch to View > LaTeX and read document.tex.
Actual: Focus stays on BODY: Backspace leaves the math node in place (`\(y=2\)` still in the source) and typed text (`YY`) never reaches the document. The same occurs for a display 'Equation block' after clicking it and pressing Escape then Delete. Typing works again only after clicking the editor first; clicking earlier and deleting via a positioned caret does work, so there is no direct delete affordance after dialog dismissal.
items.source: explore:math:dismissing a math edit dialog with cancel/escape drops editor focus; typing and backspace are swallowed

items.title: Bibliography manager
items.why: Citations exist but the .bib file can only be edited by hand. Word's citation manager is a core reason people stay.
items.hint: A References-tab panel listing entries parsed from references.bib (key, author, year, title) with search, add, edit and delete; inserting a citation opens this list. Keep the .bib text the source of truth and parse/write it in src/lib (add round-trip tests next to latex.test.ts).
items.source: roadmap:bibliography manager

items.title: Track changes UI
items.why: Revision data exists in the model but a reviewer cannot see, accept or reject individual changes.
items.hint: Show insertions and deletions inline in the visual editor (marks with author colours), a Review-tab toggle for tracking, and per-change accept/reject plus accept-all/reject-all in the History panel. Review state must never leak into the exported LaTeX.
items.source: roadmap:track changes ui

items.title: Footnote text containing a closing brace is corrupted on LaTeX source round-trip
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (functional): expected The footnote's text/title stays `Note with } and &`, the paragraph stays `Brace note 1`, and re-exported LaTeX stays `\footnote{Note with \} and \&}`. A control round-trip with `Cost & 50%` already behaves this way.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. Type `Brace note `, choose Insert > Footnote, enter `Note with } and &`, and click Insert. View > Source shows `\footnote{Note with \} and \&}`. Click Apply source, then switch back to Visual and to Source again.
Actual: After Apply source the footnote's text/title is `Note with \`, the literal text ` and &}` appears in the paragraph after the marker, and the exported source is `\footnote{Note with \textbackslash{}} and \&\}`; part of the footnote moved into body text.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:footnote text containing a closing brace is corrupted on latex source round-trip

items.title: Document themes and style gallery
items.why: Word's style gallery is how normal people get a consistent document without knowing LaTeX.
items.hint: A small gallery of named themes (e.g. Classic, Modern, Compact) that set documentClass/fontFamily/fontSize/lineSpacing/paragraphSpacing/margins at once, previewed as a styled thumbnail. Apply through the existing settings object so the LaTeX preamble follows.
items.source: roadmap:document themes and style gallery

items.title: Multi-document workspace tabs
items.why: One document per window forces people to juggle windows for a paper plus its notes.
items.hint: Tabs above the page area holding multiple open projects, with dirty indicators and per-tab close. Keep one editor instance and swap the workspace snapshot to avoid memory blowup. Desktop only for real projects; browser mode keeps the single demo workspace.
items.source: roadmap:multi-document workspace tabs

items.title: Export to HTML and Markdown alongside LaTeX
items.why: People need to publish the same text as a blog post or a web page, and currently the only portable output is .tex.
items.hint: Add exporters next to documentToLatex in src/lib, driven by the same document model, with round-trip tests for the supported subset. Wire them into a File/Export menu that is honest about which subset is supported.
items.source: roadmap:export to html and markdown alongside latex

items.title: source view toggle did not reveal an editable LaTeX surface
items.why: Found by the automated pass (medium/functional).
items.source: source view toggle did not reveal an editable latex surface

items.title: no View ribbon tab found, cannot check source-view round trips
items.why: Found by the automated pass (medium/ux).
items.source: no view ribbon tab found, cannot check source-view round trips

items.why: The automated gate is red; nothing else can be trusted until it is green.

items.source: smoke-fail:harness

items.title: Rejecting a tracked edit made after a comment removes the comment highlight and leaves the thread unanchored
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected Rejecting the tracked edit should undo only ' tail'; the 'Comment' highlight should remain and the comment thread should still point at that word.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. In a fresh document type 'Comment on tracked text'. 2. Review tab > Track changes (the button changes to 'Tracking on'). 3. Select the first word 'Comment', Review tab > New comment, enter 'Comment before tracked edit' and click Comment. 4. Put the caret at the end and type ' tail', wait ~2 s for the tracked change to appear, open the History sidebar and click Reject on the pending revision. 5. Open the Review sidebar.
Actual: The editor text returned to 'Comment on tracked text', but zero [data-comment-id] highlight spans remained. The Review panel still listed 'Comment before tracked edit' with badge 1, so the thread survived with no anchor; clicking it cannot locate or highlight any text.
items.source: explore:review:rejecting a tracked edit made after a comment removes the comment highlight and leaves the thread unanchored

items.title: Adding a comment to a selection that overlaps an existing comment silently removes the first comment's highlight
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected Each comment keeps its own anchored highlight (two highlights), or the app refuses the overlapping comment and explains why.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. In a fresh document type 'Alpha beta gamma delta'. 2. Select 'Alpha' (Ctrl+Home, then Ctrl+Shift+Right) and add the comment 'First comment body'. 3. Select 'Alpha beta' (Ctrl+Home, then Ctrl+Shift+Right twice) and add the comment 'Second overlapping comment'. 4. Inspect the editor spans and the Review sidebar, then click the 'First comment body' thread.
Actual: The Review sidebar shows two threads (badge 2) but the editor has a single highlight, 'Alpha beta', carrying the second comment's mark id. The first comment's mark id is absent from the document. Clicking the first thread marks it active in the sidebar but no part of the document highlights (0 active highlight elements), so that thread can no longer locate its text.
items.source: explore:review:adding a comment to a selection that overlaps an existing comment silently removes the first comment's highlight

items.title: Applying an edited LaTeX source drops every comment highlight and leaves comment threads unanchored
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected Comment highlights stay attached to their text across the source round trip, or the app warns that applying source will detach the comments.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Type 'Source sync target text'. 2. Select the last word 'text' and add the comment 'Comment through source sync'; confirm the Review sidebar shows one highlight. 3. View tab > LaTeX, change the body text to 'Source sync target text rewritten in source', click Apply source, then click Visual and open the Review sidebar.
Actual: The thread body 'Comment through source sync' is still listed with badge 1, but no [data-comment-id] highlight remains in the document, so the comment is unanchored. The only feedback was 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.'
items.source: explore:review:applying an edited latex source drops every comment highlight and leaves comment threads unanchored

items.title: Tracked-change decorations misreport existing text as deleted and re-inserted when the paragraph contains a comment mark
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (visual): expected The inline tracked-change decoration marks only the newly typed ' tail' as inserted, matching the revision card's before 'Comment on tracked text' / after 'Comment on tracked text tail'.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Type 'Comment on tracked text'. 2. Turn on Review > Track changes. 3. Select the first word 'Comment' and add the comment 'Comment before tracked edit'. 4. Put the caret at the end and type ' tail', wait ~2 s, and open the History sidebar while the revision is pending.
Actual: The editor renders an insertion decoration with text ' on tracked text tail' and a deletion decoration with text ' on tracked text', so most of the unchanged sentence is shown as both deleted and inserted. The revision card text is correct; only the inline decorations are wrong.
items.source: explore:review:tracked-change decorations misreport existing text as deleted and re-inserted when the paragraph contains a comment mark

items.title: New comment with no selection accepts a comment body and then discards it
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (ux): expected New comment is unavailable until text is selected, or the dialog stays open with the typed body and an inline error so the text is not lost.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. In an empty document (no text selected), open Review > New comment. 2. Type 'Comment without a selection' in the dialog and click Comment.
Actual: The dialog closes, a transient toast reads 'Select text before adding a comment.', no thread is created, and the typed comment body is discarded.
items.source: explore:review:new comment with no selection accepts a comment body and then discards it

items.title: Leaving the LaTeX view after a failed Apply silently discards the broken source draft
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (functional): expected The hand-written source, including the draft that failed validation, stays available so the user can fix the missing \end{itemize}; alternatively the app warns before discarding it.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project, click View > LaTeX, put the caret at the end of the document body just before \end{document}, and type a line `ZXBROKEN paragraph` followed by a newline and `\begin{itemize}` with no closing `\end{itemize}`. 2. Click 'Apply source': the toast reads `Invalid LaTeX: unbalanced environment "itemize".` and the visual document is correctly left unchanged. 3. Click View > Visual (the app switches to the visual document and repeats the error toast). 4. Click View > LaTeX and read the textarea.
Actual: The textarea is regenerated from the visual document and the typed lines are gone (source length returns from the edited value to the original 2794 characters, 'Apply source' is disabled). The probe reproduced this both through Apply source and by clicking Visual directly from the broken source (brokenTextStillInSourceAfterReturn=false in both cases). The visual document is preserved, but the unapplied source draft is lost with no confirmation.
items.source: explore:source-editor:leaving the latex view after a failed apply silently discards the broken source draft

items.title: Headings and tables placed directly after text are escaped into literal text instead of being recognized
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (content): expected The section command immediately after paragraph text is valid LaTeX and should become a heading, and the following table should become a table.
items.source: explore:source-editor:headings and tables placed directly after text are escaped into literal text instead of being recognized

items.title: Missing closing braces are accepted as valid LaTeX and the malformed text is rewritten on export
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (content): expected The parser should report the missing closing brace the way it reports an unbalanced environment, rather than applying the document.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project, switch to View > LaTeX, and before \end{document} add:
\begin{tabular}{ll
ZXCOLCELL & 7 \\
\end{tabular}
(notice the missing closing brace after `ll`). 2. Click 'Apply source' and read the toast. 3. Click View > Visual and inspect the table. 4. Switch back to View > LaTeX and read the table block.
Actual: No error is shown: the toast says `Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.` and the visual document contains a one-row table whose first cell is the literal text `{ll`. Re-exporting rewrites the block as a valid table with the cell `\{ll`, changing the user's content. The same class of failure occurs with `\section{ZXSEC UNCLOSED` (no closing brace): Apply reports success, the raw command appears as body text, and it is re-exported as `\textbackslash{}section\{ZXSEC UNCLOSED`.
items.source: explore:source-editor:missing closing braces are accepted as valid latex and the malformed text is rewritten on export

items.title: Stale 'Retry save' error remains after the failed source draft has been discarded
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (ux): expected Once the broken draft is discarded and the source matches the saved visual document, the save-error indicator should clear.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project, switch to View > LaTeX, add `ZXFAIL persistent paragraph` plus an unclosed `\begin{itemize}` before \end{document}. 2. Click 'Apply source' (error toast appears). 3. Wait about 1.5 seconds so autosave attempts the same parse; a 'Retry save' button appears in the status bar. 4. Click View > Visual, then View > LaTeX. The broken draft is gone and the source has been regenerated from the visual document ('Apply source' is disabled). Look at the status bar.
Actual: The status bar still shows the 'Retry save' button after returning to the regenerated, clean source (saveErrorAfterReturn='Retry save' while 'Apply source' is disabled), suggesting unsaved or invalid work remains when there is none.
items.source: explore:source-editor:stale 'retry save' error remains after the failed source draft has been discarded

items.title: Split view silently discards visual-pane edits when the source pane has an unapplied draft
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (functional): expected The app keeps the visual edit or warns that it is about to be replaced by the older, unapplied source draft.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and make sure the source is clean (View > LaTeX, then 'Apply source' is disabled). 2. Click View > Split. 3. In the source pane, put the caret before \end{document} and type `ZXDRAFTPARAGRAPH unapplied` on its own line. Do not click Apply. 4. Click at the end of the visual text in the other pane and type `ZXVISUALTYPED`; the text appears at the end of the last paragraph. 5. Click View > Visual.
Actual: The mode switches with the success toast `Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.` and the freshly typed visual text is gone: the visual document shows `ZXDRAFTPARAGRAPH unapplied` and no longer contains `ZXVISUALTYPED` (probe: visualAcceptedTyping=true, visualStillHasTypedText=false, visualHasSourceDraft=true). The source pane keeps the draft and 'Apply source' remains enabled, so the same overwrite happens with no warning and no way to recover the visual typing.
items.source: explore:source-editor:split view silently discards visual-pane edits when the source pane has an unapplied draft

items.title: Clicking Apply source drops keyboard focus, so subsequent typing and redo are silently ignored
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (ux): expected Focus and the caret stay in the source textarea, so continued typing edits the source and redo works.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. View > LaTeX and click into the textarea before \end{document}. 2. Type `ZXFOCUS` and click 'Apply source'. 3. Without clicking back into the textarea, type `ZXLOST`. 4. Press Ctrl+Z, then Ctrl+Shift+Z. 5. Click back into the textarea and press Ctrl+Shift+Z again.
Actual: After Apply, document.activeElement is BODY (the Apply button is disabled and blurred) and `ZXLOST` never reaches the source (typingAfterApplyReachedEditor=false). Ctrl+Z does undo `ZXFOCUS`, but Ctrl+Shift+Z does nothing (redoAfterApplyWorked=false) until the user clicks into the textarea, after which redo restores `ZXFOCUS` and typing works again. The same happens after a failed Apply, where the enabled button keeps focus (activeElement=BUTTON): typing is lost and Ctrl+Shift+Z does not redo the draft (redoRestoredDraft=false).
items.source: explore:source-editor:clicking apply source drops keyboard focus, so subsequent typing and redo are silently ignored

items.title: LaTeX comments in the document body become visible text and are escaped on export
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (content): expected Text after an unescaped `%` is a LaTeX comment: it should be ignored by the document (or at least preserved as a comment), not turned into body text.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. View > LaTeX and before \end{document} add two lines: `ZXCOMMENTBLOCK text body` followed by `% ZXCOMMENTBLOCK ignored by LaTeX`, then a blank line and `ZXCOMMENTINLINE text % ZXCOMMENTINLINE note`. 2. Click 'Apply source'. 3. Click View > Visual. 4. Click View > LaTeX and read the textarea.
Actual: Apply reports success and the visual document shows the literal text `% ZXCOMMENTBLOCK ignored by LaTeX` and `% ZXCOMMENTINLINE note`. Returning to the source shows both comments rewritten with escaped percent signs (`\% ZXCOMMENTBLOCK ignored by LaTeX`, `\% ZXCOMMENTINLINE note`), so the comments are permanently converted into visible document content. Reproduced for both a whole-line comment and a trailing comment.
items.source: explore:source-editor:latex comments in the document body become visible text and are escaped on export

items.title: Unclosed math delimiters are accepted as valid and escaped instead of reported
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (functional): expected Like an unbalanced environment or brace, the unclosed math delimiter should be reported as invalid and the draft left unapplied.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. View > LaTeX and before \end{document} add a line `ZXUNCLOSEDPAREN \(a^2 + b^2` (no closing `\)`). 2. Click 'Apply source' and read the toast. 3. Click View > Visual, then View > LaTeX. 4. Repeat with `ZXUNCLOSEDDOLLAR $a^2 + b^2` (no closing `$`).
Actual: Both applies report success (`Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.`) and 'Apply source' becomes disabled, so the broken input is committed. The visual document contains the delimiter as literal text, and the regenerated source escapes it: `\textbackslash{}(a\textasciicircum{}2 + b\textasciicircum{}2` for the unclosed `\(` and `\$a\textasciicircum{}2 + b\textasciicircum{}2` for the unclosed `$`. No error is shown at any point.
items.source: explore:source-editor:unclosed math delimiters are accepted as valid and escaped instead of reported

items.title: Undo history is discarded after leaving and re-entering the LaTeX view
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (ux): expected Ctrl+Z undoes the last source edit (`ZXVISIT`), since the user has not done anything else in between.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. View > LaTeX and put the caret before \end{document}. 2. Type `ZXVISIT`. 3. Click View > Visual, then View > LaTeX. 4. Press Ctrl+Z.
Actual: Ctrl+Z does nothing: the reminder of the edit stays in the source (`ZXVISIT` is still present), 'Apply source' is disabled, and there is no indication that undo history was dropped. The source editor is remounted on every view switch with a fresh history, so the normal source > visual > source check loses undo for the whole visit.
items.source: explore:source-editor:undo history is discarded after leaving and re-entering the latex view

items.title: Page divider lines are painted through text lines and headings
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (visual): expected A page boundary should fall in a page margin/gap, so no body line or heading is bisected by the divider; a heading should not sit on a page boundary.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the app, create a new document, Ctrl+A and Backspace to empty it, then paste (Ctrl+V) 30 blank-line-separated paragraphs of ~95 words each (the probe uses 'PASTEP1'..'PASTEP30' plus a repeated 30-word sentence). The status bar shows 2,670 words / 5 pages. Scroll to any of the four horizontal page rules the sheet paints every 1,123 px: each one crosses the middle of a text line (first rule at 3,518 px crosses the line box 3,514-3,530 px of the 'PASTEP5' paragraph). Repeat with a 50-heading / 6,050-word document: 8 of 14 rules cross a text line and, with page breaks inserted, a rule crosses the heading 'Section 14 TOKENH14' (line box 3,747-3,770 px, rule at 3,758 px). Screenshot: qa/shots/probe-long-page-boundary.png.
Actual: The paper sheet is one continuous text flow and the page rules are painted over it every paper height. On the 5-page paste all 4 rules cross a line of text (4/4); on the 15-page document 8/14 rules cross text and the rule at 3,758 px runs through the middle of the heading 'Section 14 TOKENH14', which reads as a strikethrough.
items.source: explore:long-document:page divider lines are painted through text lines and headings

items.title: Outline entry drops inline math from a heading
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (content): expected The Outline entry mirrors the visible heading text, including the formula (e.g. 'Energy model E=mc^2').
items.hint:
Repro: New document. Type 'Energy model', set Paragraph style to 'Heading 1', press End, then Insert tab > Inline equation, enter E=mc^2 and click Insert. Compare the rendered heading with the Outline panel entry.
Actual: The heading renders 'Energy model E=mc²' but the Outline entry is only 'Energy model ' (13 characters, formula omitted), so headings whose titles differ by their formulas look identical in the outline.
items.source: explore:long-document:outline entry drops inline math from a heading

items.title: Visual edits are never saved while an invalid LaTeX draft is left in the hidden source pane, and are lost on reload
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (functional): expected Visual edits continue to autosave, or the app blocks/surfaces the pending invalid source draft instead of silently accepting visual typing that can never be stored. Reloading must not drop text the editor displayed as part of the document without warning.
items.hint:
Repro: 1) Open the browser app, click New document, wait 1.5 s until the heading says 'Saved locally'. 2) Click 'Source' in the status bar. 3) In the LaTeX textarea delete the final \end{document} line. 4) Wait 1.5 s: the heading reads 'Editing', a toast says 'Invalid LaTeX: missing \end{document}.', and a 'Retry save' button appears. 5) Click 'Visual' in the status bar; the source textarea disappears (0 visible). 6) Put the caret at the end of the document and type ' persist-lost-X'. 7) Wait 1.5 s and read localStorage['sentence.workspace']: the typed text is absent, the heading still reads 'Editing', and 'Retry save' stays visible. 8) Reload the page: 'persist-lost-X' is gone from both the editor and localStorage, the document is the last version saved before the invalid draft, and the heading now reads 'Saved locally'.
Actual: The invalid draft is kept in memory but hidden when the user switches to Visual. Every autosave attempt re-parses that hidden draft, fails with 'Invalid LaTeX: missing \end{document}.' and writes nothing, so the visual text typed afterwards is never persisted. After 1.5 s the marker is in the editor but not in localStorage; after reload it is in neither, while the top bar reports 'Saved locally' for the restored older document. The only cue is the transient error toast and the 'Retry save' button, which retries the same failing parse.
items.source: explore:persistence:visual edits are never saved while an invalid latex draft is left in the hidden source pane, and are lost on reload

items.title: Tab is trapped in the document editor and each press nests the paragraph in another blockquote
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (functional): expected Tab moves keyboard focus to the next focusable control (or there is a documented escape from the editing surface), and a focus-navigation key does not modify the document.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the editor, click into a paragraph, then press Tab three times. Then try Shift+Tab three times and Escape while the editor is focused.
Actual: Focus stays on the .sentence-editor contenteditable after every key. A clean run went from 1 to 4 blockquotes over three Tab presses (each press wraps the paragraph in another blockquote); the 40-stop Tab walk reached the editor at stop 35 and stops 36-40 were all the editor, never the status bar or any later control. Shift+Tab left focus in the editor for all three presses, and Escape also left focus in the editor.
items.source: explore:keyboard:tab is trapped in the document editor and each press nests the paragraph in another blockquote

items.title: Ctrl+F opens the find bar behind an open modal and moves focus out of the dialog
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (functional): expected While a modal dialog is open, focus stays inside the dialog and global shortcuts for background UI do not run.
items.hint:
Repro: Focus the editor, press Ctrl+K to open the Add link dialog, then with the dialog still open press Ctrl+F (and separately Ctrl+Enter).
Actual: Ctrl+F opens .find-bar (computed z-index 12) behind the modal backdrop (z-index 100), moves focus to the Find input outside the dialog, and leaves the Add link dialog open. In the same state Ctrl+Enter fires compilation and shows the 'Compilation is available in the desktop application.' toast while the dialog is still open.
items.source: explore:keyboard:ctrl+f opens the find bar behind an open modal and moves focus out of the dialog

items.title: arXiv dialog opens with focus still on the ribbon button and loses focus to <body> when closed
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected Focus moves into the dialog when it opens and returns to the 'Create arXiv ZIP' button when it closes.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the editor, select the Paper ribbon tab, Tab to the 'Create arXiv ZIP' button, press Enter, then press Tab once and Escape.
Actual: On open, document.activeElement is the 'Create arXiv ZIP' ribbon button behind the aria-modal dialog (not inside it); the first Tab moves focus to the dialog's Close button. Escape closes the dialog but leaves document.activeElement on <body>, so the next Tab restarts at the top of the page instead of the invoking button.
items.source: explore:keyboard:arxiv dialog opens with focus still on the ribbon button and loses focus to <body> when closed

items.title: Escape does not close the Text color popover
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (functional): expected Escape dismisses the open popover.
items.hint:
Repro: On the Home ribbon tab, Tab to the 'Text color' button, press Enter to open the swatch popover, then press Escape.
Actual: The .color-popover is still open after Escape and focus remains on the 'Text color' trigger; nothing else closes it except toggling the trigger or clicking the backdrop.
items.source: explore:keyboard:escape does not close the text color popover

items.title: Page furniture and block images inserted in a table cell disappear from the exported LaTeX
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (functional): expected Either the commands are disabled inside table cells, or the inserted contents/page-break/figure are exported inside the cell (\tableofcontents, \newpage, \includegraphics).
items.hint:
Repro: In the demo document click Insert > Insert table. Click an empty body cell and click References > Table of contents. Click a second empty body cell and click Insert > Page break. Click a third empty body cell, click Insert > Image and supply any PNG through the hidden file input. Compare the visual page with View > LaTeX.
Actual: The cells visibly contain nav[data-toc], div[data-page-break] and img (probe cell counts toc=1, breaks=1, images=1), but the exported document body has \tableofcontents count 0, \newpage count 0 and \includegraphics count 0, and the tabular rows contain only empty cells. Nothing warns that the content will be missing from the PDF. The page break also stretches its cell to 752px tall in the visual page. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario blockMediaInTableCell.
items.source: explore:insert-media:page furniture and block images inserted in a table cell disappear from the exported latex

items.title: Typing after inserting an image, page break or table of contents replaces the just-inserted block
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (functional): expected The inserted page break/figure/contents block stays in the document and typing continues after it; a second media command adds a second item instead of replacing the first.
items.hint:
Repro: Type 'Alpha.' at the end of a paragraph. Click Insert > Page break, then type 'Bravo.' without clicking back into the page. Repeat with Insert > Image (supply a PNG through the hidden file input) then typing, and with References > Table of contents then typing. Also click Insert > Page break followed immediately by Insert > Image, and Insert > Image followed immediately by Insert > Page break.
Actual: The inserted atom keeps a ProseMirror node selection (probe selectedAtoms=1). Typing one character replaces it: the page break count goes 1 -> 0, \newpage 1 -> 0 and the page count 2 -> 1; the image count goes 1 -> 0 and \includegraphics 1 -> 0; the contents block count goes 1 -> 0 and \tableofcontents 1 -> 0. Inserting an image after a page break leaves only the image (\newpage 0), and inserting a page break after an image leaves only the break (\includegraphics 0). Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario insertThenTypeOrInsert.
items.source: explore:insert-media:typing after inserting an image, page break or table of contents replaces the just-inserted block

items.title: Applying the LaTeX source turns an inserted image into a broken image
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (visual): expected The image keeps rendering after the visual document is synchronised from LaTeX, or the app reports that the asset cannot be loaded.
items.hint:
Repro: Type 'Caption target paragraph.', click Insert > Image and supply a PNG through the hidden file input. Switch to View > LaTeX, press Ctrl+End, type a space and press Backspace so Apply source becomes enabled, click Apply source, then View > Visual.
Actual: Before Apply the img has a data: src and naturalWidth/Height 1x1. After Apply its src is the relative path 'assets/images/qa-image--1.png' with naturalWidth/Height 0x0, so the page shows the browser's broken-image box with the alt text, while the toast says 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.' No warning is shown. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario blockImageSourceRoundTrip (screenshot qa/shots/probe-insert-media-image-after-apply.png).
items.source: explore:insert-media:applying the latex source turns an inserted image into a broken image

items.title: Exported figure captions use the file name and are invisible in the visual editor
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (content): expected The caption that will appear in the PDF is shown under the figure in the visual editor (and is editable), or no caption is generated at all.
items.hint:
Repro: Type a paragraph, click Insert > Image and supply a file named 'qa image #1.png' through the hidden file input. Read the visual page, then switch to View > LaTeX.
Actual: The visual page renders only img (no caption element or caption text). The exported LaTeX adds \caption{qa image \#1.png}, so the PDF will show the raw file name as a caption that the user never saw or edited. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario blockImageSourceRoundTrip.
items.source: explore:insert-media:exported figure captions use the file name and are invisible in the visual editor

items.title: Tab on the first item of a list moves focus out of the editor instead of nesting
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (functional): expected Tab nests the current item one level (the same way it works for a second or later item), or at minimum keeps keyboard focus in the editor.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new document. With the empty paragraph active, click Home > Bulleted list, then press Tab. Repeat with 'only item' typed into the list first, with the caret in the first of two list items, and with the caret in the only item of a nested list. In every case inspect document.activeElement after Tab.
Actual: The item stays at its current level and focus leaves the editor: document.activeElement becomes the 'Visual (Ctrl+Alt+1)' button in the status bar. Typing after that inserts nothing into the document. This happens for the first item of a list, the first of two items, the only item of a nested sublist, and an empty list. Only items that have a previous sibling at the same level can be nested with Tab.
items.source: explore:lists:tab on the first item of a list moves focus out of the editor instead of nesting

items.title: A list followed by paragraph text without a blank line is imported as escaped literal text
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (content): expected The visual document shows a two-item bulleted list followed by a normal paragraph 'Following paragraph', and the regenerated LaTeX keeps an itemize environment plus the paragraph.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new document and click Source in the status bar. Replace the body between \begin{document} and \end{document} with exactly: '\begin{itemize}' newline '\item a' newline '\item b' newline '\end{itemize}' newline 'Following paragraph' (no blank line after \end{itemize}). Click Apply source, click Visual, then reopen Source and click Refresh from visual.
Actual: Apply reports 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.' but the visual document is one plain paragraph containing the literal text '\begin{itemize}', '\item a', '\item b', '\end{itemize}' and 'Following paragraph'. The regenerated LaTeX escapes it as '\textbackslash{}begin\{itemize\}', '\textbackslash{}item a', '\textbackslash{}item b' and '\textbackslash{}end\{itemize\}' followed by the text, so the list is permanently corrupted. The same happens with an enumerate and when two itemize environments are separated by text with no blank lines. Adding a blank line after \end{itemize} makes the same source import correctly.
items.source: explore:lists:a list followed by paragraph text without a blank line is imported as escaped literal text

items.title: Ctrl+A then the list button does not convert a list to paragraphs; it appends an empty item
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (functional): expected Both items become ordinary paragraphs and the LaTeX contains no list environment and no empty \item.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new document, type 'one', click Home > Bulleted list, press Enter, type 'two'. Press Ctrl+A (the editor selection covers both items), then click Home > Bulleted list again and read the LaTeX source. Repeat with Numbered list and with Ctrl+Shift+8. Actual: The document stays a list and gains a third empty item: the editor DOM is '
  • one
  • two

' and the LaTeX is ' egin{itemize} \item one \item two \item \end{itemize}'. The Numbered list case produces an extra '\item ' in an enumerate, and Ctrl+Shift+8 behaves the same. While the whole list is selected the Bulleted/Numbered list button reports aria-pressed=false. Selecting only the two list items and toggling does convert them to paragraphs.
items.source: explore:lists:ctrl+a then the list button does not convert a list to paragraphs; it appends an empty item

items.title: keyboard shortcut "Tab indent" has no visible effect on the document
items.why: Found by the automated pass (low/ux).
items.hint: innerHTML unchanged
items.source: keyboard shortcut "tab indent" has no visible effect on the document

items.title: Inserting a table inside a table silently flattens the nested table's cells into the parent cell
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (functional): expected Either the nested table keeps its own rows and columns in the exported tabular (so n1, n2 and n3 stay in separate cells), or Insert table is disabled while the caret is inside an existing table.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new project. Insert tab > Insert table (3x3 with header row). Click the middle cell (row 2, column 2) and type 'outer'. Click Insert tab > Insert table again. In the nested table click its first cell, type 'n1', press Tab, type 'n2', press Tab, type 'n3'. Switch to View > LaTeX and read the table block, then click Apply source and switch back to View > Visual.
Actual: The visual editor holds 2 tables (a 3x3 outer table plus a 3x3 nested table, 6 rows in the DOM), but the exported tabular has only the outer 3 rows and one cell reading 'outer\par n1n2n3' — the nested table's rows/cells are flattened with no separators. Applying that source back removes the nested table entirely and leaves the concatenated text inside the parent cell. The Insert table button stays enabled inside a cell.
items.source: explore:tables:inserting a table inside a table silently flattens the nested table's cells into the parent cell

items.title: Turning the header row off is not exported and is silently re-enabled by a source round trip
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (content): expected A table whose header row was turned off stays header-less after the LaTeX round trip, or the header-row state is represented in the exported tabular so it can be restored.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new project. Insert tab > Insert table (3x3 with header row). Type 'Head' in the top-left cell, click a body cell, then click 'Header row' in the Table toolbar so the first row changes from TH to TD. Switch to View > LaTeX and read the table block. Click Apply source, then View > Visual and inspect the first row.
Actual: The exported LaTeX is identical to the header-row-on export (only \hline above and below the body; no bold text and no header rule), so the header state has no representation. After Apply source the first row is rebuilt as TH and the Table toolbar's Header row button reports pressed: the header the user disabled has come back.
items.source: explore:tables:turning the header row off is not exported and is silently re-enabled by a source round trip

items.title: Add row above the header row moves the header into row 2 and the toolbar then reports no header row
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (functional): expected A new row is added above the table and the header row stays the top row (or the new row is itself a header row).
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new project. Insert tab > Insert table (3x3 with header row). Click a cell in the first (header) row, then click 'Add row above' in the Table toolbar. Inspect the first two rows, then switch to View > LaTeX, click Apply source and return to View > Visual.
Actual: A TD row is inserted above the header row, so the table's TH cells end up in row 2 while row 1 is plain TD. The Table toolbar's 'Header row' button now reports unpressed (aria-pressed=false) even though row 2 is still a header row. After Apply source the header is back in row 1, so the same document looks different before and after the round trip.
items.source: explore:tables:add row above the header row moves the header into row 2 and the toolbar then reports no header row

items.title: Delete row and Delete column stay enabled at one row/column and silently do nothing
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (ux): expected Delete column is disabled when the table has a single column and Delete row is disabled when it has a single row.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new project. Insert tab > Insert table. Click a body cell. In the Table toolbar click 'Delete column' twice to reach one column, then click it again. Then click 'Delete row' twice to reach one row, then click it again.
Actual: Both buttons remain enabled (not disabled) at the minimum. Clicking Delete column with one column left leaves the table at 3x1 and clicking Delete row with one row left leaves it at 1x1; the exported LaTeX stays a one-column, one-row tabular. The controls give no feedback that nothing happened.
items.source: explore:tables:delete row and delete column stay enabled at one row/column and silently do nothing

items.title: Footnote text cannot be edited in the visual editor; typing over the marker deletes the note
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (functional): expected Double-clicking a footnote marker opens an editor for its text (or makes the marker editable) so the note can be corrected without being removed.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. At the end of the last paragraph press Enter, type `Footnotes `, then Insert > Footnote, enter `First note` and Insert, then repeat with `Second note`. Double-click the `2` marker on the page, then type `Z`.
Actual: Double-clicking only selects the atom: no dialog and no inline input appear, and the marker is `contenteditable=false`. items.title: Turning tracking off within the revision debounce silently discards the edit that was made while tracking was on
