items.title: A section with a label on the same line gets its heading corrupted and loses the label
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (content): expected The visual document shows a level-1 heading `ZXLABEL SECTION`, and the re-exported source keeps `\label{sec:zxlabel}` attached to the section so \ref can resolve it.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and open the editor. 2. View tab > LaTeX. 3. Before \end{document}, add the line `\section{ZXLABEL SECTION}\label{sec:zxlabel}`, then a blank line and `ZXLABEL BODY`. 4. Click Apply source. 5. View tab > Visual. 6. View tab > LaTeX, click Refresh from visual, and read the section line.
Actual: Apply reports `Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.` but the visual heading is read as `ZXLABEL SECTION}\label{sec:zxlabel` (probe heading: `H1:ZXLABEL SECTION}\label{sec:zxlabel`). After Refresh from visual the line is `\section{ZXLABEL SECTION\}\textbackslash{}label\{sec:zxlabel}`: the label is gone and its backslash/braces are escaped into the heading text, so the section is no longer referenceable.

items.title: Display math written with \[...\], $$...$$ or a one-line equation environment is imported as literal text and escaped
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (functional): expected Each form is a valid display equation, so it should become an editable display-math node (as the multi-line equation environment already does) and re-export as display math.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. View tab > LaTeX. 2. Before \end{document}, add the standalone line `\[ ZXBRACKET E = mc^2 \]`. 3. Click Apply source, then View tab > Visual. 4. Repeat steps 2-3 with `$$ ZXDOLLAR E = mc^2 $$` and with `\begin{equation}ZXONELINE E = mc^2\end{equation}` all on one line.
Actual: All three applies report `Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.` and the visual pane shows the delimiters as ordinary paragraph text with zero math blocks (probe mathBlocks: []). Refresh from visual then writes `\textbackslash{}[ ZXBRACKET E = mc\textasciicircum{}2 \textbackslash{}]`, `\$\$ ZXDOLLAR E = mc\textasciicircum{}2 \$\$`, and `\textbackslash{}begin\{equation\}ZXONELINE E = mc\textasciicircum{}2\textbackslash{}end\{equation\}`. The equations survive only as escaped text, not as math.

items.title: Table rows ending with \\[4pt] make the entire table fall back to escaped literal text
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (content): expected An editable two-row table; the optional `[4pt]` only controls vertical row spacing.

Repro: 1. View tab > LaTeX. 2. Before \end{document}, add a table whose rows are `Name & Value \\[4pt]` and `ZXSPACED & 77 \\[4pt]` (valid LaTeX row spacing) inside a tabular{ll}. 3. Click Apply source, then View tab > Visual.

items.title: A heading at a page boundary is pushed to the bottom of a nearly blank page
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (visual): expected A heading that cannot fit at the bottom of a page starts at the top margin of the next page, and the previous page's body text ends near its normal bottom margin; a page is not left almost entirely blank.
items.hint:
Repro: New document, Ctrl+A then Backspace to empty it. Paste 50 sections: for N=1..50 a line 'Heading N HDOCN', a blank line, then one ~65-word paragraph ending 'BODYN' (the exact text is generated by qa/probes/long-document.mjs, 3,600 words, 100 paragraphs). Select each heading paragraph and choose 'Heading 1' in the Paragraph style dropdown (every 7th heading choose 'Heading 2'). After the last change the status bar reads 3,600 words / 12 pages; scroll to page 4 (the fourth horizontal rule from the top) and then page 11. Heading 16 (page 4) and Heading 50 (page 11) have padding-top:980px while the other 48 headings have 0. Heading 16's text sits 981px into the 1,123px page, 1,022px below the previous paragraph's last line, so page 4 is empty except for that heading near its bottom; Heading 50 is identical on page 11 (text at 981px, gap 1,022px). Screenshot: qa/shots/probe-long-padded-heading.png.
Actual: Headings 16 and 50 each carry 980px of padding-top and render 981px down a page, leaving a 1,022px blank gap above them (page 4 and page 11 are blank apart from a heading near the bottom). The gap is padding inside the heading block, not a normal page break, and the padded block box is 1,007px tall against the page's 931px content height.

items.title: Outline click on a page-snapped heading scrolls to blank space instead of the heading

Repro: Build the same 3,600-word / 50-heading document (Headings 16 and 50 end up with padding-top:980px). In the Outline panel click 'Heading 50 HDOC50' and wait 1.4s for the smooth scroll. The viewport shows only blank paper: the heading text line is at y=941 while the editor viewport spans y=149-776 (scrollTop 11,449). Clicking 'Heading 16 HDOC16' reproduces it (text at y=941). Screenshot: qa/shots/probe-long-outline-last-heading.png. Clicking the 48 unpadded entries (Heading 1, 10, 20, 25, 30, 40 tested) lands with the text at y=450-451, inside the viewport.
Actual: The click centers the heading element including its 980px of pagination padding, so the block box is centered but the heading text ends up 165px below the bottom of the viewport; the user is left looking at an empty page.

items.title: A failed localStorage write for the recent-projects list unmounts the whole app to a blank page
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (functional): expected A failed localStorage write is surfaced in the existing 'Retry save' error UI (as happens when the workspace write itself fails) and the editor stays on screen, so the user can keep writing or retry.
items.hint:
Repro: 1) Open http://localhost:1420 in a fresh browser profile so the start screen with 'New document' is shown. 2) In the devtools console run: const orig = Storage.prototype.setItem; Storage.prototype.setItem = function () { throw new DOMException('The quota has been exceeded.', 'QuotaExceededError'); }; (simulates private mode, blocked storage, or a zero quota). 3) Click the 'New document' button in the masthead. 4) Wait 1.5 s: document.body.innerText is empty (length 0), there is no .start-screen and no editor surface, and the console shows an uncaught 'pageerror: The quota has been exceeded.' Variant with a saved document: with an editor open and 'Saved locally', run const orig = Storage.prototype.setItem; Storage.prototype.setItem = function (k, v) { if (k === 'sentence.recent') throw new DOMException('The quota has been exceeded.', 'QuotaExceededError'); return orig.call(this, k, v); }, type ' persist-recent-1' at the end of the document and wait 1.6 s: localStorage['sentence.workspace'] contains the typed text but the editor is gone and the body is empty.
Actual: The app renders nothing at all. persistBrowser catches the failed workspace write, but rememberProject (src/App.tsx) then calls localStorage.setItem('sentence.recent', ...) inside the setRecent state updater with no try/catch. The exception is thrown during React render, there is no error boundary, and the whole tree is unmounted: body innerText length 0, editor count 0, start-screen count 0, and one 'pageerror: The quota has been exceeded.' In the recent-only variant the workspace was written successfully (workspaceSaved true) while the UI still went blank. Probe evidence: qa/probes/persistence.mjs phases 'storage-unavailable-on-create' and 'storage-unavailable-recent-only'.
items.source: explore:persistence:a failed localstorage write for the recent-projects list unmounts the whole app to a blank page

items.title: An unapplied, unparsable LaTeX draft is discarded on navigation away or reload with no warning
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (functional): expected The hand-written draft stays available so the user can fix it (the app already keeps invalid drafts across in-app Visual/Source switches), or the app warns before the page unloads.
items.hint:
Repro: 1) Open http://localhost:1420, click 'New document', wait until the top bar reads 'Saved locally'. 2) Click 'Source' in the status bar. 3) In the LaTeX textarea replace the final \end{document} line with 'Plan persist-nav-1' (the draft now has no \end{document}). 4) Within 400 ms, before the 1100 ms autosave, navigate to about:blank and then back to http://localhost:1420. 5) Read the top bar, the editor, and localStorage['sentence.workspace']. Variant: instead wait 1.5 s (the top bar shows 'Editing' and 'Retry save: Invalid LaTeX: missing \end{document}.'), then reload the page and open 'Source' to read the textarea.
Actual: No warning is shown (0 beforeunload dialogs in either variant), and the draft text is gone from the editor, the textarea and localStorage['sentence.workspace'] after returning; the top bar then reads 'Saved locally'. In the 400 ms variant no parse error was ever displayed before leaving (saveError null, toast null) because the debounce had not fired. In the awaited variant the draft is likewise absent after reload (draftMarkerInSource false, draftMarkerInStorage false, dialogsSeen 0). The pagehide flush in persist() re-parses the draft, catches the failure, and writes only the last good visual document, so the unapplied source text is lost silently. Probe evidence: qa/probes/persistence.mjs phases 'invalid-draft-navigation' and 'invalid-source-draft-after-reload'.
items.source: explore:persistence:an unapplied, unparsable latex draft is discarded on navigation away or reload with no warning

items.title: Every inserted image exports at 80% of the line width regardless of its natural size, so the PDF does not match the page
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (content): expected The exported image keeps the size the user sees on the page (natural size, or a size capped to the text block and page height), and an inline image is not 80% of the line width.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the demo document and press Ctrl+End. Click Insert > Image and supply a 40x80 px portrait PNG (the browser build feeds the hidden file input; cancelling the picker is clean). The figure renders 42x82 px on the page. Click View > LaTeX: the source contains \includegraphics[width=0.8\linewidth]{assets/images/<name>.png}. For the inline case, type 'SPLITLEFT SPLITRIGHT', place the caret after 'SPLITLEFT' and insert the same PNG: the image renders 12x22 px inside the sentence, yet the source again uses width=0.8\linewidth. An image inserted into a table cell (cell 303 px wide) is exported with the same width=0.8\linewidth inside the tabular.
Actual: The generated LaTeX always requests width=0.8\linewidth (src/lib/latex.ts imageWidthArgument falls back to 0.8 when attrs.width is 0) and the editor exposes no width control. A 40x80 image shown at 42x82 px is exported ~361 pt wide and ~722 pt tall; compiling that exported source with the bundled Tectonic prints 'LaTeX Warning: Float too large for page by 24.69325pt', pushes the figure to its own page, and the image fills the whole text block and reaches into the footer. The mid-sentence image (12x22 px, max-height 1.5em in the editor) becomes the same 0.8\linewidth graphic and the compiled document reports 'Overfull \hbox (56.59232pt too wide)' on that line. Probe: qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenarios 'image', 'image-inline-and-heading', 'table-cell'.
items.source: explore:insert-media:every inserted image exports at 80% of the line width regardless of its natural size, so the pdf does not match the page

items.title: Two different images with the same file name share one asset path and become the same picture after Apply source
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (functional): expected The two figures keep their own pictures (distinct asset paths or per-node image sources).
items.hint:
Repro: In the demo document press Ctrl+End, click Insert > Image and supply a red 120x60 PNG named 'qa image #1.png'. Press Ctrl+End again and use Insert > Image with a blue 40x80 PNG that has the same file name. Click View > LaTeX: both \includegraphics entries read assets/images/qa-image--1.png. Press Ctrl+End in the source textarea, type a space and Backspace so Apply source becomes enabled, click Apply source, then View > Visual.
Actual: Both image nodes carry data-path='assets/images/qa-image--1.png' and the LaTeX references that one path twice. After Apply source both figures show the second (blue 40x80) image (both imgs report natural 40x80); the first image is silently replaced, with the toast 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.' Probe: qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario 'image' (latexTwice, apply.info). Observed in the browser build, whose asset path comes from imageAssetPath(file.name) with no uniquifier.
items.source: explore:insert-media:two different images with the same file name share one asset path and become the same picture after apply source

items.title: Block images lose their alt text when the document is synchronized from LaTeX
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (content): expected The image keeps the alt text it had before the source synchronization (the file name).
items.hint:
Repro: Insert an image named 'qa image #1.png' at the end of the document. Click View > LaTeX, press Ctrl+End, type a space and Backspace so Apply source becomes enabled, click Apply source, then View > Visual and read the img alt attribute.
Actual: Before Apply the img has alt='qa image #1.png'; after Apply it has alt=''. Block images emit no '% Sentence alt' comment in the generated LaTeX (only inline images do) and the parser fills alt from the empty figure caption, so the alt text disappears from the document and from the HTML/Markdown exports. Probe: qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario 'image' (once.info vs apply.info).
items.source: explore:insert-media:block images lose their alt text when the document is synchronized from latex

items.title: Ctrl+A then switching list type wraps the whole document and nests the existing list
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (functional): expected The existing bullet list becomes a numbered list and 'intro' and 'outro' stay ordinary paragraphs, which is what happens when the same conversion is applied to a selection that covers only the list items.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new document. Type 'intro', press Enter, type 'one', click Home > Bulleted list, press Enter, type 'two', press Enter twice, type 'outro'. Press Ctrl+A (all four blocks are selected) and click Home > Numbered list. Repeat the same conversion with only the two list items selected (click 'one', press Home, then Shift+Down and Shift+End). Actual: With the whole document selected, clicking Numbered list turns every selected block into one ordered list: the editor DOM is '

  1. intro

    • one
    • two

  2. outro


' and the LaTeX is ' egin{enumerate} \item intro egin{itemize}...\end{itemize} \item outro \item \end{enumerate}'. The existing bullet list is moved under 'intro' as a sublist and an empty item is appended. With only a two-item bullet list in the document, Ctrl+A then Numbered list (ribbon button or Ctrl+Shift+7) also produces a third empty item and exports a trailing '\item '; selecting only the list items produces two items with no empty item.
items.source: explore:lists:ctrl+a then switching list type wraps the whole document and nests the existing list

items.title: Enter at the end of a parent item moves its nested sublist to the new item
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (functional): expected 'sibling' is added as a new top-level item after the sublist and 'child' stays nested under 'parent'.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new document. Type 'parent', click Home > Bulleted list, press Enter, type 'child', press Tab. Click at the end of the 'parent' line, press Enter and type 'sibling'. Actual: The existing sublist is transferred to the new item: the DOM is '

  • parent

  • sibling

    • child

', exported as '\item parent \item sibling egin{itemize} \item child \end{itemize}'. The child item silently changes parent from 'parent' to 'sibling'.
items.source: explore:lists:enter at the end of a parent item moves its nested sublist to the new item

items.title: Leaving a numbered list from the middle restarts the remaining items at 1
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (content): expected The remaining items keep their place in the sequence, so 'two' is number 2 and 'three' is number 3 and the resumed ordered list starts at 2.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new document. Type 'one', click Home > Numbered list, press Enter, type 'two', press Enter, type 'three'. Click at the end of 'one', press Enter (an empty item appears as number 2), then press Enter again on that empty item. Read the editor and then the LaTeX source. Actual: The list is split in two and the second list restarts at 1: the DOM is '

  1. one


  1. two

  2. three

', the second '
    ' has no start attribute, and the LaTeX is two separate '\begin{enumerate}' blocks, '\item one' then '\item two'/'\item three', with no '\setcounter'. The PDF therefore numbers 'two' as 1 and 'three' as 2, and the document shows two items numbered 1.
items.source: explore:lists:leaving a numbered list from the middle restarts the remaining items at 1

items.title: Deleting the last row or last column ejects the caret from the table, hides the table toolbar, and sends subsequent typi
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (functional): expected After deleting a row or column, the caret stays in the nearest remaining cell of the table, the Table toolbar stays available, and typing continues inside the table.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new project. Insert tab > Insert table (3x3 with header row). Click the middle cell of the last (third) row, type 'tail', then click 'Delete row' in the Table toolbar and type 'OUTSIDE' without clicking anywhere else. Repeat with a column: click a cell in the last column and click 'Delete column', then type 'AFTERCOL'.
Actual: The table shrinks (3x3 to 2x3 for the row delete, then 2x3 to 2x2 for the column delete) but the selection is no longer in any cell: document.activeElement is the editor div, focusCell reports inTable: false, and .table-toolbar is gone. Typing then lands in a paragraph after the table, so the exported LaTeX ends with '\end{table}

OUTSIDE' (and '

AFTERCOL' after the column delete) instead of putting the text in a cell. Deleting a non-last row/column leaves the caret in the table and the toolbar visible.
items.source: explore:tables:deleting the last row or last column ejects the caret from the table, hides the table toolbar, and sends subsequent typi

items.title: A table caption typed in the Table toolbar is exported to LaTeX but never shown in the visual document
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (visual): expected The caption is rendered with the table in the visual page, matching the exported \caption{Data \& results}, as figure captions are rendered under images.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new project. Insert tab > Insert table. Click a body cell so the Table toolbar appears, type 'Data & results' into its Caption field, then look at the page around the table. Switch to View > LaTeX and read the table block.
Actual: The caption exists only as data-caption="Data & results" on the table element and in the exported LaTeX (\caption{Data \& results}); the visual page renders no caption element and no caption text next to the table, so the caption is invisible unless the user opens the LaTeX source or the compiled PDF.
items.source: explore:tables:a table caption typed in the table toolbar is exported to latex but never shown in the visual document

items.title: Display equation inside a table cell is silently dropped from the LaTeX export
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (content): expected None
items.hint:
Repro: 1. From the start screen choose 'New document' and type 'Table below.' in the editor.
2. Open the Insert tab and click 'Insert table'; click the middle cell (second row, second column).
3. With the caret in that cell, open the Insert tab, click 'Equation block', enter `x^2+y^2=z^2` and click Insert. The equation renders inside the cell (`[data-math-block]` with `inCell: true`, `latex: x^2+y^2=z^2`).
4. Open the View tab and click 'LaTeX', then click 'Refresh from visual' and read document.tex.
5. Click 'Apply source' to load that exported text back into the visual document.
Expected: the equation is written into the tabular cell (or the editor refuses to place display math in a table cell and says so); applying the exported source must not lose it.
Actual: document.tex contains the table with three completely empty rows and no `x^2+y^2=z^2` or equation environment anywhere (the equation exists only in the visual model, because table cells export through inlineContent). After 'Apply source' the toast says 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.' and the visual table has no math node at all, so the equation is permanently lost.
Actual: None
items.source: explore:math:display equation inside a table cell is silently dropped from the latex export

items.title: Blank line inside inline math is accepted, exported as invalid LaTeX, then silently converted to text on Apply source
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (functional): expected None
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Choose 'New document', type 'Before ' and open Insert > 'Inline equation'.
2. In the LaTeX source textarea enter `a`, then an empty line, then `b` (the value is `a\n\nb`). The preview renders 'ab' and Insert/Update stays enabled (`invalidClass: false`, `submitDisabled: false`).
3. Click Insert, open View > 'LaTeX', click 'Refresh from visual' and read document.tex: it contains `Before \(a` followed by a blank line and `b\)`.
4. Click 'Apply source'. The toast reports 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.'
5. Switch to View > 'Visual': the math node is gone; the document is two plain paragraphs containing the literal text `\(a` and `b\)`.
6. Open View > 'LaTeX' and click 'Refresh from visual' again: the body is now `Before \textbackslash{}(a` / blank line / `b\textbackslash{})`.
Expected: a blank line inside math is invalid LaTeX (LaTeX ends the paragraph before the closing delimiter), so the dialog should flag it and disable Insert just as it does for `\frac{` and unclosed `{`; failing that, Apply source must report an error instead of destroying the equation.
Actual: the blank line passes KaTeX validation and is inserted; the exported source is uncompilable, and applying it is reported as a success while the math node is silently replaced by escaped literal text.
Actual: None
items.source: explore:math:blank line inside inline math is accepted, exported as invalid latex, then silently converted to text on apply source

items.title: Display equations inside blockquotes or list items are imported as literal text and escaped on export
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (content): expected None
items.source: explore:math:display equations inside blockquotes or list items are imported as literal text and escaped on export

items.title: Two-column documents: settings, preamble and round trip
items.why: A two-column arXiv paper is the single most common LaTeX target the app cannot produce.
items.hint: Add `columns: "one" | "two"` to ProjectSettings in src/lib/types.ts (default "one"). Emit the `twocolumn` class option in documentToLatex (src/lib/latex.ts, the \documentclass line around 512) and parse it back in latexToDocument. Add a Columns control to the Layout ribbon group in src/components/Ribbon.tsx. Acceptance: unit tests in src/lib/latex.test.ts prove article+two emits \documentclass[11pt,a4paper,twocolumn]{article} and that latexToDocument reads it back; gate green.
items.source: roadmap:two-column documents: settings, preamble and round trip

items.title: Multi-key citations are merged into one invalid key by the LaTeX round trip
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (content): expected The two cited keys stay separate in the document and in the export: `\cite{sentence2026,ghost2026}` (a citation with two keys).
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. Open View > LaTeX and insert the line `MultiCite \cite{sentence2026,ghost2026} done.` before `\end{document}`, then click Visual. Type `ZZ` at the end of the document and open View > LaTeX again.
Actual: The visual editor turns the pair into one citation labelled `[sentence2026,ghost2026]`, the References panel reports `sentence2026,ghost2026` as a single key missing from the bibliography, and the regenerated source reads `\cite{sentence2026ghost2026}`: the comma is stripped and both keys become one nonexistent key. The manual citation dialog also rejects commas, so a multi-key citation cannot be created or preserved through the UI.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:multi-key citations are merged into one invalid key by the latex round trip

items.title: Typing after applying or removing a hyperlink replaces the link text
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (functional): expected Applying or removing a link leaves the document text intact and puts the caret after it, so continuing the sentence appends the typed characters.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. At the end type `LinkTypeAdd `, then `wordone`, select `wordone`, press Ctrl+K, enter `https://type.example.org/add`, click Insert, and immediately type `AFTER` without clicking in the page. Then at the end type `RemoveType linkedword`, select `linkedword`, press Ctrl+K, enter `https://remove.example.org`, click Insert, click the new link, press Ctrl+K, click `Remove link`, and type `KEEP`.
Actual: The link text stays selected when the dialog closes. Typing `AFTER` replaces `wordone`, so the paragraph reads `LinkTypeAdd AFTER` and the link now has the text `AFTER`. Likewise, after Remove link, typing `KEEP` replaces `linkedword` and the paragraph reads `RemoveType KEEP`: the linked word is silently destroyed by the next keystroke.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:typing after applying or removing a hyperlink replaces the link text

items.title: Clicking a footnote marker and typing deletes the footnote
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (functional): expected Typing after clicking the footnote reference should not discard the note; text may be inserted next to the marker, or the marker should require an explicit delete.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. At the end type `MarkerType `, open Insert > Footnote, enter `MT note`, click Insert. Click the superscript marker once, then type `Q`.
Actual: The click selects the footnote atom (`.ProseMirror-selectednode` is set); the next keystroke replaces it with body text. The paragraph becomes `MarkerType Q`, `MT note` disappears from the page, and the note is removed from the exported LaTeX instead of only the marker being edited.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:clicking a footnote marker and typing deletes the footnote

items.title: After updating a footnote the caret is placed before the marker
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (ux): expected After Update the caret stays after the footnote reference, so the line reads `EditFocus ¹NEXT` with the note attached after `EditFocus`.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. At the end type `EditFocus `, open Insert > Footnote, enter `EF note`, click Insert, double-click the marker, change the note to `EF edited`, click Update, then type `NEXT`.
Actual: The caret is left before the marker, so typing `NEXT` inserts ahead of it: the line becomes `EditFocus NEXT¹`. The continuing text is written on the wrong side of the note reference.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:after updating a footnote the caret is placed before the marker

items.title: Tracked-change decorations are drawn in the wrong paragraph when an identical line appears earlier
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (visual): expected The struck-through deletion is displayed in the second paragraph (the paragraph that was edited), and the first paragraph still reads 'Same line'.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a fresh document, type 'Same line', press Enter, and type 'Same line' again so two identical paragraphs exist. 2. Open the Review tab and click Track changes. 3. Put the caret at the end of the second paragraph, press Ctrl+Shift+Left to select its last word 'line', then press Backspace. 4. Wait 2.5 s and open the History sidebar. Insertion variant: start from paragraphs 'Same row' and 'Same line', tracking on, select 'line' in the second paragraph and type 'row'.
Actual: The deletion decoration is rendered inside the first, unedited paragraph, which displays 'Same lineline' with 'line' struck through, while the edited second paragraph shows only 'Same '. The insertion variant similarly highlights the inserted 'row' in the first paragraph instead of the second. Probe: deletions [{text:'line', paragraph:0, parent:'Same lineline'}], insertions [{text:'row', paragraph:0}].
items.source: explore:review:tracked-change decorations are drawn in the wrong paragraph when an identical line appears earlier

items.title: Edits applied from the LaTeX source pane while tracking is on are never recorded as revisions
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected Because tracking is on, applying the edited LaTeX is recorded as a pending tracked change the reviewer can accept or reject.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. In a fresh document type 'Source track base' and let it settle. 2. Review tab > Track changes; the button now reads 'Tracking on'. 3. View tab > LaTeX, change the body text to 'Source track base revised', and click Apply source. 4. Wait 2.5 s and open the History sidebar.
Actual: History lists 0 tracked changes. The edited text is applied immediately (editor reads 'Source track base revised') while the Review tab still reports 'Tracking on', so the change silently bypasses review. Probe: revisions [], text 'Source track base revised', trackingButtonLabel 'Tracking on'.
items.source: explore:review:edits applied from the latex source pane while tracking is on are never recorded as revisions

items.title: Undoing a comment addition leaves an orphaned thread with a false 'text was deleted' note
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected Undo removes the comment highlight and its thread together, so no comment remains for text that still exists.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Type 'Undo comment body'. 2. Select 'comment', open Review > New comment, enter 'Undo this comment' and click Comment. 3. Click in the editor and press Ctrl+Z.
Actual: The highlight disappears, but the thread stays in the Review panel, is marked with the note 'The text this comment was attached to was deleted, so it has no highlight in the document.' and still counts in the unresolved badge. The text was not deleted — the comment mark was undone. Probe: marks [], thread body 'Undo this comment', detached=true, detachedNote=true.
items.source: explore:review:undoing a comment addition leaves an orphaned thread with a false 'text was deleted' note

items.title: A paragraph-break-only tracked change produces a History card with identical before/after text and no inline decoration
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (ux): expected The tracked revision shows what changed (the inserted paragraph break/empty paragraph) so the reviewer can accept or reject it knowingly.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Type 'Only paragraph'. 2. Review tab > Track changes. 3. Put the caret at the end of the paragraph and press Enter. 4. Wait 2.5 s and open the History sidebar.
Actual: The card shows before 'Only paragraph' and after 'Only paragraph' — identical — and the document gets no insertion decoration for the new empty paragraph. Accepting leaves the empty paragraph behind. Probe: revision {before:'Only paragraph', after:'Only paragraph'}, insertions [], deletions [], paragraphs ['Only paragraph', ''].
items.source: explore:review:a paragraph-break-only tracked change produces a history card with identical before/after text and no inline decoration

items.title: History card preview clips to the last 180 characters, so edits near the start of a long document show identical before/
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (ux): expected The revision card's before/after previews show the inserted 'Z' at the start of the paragraph.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Type a long paragraph of about 400 characters, for example 'start ' followed by 42 filler words and ' end'. 2. Review tab > Track changes. 3. Put the caret at the very start of the paragraph and type 'Z'. 4. Wait 2.5 s and open the History sidebar.
Actual: Both previews are the last 180 characters of the paragraph and are byte-identical, so the card shows no difference even though the document now starts with 'Zstart ...'. Probe: beforeLength 180, afterLength 180, identical=true, editorStart 'Zstart filler0 filler1 filler2'.
items.source: explore:review:history card preview clips to the last 180 characters, so edits near the start of a long document show identical before/

items.title: A commented-out \end{document} silently truncates the rest of the document
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (functional): expected The comment is ignored (as LaTeX does), the paragraph after it is imported into the visual document, and the regenerated LaTeX contains it before the real \end{document}.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and open the editor. 2. View > LaTeX. 3. Before the real \end{document}, add the comment line `% ZXCOMMENTED \end{document} marker`, a blank line, the paragraph `ZXAFTERCOMMENT paragraph`, a blank line, and keep the real \end{document}. 4. Click Apply source. 5. View > Visual, then View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual.
Actual: Apply reports `Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.` but the visual document does not contain ZXAFTERCOMMENT, and Refresh from visual drops the paragraph from the source. The draft still contains the paragraph immediately after Apply and Apply is disabled, so the pane looks synchronized while the document has silently lost the text. Probe: visualHasAfterComment=false, draftKeptAfterApply=true, regeneratedHasAfterComment=false, applyEnabledAfter=false.
items.source: explore:source-editor:a commented-out \end{document} silently truncates the rest of the document

items.title: Undo after Apply also removes the text that was just applied, and re-applying deletes it from the page
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (functional): expected One Ctrl+Z removes only `ZXNEW`; the applied `ZXAPPLIED` stays in the source, Apply stays disabled because the draft still equals the applied LaTeX.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. View > LaTeX. 2. Put the caret before \end{document} and type `ZXAPPLIED`. 3. Click Apply source and wait for the success toast. 4. Without moving the caret, type `ZXNEW`. 5. Press Ctrl+Z once. 6. Click Apply source if it is enabled. 7. Variant from a clean applied document: type `ZXFAIL`, Enter, `\begin{itemize}`, Enter, `NOEND`; click Apply source (it fails); type `ZXTYPEDAFTERFAIL`; press Ctrl+Z once.
Actual: One Ctrl+Z removes both `ZXNEW` and the applied `ZXAPPLIED` from the textarea. Apply becomes enabled, and clicking it synchronizes the document without ZXAPPLIED, so the paragraph disappears from the visual page. Probe: undoKeptAppliedText=false, undoRemovedNewText=true, applyEnabledAfterUndo=true, visualHasAppliedTextAfterReapply=false. The same coalescing occurs when the edit was applied by switching to Visual and when Apply failed: after typing `ZXTYPEDAFTERFAIL` and pressing Ctrl+Z once, the `NOEND` line of the broken draft also disappeared (undoKeptEnvironmentText=false).
items.source: explore:source-editor:undo after apply also removes the text that was just applied, and re-applying deletes it from the page

items.title: A section with an optional short title is imported as literal text and escaped
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (content): expected A level-1 heading `ZXOPT FULL TITLE` appears (the optional argument is the short title used in the table of contents), and the re-exported LaTeX keeps `\section[ZXSHORT]{ZXOPT FULL TITLE}` or at least `\section{ZXOPT FULL TITLE}`.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. View > LaTeX. 2. Before \end{document}, add `\section[ZXSHORT]{ZXOPT FULL TITLE}`, a blank line, and `ZXOPT BODY`. 3. Click Apply source. 4. View > Visual. 5. View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual.
Actual: Apply reports success but no heading is created: the visual page shows the raw line `\section[ZXSHORT]{ZXOPT FULL TITLE}` as a paragraph (headings remain only Introduction and Drafting with constraints). Refresh from visual writes `\textbackslash{}section[ZXSHORT]\{ZXOPT FULL TITLE\}`, corrupting valid LaTeX. Probe: headingKept=false, escapedCommand=true.
items.source: explore:source-editor:a section with an optional short title is imported as literal text and escaped

items.title: A section \label on the line after the heading becomes literal text and is lost
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (content): expected The heading is `ZXSEPLABEL`, the label is attached to it, and the re-exported LaTeX contains `\section{ZXSEPLABEL}\label{sec:seplabel}` or an equivalent attached label so `\ref{sec:seplabel}` resolves.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. View > LaTeX. 2. Before \end{document}, add `\section{ZXSEPLABEL}` on one line, `\label{sec:seplabel}` on the next line, a blank line, `ZXSEP BODY`, a blank line, and `See \ref{sec:seplabel}.` 3. Click Apply source. 4. View > Visual. 5. View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual.
Actual: The heading is created, but the label becomes its own paragraph showing the raw command `\label{sec:seplabel}` in the visual document (leakedCommands=true). Refresh from visual writes `\textbackslash{}label\{sec:seplabel\}`, so the label is gone while `\ref{sec:seplabel}` remains. Probe: labelKept=false, labelEscaped=true, refKept=true.
items.source: explore:source-editor:a section \label on the line after the heading becomes literal text and is lost

items.title: Preamble packages and macros are reported synchronized but silently dropped, and their calls are escaped
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (functional): expected The package and macro definition survive in the LaTeX (or Apply reports that preamble edits are unsupported), and the macro call is either expanded or preserved.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. View > LaTeX. 2. Before `\begin{document}`, add `\usepackage{amsthm}` and `\newcommand{\ZXMACRO}{ZXMACRO EXPANDS}`. 3. Before `\end{document}`, add `ZXPREAMBLE use \ZXMACRO{} here.` 4. Click Apply source. 5. View > Visual. 6. View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual.
Actual: Apply reports `Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.` The draft still contains the package and definition immediately after Apply, but the visual page shows the literal `\ZXMACRO` call. After Refresh from visual the preamble no longer contains amsthm or \newcommand, and the body contains `\textbackslash{}ZXMACRO\{\}`. Probe: regeneratedPreambleHasPackage=false, regeneratedHasMacro=false, escapedMacroCall=true. The source only reveals the loss after a refresh, so the success toast is the only feedback at Apply time.
items.source: explore:source-editor:preamble packages and macros are reported synchronized but silently dropped, and their calls are escaped

items.title: Hand-written align environments are imported as literal text and escaped
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (content): expected The align environment becomes display math (editable, like the supported equation environment), or Apply reports it as unsupported rather than rewriting it.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. View > LaTeX. 2. Before \end{document}, add a display block containing `\begin{align}`, `ZXALIGN a &= b + c \\`, `d &= e`, and `\end{align}`. 3. Click Apply source. 4. View > Visual. 5. View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual.
Actual: Apply reports success, but zero math blocks are created and the visual page shows the raw `\begin{align}...\end{align}` lines as paragraph text (leakedCommands=true). Refresh from visual escapes every command: `\textbackslash{}begin\{align\}`, `\&`, `\textbackslash{}end\{align\}`. Probe mathBlocks=[], escaped commands present.
items.source: explore:source-editor:hand-written align environments are imported as literal text and escaped

items.title: A hand-written table \label is silently dropped, leaving a dangling \ref
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (content): expected The table is imported with its caption and `\label{tab:zxtable}` intact in the regenerated LaTeX, so the following \ref refers to the table.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. View > LaTeX. 2. Before \end{document}, add a table with `\caption{ZXCAPTION}` and `\label{tab:zxtable}`, rows `Name & Value \\` and `ZXTABLELABEL & 7 \\`, then a blank line and `See Table~\ref{tab:zxtable}.` 3. Click Apply source. 4. View > Visual. 5. View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual.
Actual: The table and caption import correctly, but the regenerated table contains no `\label{tab:zxtable}`; only `See Table\textasciitilde{}\ref{tab:zxtable}` remains. The label was silently dropped, so the reference has no target. Probe: labelKept=false, refKept=true.
items.source: explore:source-editor:a hand-written table \label is silently dropped, leaving a dangling \ref

items.title: \multicolumn in a hand-written table is turned into a cell's literal text
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (content): expected The first row is a two-column spanning header (or Apply rejects the unsupported construct); the row should not contain the raw \multicolumn command.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. View > LaTeX. 2. Before \end{document}, add a tabular with `\hline`, `\multicolumn{2}{c}{ZXMULTI HEADER} \\`, `ZXMULTI A & B \\`, `\hline`, `\end{tabular}` wrapped in a table environment. 3. Click Apply source. 4. View > Visual. 5. View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual.
Actual: The visual table has two rows, with the first row as an empty first cell and the second cell containing the literal string `\multicolumn{2}{c}{ZXMULTI HEADER}`. Refresh from visual writes `\textbackslash{}multicolumn\{2\}\{c\}\{ZXMULTI HEADER\}`, so the valid spanning header is destroyed. Probe cells: `["", "\multicolumn{2}{c}{ZXMULTI HEADER}"]`.

items.title: Page text and headings overflow into the top and bottom margins

items.hint:
Repro: Run `node qa/probes/long-document.mjs` and read the `layout` stage, or reproduce by hand: open http://localhost:1420 at 1280x800, click 'New document', then Ctrl+A and Backspace to empty the page. Put the probe's 50-section HTML on the clipboard (50 blocks of `

Heading N HDOCN

[the probe's 69-word body] BODYN

`, with `

` for N divisible by 5 and `

` for N divisible by 11; 3,600 words total) and press Ctrl+V. The status bar reads 3,600 words / 10 pages and the sheet is 11,230px tall. The page height is 1,123px and the configured margin is 96px, so each page's text area is y=96..1027. The probe's DOM audit finds 26 text lines below the bottom margin and 22 above the top margin. On page 1 the last three line boxes end at 1,069, 1,094 and 1,120px, i.e. the final line is 3px above the page edge. Headings also sit in the margins: Heading 5 at 89px and Heading 16 at 18px from the top of pages 2 and 4, and Heading 10 at 1,093px and Heading 37 at 1,088px down pages 2 and 7 (the bottom margin starts at 1,027px). Actual: The probe measures 26 text lines below the bottom margin and 22 above the top margin across the 10 pages, with the last line of page 1 ending 3px above the page edge. items.title: A paragraph longer than a page is cut by every page rule

Repro: In the same empty document, paste one 3,100-word paragraph with Ctrl+V: 100 copies of the 30-word sentence 'The visual editor keeps this sentence in the document model while the LaTeX source is generated. Measurements and observations are recorded together so that later edits remain easy to review.' joined by single spaces, with W1..W100 appended to the copies (the probe's `oneParagraph` stage builds exactly this). The status bar reads 3,100 words / 5 pages and the editor contains one paragraph whose box is 5,047px tall. The page rules sit at 1,123, 2,246, 3,369 and 4,492px in sheet coordinates. All four rules cross a line box: 1,123 vs 1,123-1,139, 2,246 vs 2,233-2,249, 3,369 vs 3,368-3,384, and 4,492 vs 4,479-4,495. Screenshot: qa/shots/probe-long-document-one-paragraph.png.

items.title: Text typed after \end{document} in the LaTeX pane is silently discarded while the app reports it saved
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (functional): expected Text typed at the end of the source after \end{document} should either be placed into the document, or rejected with a visible parse error that keeps the draft and leaves the indicator unsaved. It must never disappear while the UI reports a successful save.
items.hint:
Repro: 1) Open http://localhost:1420 with no saved workspace (the start screen shows), click 'New document' and wait for the top bar to read 'Saved locally'. 2) Click 'Source' in the status bar. 3) Click in the LaTeX textarea, press Ctrl+End (the caret lands after the final \end{document}) and type a new line such as 'trailing paragraph tail-1'. 4) Wait 1.6 s: the top bar still reads 'Saved locally' with its check icon and the console shows no error, localStorage['sentence.workspace.draft'] has been removed, and the textarea still shows the typed line, but the document inside localStorage['sentence.workspace'] does not contain 'tail-1'. 5) Switch to 'Visual': the text is not in the document. 6) Switch back to 'Source': the text is gone from the textarea too. 7) Reload the page: the textarea, the visual editor and localStorage contain no 'tail-1', there is no draft and no warning (toast null, Retry save absent). Variant: after step 3 click 'Apply source' instead of waiting; the toast reads 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.' while the visual editor and the stored document still do not contain the text, and a reload drops it permanently. Probe evidence: qa/probes/persistence.mjs phases 'source-after-end-document', 'source-after-end-autosave' and 'apply-source-after-end' (both the autosave path and the Apply path observed on 2026-11-25).
Actual: The source parser takes only the slice between \begin{document} and \end{document} (src/lib/latex.ts documentBody), so the trailing text is dropped without an error and the draft is treated as successfully applied. persist() deletes the mirrored draft (localStorage['sentence.workspace.draft'] gone), sets saveState to 'saved' ('Saved locally' plus check icon) and writes a workspace whose document JSON has no trace of the typed text. After autosave the source pane still shows the typed line, so the pane and the saved document disagree; switching views or reloading removes the line for good, with no toast and no Retry save. In the Apply variant the toast explicitly claims 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.' while the visual editor and stored document lack the text.
items.source: explore:persistence:text typed after \end{document} in the latex pane is silently discarded while the app reports it saved

items.title: The save indicator says 'Saved locally' while the initial workspace write has failed
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (ux): expected When the only workspace write fails, the save indicator should not claim the document is saved; it should show the unsaved/error state that the Retry save button is already reporting.
items.hint:
Repro: 1) Open http://localhost:1420 with no saved workspace so the start screen shows. 2) In the devtools console run: const orig = Storage.prototype.setItem; Storage.prototype.setItem = function (key, value) { if (key === 'sentence.workspace') throw new DOMException('The quota has been exceeded.', 'QuotaExceededError'); return orig.call(this, key, value); }; (simulates a full or blocked localStorage). 3) Click 'New document'. 4) Wait 1 s. The editor opens and the top bar reads 'Saved locally' next to a 'Retry save: The quota has been exceeded.' button and the same quota toast, while localStorage['sentence.workspace'] does not exist and no check icon is shown. 5) Restore Storage.prototype.setItem to orig and click 'Retry save': the document is then written and the indicator remains 'Saved locally'. Probe evidence: qa/probes/persistence.mjs phase 'create-with-storage-blocked'.
Actual: The header label is driven only by the dirty flag, which is set to false when a workspace is adopted, so it renders 'Saved locally' even though persistBrowser failed. The same top bar simultaneously shows 'Retry save: The quota has been exceeded.' and localStorage has no sentence.workspace key (workspaceKey false), i.e. no saved copy exists. The error UI and the saved label contradict each other.
items.source: explore:persistence:the save indicator says 'saved locally' while the initial workspace write has failed

items.title: Ctrl+Alt+1/2/3 change the current block's heading level on their way to switching views

Repro: Open a project, click into a plain paragraph reading "mode probe paragraph" and press Ctrl+Alt+2 — the shortcut the View ribbon advertises on its "LaTeX (Ctrl+Alt+2)" button and the status bar repeats as "Source (Ctrl+Alt+2)". The app switches to the source view and the LaTeX for that line reads \subsection{mode probe paragraph}. Switching back with the status-bar Visual button shows

mode probe paragraph

plus an extra empty paragraph. The same collision happens for Ctrl+Alt+1 while already in Visual (the paragraph becomes

and is exported as \section{mode probe two}; the view stays Visual) and for Ctrl+Alt+3 (

, \subsubsection). Ctrl+Alt+2 pressed with the caret in the third of three paragraphs turns only that paragraph into \subsection and leaves the other two alone. Actual: Tiptap also binds Mod-Alt-1/2/3 to setHeading(level 1/2/3), so one key press does both: the mode switch runs and the block under the caret is rewritten as a heading. The rewritten heading is saved and exported (\section / \subsection / \subsubsection). Probe evidence: before {"

mode probe paragraph

", mode Visual} -> after Ctrl+Alt+2 {mode Source, visual

mode probe paragraph

, source line \subsection{mode probe paragraph}}; after Ctrl+Alt+1 in Visual:

mode probe two

, source line \section{mode probe two}.

items.title: Escape closes the Properties panel behind a dialog instead of the dialog in front of it, and leaves focus on the page be
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected One Escape closes the front-most overlay (the dialog, or the find bar) and focus stays inside it; the non-modal Properties panel behind it is left alone. Navigating the page behind an open aria-modal dialog should not be possible with the keyboard.
items.hint:
Repro: In the editor click the Settings (avatar) button to open the Properties panel, click into a word in the document, then press Ctrl+K to open the Add link dialog. Press Escape once. The Properties panel closes, the Add link dialog and its backdrop stay open, and focus is moved to the avatar Settings button underneath the backdrop. Pressing Escape a second time finally closes the dialog. The find bar behaves the same way: with Properties open press Ctrl+F, then Escape — the panel closes, the find bar stays open and focus is on the Settings button.
Actual: The Inspector's window keydown handler closes the panel on Escape without checking for a dialog or find bar on top, and its effect cleanup restores focus to the Settings button. Probe counts before/after one Escape: {modal 1, inspector 1} -> {modal 1, inspector 0, focus BUTTON.avatar-button "Settings"}; the dialog needs a second Escape. For the find bar: {find 1, inspector 1} -> {find 1, inspector 0, focus "Settings"}.
items.source: explore:keyboard:escape closes the properties panel behind a dialog instead of the dialog in front of it, and leaves focus on the page be

items.title: Tabbing out of the text-colour palette leaves it and its full-window backdrop open, and Escape no longer closes it
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (functional): expected Leaving the palette with Tab closes it (or Escape closes it from anywhere), so a keyboard user can keep using the ribbon.
items.hint:
Repro: Home ribbon tab, focus "Text color" and press Enter to open the palette, then press Tab twelve times. Focus walks through the ten swatches to the neighbouring "Highlight" trigger and on to the Paragraph style select, but the palette remains open with its .color-backdrop (position fixed, inset 0, z-index 60) over the ribbon. Press Escape on the select: nothing happens. Shift+Tab back once to the "Highlight" trigger and press Escape: still nothing. elementFromPoint at a ribbon button's position returns DIV.color-backdrop, so ribbon clicks hit the backdrop instead of the control. Only Shift+Tab back onto one of the ten swatches and pressing Escape (or clicking the invisible backdrop) closes it and returns focus to the "Text color" button.
Actual: The palette stays mounted: popover 1 and color-backdrop 1 after the twelve Tabs and after both Escape presses; hit-test over the ribbon returns "DIV.color-backdrop". Only Escape while focus is inside the owning .color-menu works (Escape from the neighbouring Highlight palette is ignored because that menu's own open state is false).
items.source: explore:keyboard:tabbing out of the text-colour palette leaves it and its full-window backdrop open, and escape no longer closes it

items.title: Existing equations cannot be opened from the keyboard; Enter on the selected math node does nothing
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected Enter opens the equation editor for the selected equation, the same way Enter opens the footnote editor for a selected footnote marker, so editing an existing equation has a keyboard path.
items.hint:
Repro: Insert ribbon tab, focus "Inline equation", press Enter, type x^2 and press Ctrl+Enter. Click into the document, press Ctrl+End and then ArrowLeft once: the equation is selected (selection constructor NodeSelection, node mathInline, class ProseMirror-selectednode). Press Enter: no dialog opens and the document is unchanged. A single mouse click on the equation opens the "Edit inline equation" dialog. The footnote control behaves as intended: arrow-select its marker and Enter opens "Edit footnote".
Actual: The editor's handleKeyDown only handles a NodeSelection whose node type is "footnote"; math nodes are edited solely through handleClick. Probe evidence: selection {type NodeSelection, node mathInline}, Enter -> modal 0; click -> modal 1, title "Edit inline equation".

items.title: The writing surface is 34 Tab presses from the top of the page, with no skip link or focus shortcut

items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (visual): expected Text fields in dialogs show the same clearly visible 2px focus outline as the buttons next to them.

two

Repro: Create a new document. Type 'outer one', click Home > Numbered list, press Enter, type 'middle one', press Tab, press Enter, type 'deep one', press Tab. Read the three markers in the editor, then open Source and read the LaTeX.

items.title: A table caption containing a closing brace is silently corrupted by a LaTeX source round trip
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (content): expected The caption stays 'R&D 50% {x}' in the visual table, the Caption field, and the re-exported LaTeX.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new project. Insert tab > Insert table. Click a body cell, type 'R&D 50% {x}' into the Table toolbar's Caption field, then switch to View > LaTeX and confirm the line \caption{R\&D 50\% \{x\}}. Add a new line containing '% check' at the end of the source and click Apply source. Look at the caption under the table and the Caption field, then switch to View > LaTeX again.
Actual: After Apply source the visible caption and the Caption field both read 'R&D 50% {x\' - the closing brace is gone and a backslash is appended. The re-exported line is \caption{R\&D 50\% \{x\\}}, so the literal '}' is permanently lost and replaced by a LaTeX line break. A caption without a brace ('Simple caption') round-trips unchanged, and caption text is the only place this was observed; the same '{x}' text in a table cell survives the round trip.
items.source: explore:tables:a table caption containing a closing brace is silently corrupted by a latex source round trip

items.title: Tab in the last table cell jumps to the 'Visual' view button and the next keystrokes are discarded
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (functional): expected Tab from the last cell either adds a row (Word's behaviour) or moves the caret into the empty paragraph directly after the table, so continued typing lands in a text position.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new project. Insert tab > Insert table. Click the bottom-right cell, type 'b3', press Tab once, then type 'AFTER' without clicking anywhere. Read the document and then switch to View > LaTeX and read the source.
Actual: The table stays 3x3 with no new row, the empty paragraph after the table is skipped, and focus lands on the 'Visual (Ctrl+Alt+1)' view button in the bottom status bar (document.activeElement is that BUTTON, activeElement.closest('.tiptap') is false).
