items.title: A tracked edit saved just before a reload loses its tracked revision
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (functional): expected Once the app reports the document as saved, or when a page unloads, any pending tracked revision should be committed with the document, so after a reload History can still show, accept, or reject the edit. The saved indicator should not say 'Saved locally' while revision metadata is still unpersisted.
items.hint:
Repro: 1) Open http://localhost:1420 with no saved workspace, click 'New document' and wait for the top bar to read 'Saved locally'. 2) Open the Review tab and click 'Track changes' (it becomes 'Tracking on'). 3) Click at the end of the last paragraph, type ' track-one' and wait 3.2 s: Review > History shows one tracked revision. 4) Reload the page (Ctrl+R). The tracking mode resets off. 5) Review > Track changes again. 6) Click at the end of the last paragraph, type ' track-two' and wait until the top bar reads 'Saved locally' with its check icon (about 1.3 s after typing), then reload immediately. 7) After the reload 'track-two' is still in the document and the top bar still reads 'Saved locally', but Review > History still lists only the 'track-one' revision; localStorage['sentence.workspace'].revisions has the same count as before the edit (2 in the probe) and no revision contains 'track-two'. The edit was silently accepted as untracked, so it can no longer be reviewed or rejected. Probe evidence: qa/probes/persistence.mjs phase 'tracked-change-reload' (pending: savedAt 1302 ms, indicator 'Saved locally' with check, revisionCount 2, storedHasThird true; after reload: textHasThird true, revisionCount 2, thirdInRevision false). Controls in the same phase show a tracked edit that waits 3.2 s does store its revision, both before and after a reload.
Actual: Visual tracked edits are committed by a separate 1800 ms timer (revisionTimer in src/App.tsx), while the workspace autosave runs after 1100 ms and sets saveState to 'saved'. The pagehide flush in App.tsx calls persist(), which writes workspaceRef.current as-is and never commits the pending revisionBaseline, so reloading between the autosave and the revision timer stores the text without its Revision. The History panel and the stored revisions array silently omit the edit even though the top bar said 'Saved locally' with a check icon.
items.source: explore:persistence:a tracked edit saved just before a reload loses its tracked revision

items.title: Ctrl+Alt+1 back to Visual leaves focus on <body>, so the next keystrokes are silently discarded
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (functional): expected The Visual view receives keyboard focus when it becomes active, exactly as the Source textarea receives focus after Ctrl+Alt+2, so a keyboard user can keep typing after switching views.
items.hint:
Repro: Open a project, click into the document, select all and type "mode probe paragraph". Press Ctrl+Alt+2 (Source): the status bar switches to Source and focus lands in the "LaTeX source" textarea. Press Ctrl+Alt+1 (Visual): the status bar switches to Visual, but document.activeElement is <body>, not the ProseMirror editor. Type "QRS": the document still reads "mode probe paragraph", and QRS appears nowhere on the page or in the LaTeX source. Typing only works again after clicking the page, pressing F6 or tabbing back. The same happens when leaving Split for Visual while the caret is in the source pane: Ctrl+Alt+1 from Split puts focus on <body> and the next typing is lost.
Actual: After Ctrl+Alt+1 the LaTeX textarea is gone from the DOM and activeElement is {tag: "BODY"}; nothing has moved focus into the visual editor. Typing QRS leaves the visual document unchanged ("mode probe paragraph") and bodyText does not contain QRS. Ctrl+Alt+2 works because focus lands in the source textarea; there is no equivalent handoff for visual.
items.source: explore:keyboard:ctrl+alt+1 back to visual leaves focus on <body>, so the next keystrokes are silently discarded

items.title: Escape does not leave the LaTeX source editor, contradicting the status-bar hint
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (functional): expected Escape leaves the source editing surface, the documented mirror of F6, matching the visual editor's Escape behaviour.
items.hint:
Repro: Open a project and press Ctrl+Alt+2 to switch to Source. Click at the end of the "LaTeX source" textarea and press Escape. Focus remains on the textarea (document.activeElement is still the LaTeX source textarea). The status-bar hint's tooltip reads "F6 moves focus into the document, Esc leaves the editing surface"; pressing Escape in the visual editor does move focus to the status bar, while in source view it does nothing. Tab does move focus out of the textarea (to the Visual button in the status bar), so Escape is not the way out.
Actual: The source textarea has no Escape handler. Probe: focus before Escape {TEXTAREA, aria-label "LaTeX source"}, focus after Escape the same textarea; no focus change.
items.source: explore:keyboard:escape does not leave the latex source editor, contradicting the status-bar hint

items.title: The LaTeX source textarea has no visible focus outline
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (visual): expected The focused source textarea shows the same visible focus indicator as the other controls, so a keyboard user can see where typing will go.
items.hint:
Repro: Switch to Source with Ctrl+Alt+2 (focus moves into the "LaTeX source" textarea) and inspect its computed style: outline-style is none and outline-width is 0px while the element matches :focus-visible. Every ribbon button, every select and the find field in the same app show the 2px solid rgb(78, 128, 103) focus outline.
Actual: Computed outline is "none 0px" with :focus-visible true; the textarea's caret is the only focus cue.
items.source: explore:keyboard:the latex source textarea has no visible focus outline

items.title: Sidebar panel buttons do not expose which panel is open to assistive technology
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected The open panel is exposed in the accessibility tree (for example aria-current="page" or role=tab with aria-selected), matching the visual active styling.
items.hint:
Repro: Open a project. The Outline panel is open and the Outline button in the sidebar rail has class "active". Inspect all four navigation buttons (Outline, Review, References, History): none has aria-pressed, aria-selected or aria-current, and the nav is a plain navigation landmark with no tablist/tab roles or aria-controls. Switch panels with the mouse or keyboard and the accessible state does not change; only the CSS class changes.
Actual: Probe data: [{text:"Outline", active:true, pressed:null, current:null, selected:null}, {text:"Review 1", active:false, pressed:null, current:null, selected:null}, ...]. A screen-reader user cannot tell which panel is displayed.
items.source: explore:keyboard:sidebar panel buttons do not expose which panel is open to assistive technology

items.title: Undo, Redo and the indent buttons are announced as toggle buttons with aria-pressed=false
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected One-shot action buttons (Undo, Redo, indent/outdent) have no aria-pressed; only real toggles carry pressed state.
items.hint:
Repro: On the Home ribbon tab inspect the Undo (Ctrl+Z), Redo (Ctrl+Y), Increase indent (Ctrl+]) and Decrease indent (Ctrl+[) buttons. Each is a one-shot action but carries aria-pressed="false", which makes the accessibility tree expose it as a toggle button in the not-pressed state. Bold, Italic and the list buttons are genuine toggles and use the same attribute legitimately, so the distinction is lost.
Actual: Probe read [{"label":"Undo (Ctrl+Z)","pressed":"false"},{"label":"Redo (Ctrl+Y)","pressed":"false"},{"label":"Increase indent (Ctrl+])","pressed":"false"},{"label":"Decrease indent (Ctrl+[)","pressed":"false"}] even though these are one-shot actions.
items.source: explore:keyboard:undo, redo and the indent buttons are announced as toggle buttons with aria-pressed=false

items.title: Colour palettes never expose the applied text colour
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected The palette exposes the current colour (aria-checked on the active swatch, or an accessible value on the trigger) so a screen-reader user can tell which colour is applied.
items.hint:
Repro: Select some text, go to the Home tab, focus "Text color", press ArrowDown twice (No color then Black) and Enter. The text turns black and focus returns to the editor. Reopen the palette with ArrowDown: none of the ten swatches has aria-checked or aria-selected, and the trigger is still named only "Text color" with no value or aria-valuetext. The applied colour is conveyed only by the CSS colour bar under the icon.
Actual: Probe data after applying Black: trigger {label:"Text color", value:null, expanded:"true"}; every swatch has checked:null and selected:null, including Black.
items.source: explore:keyboard:colour palettes never expose the applied text colour

items.title: The Git panel ignores Escape and is an unnamed complementary region
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected Escape closes the Git panel the same way it closes the Properties panel, and the panel exposes an accessible name for its complementary landmark.
items.hint:
Repro: Open a project, click the View ribbon tab, focus "Git history" and press Enter. The Git panel appears, but focus remains on the Git history button inside the ribbon. Press Escape: the panel is still open and focus is still on the Git history button. The panel is an <aside> with no role, aria-label or aria-labelledby, so it is an unnamed complementary region and its close button is not focused. By contrast, the Properties panel closes on Escape (and returns focus to the Settings button).
Actual: Probe: the Git panel count is 1 before Escape and 1 after; activeElement stays on the "Git history" button; the panel is {tag:"ASIDE", role:null, label:null, labelledby:null}.
items.source: explore:keyboard:the git panel ignores escape and is an unnamed complementary region

items.title: Creating a project from the start screen drops keyboard focus on <body>
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected The keyboard focus follows the screen change into the new editor view (for example the writing surface or the skip link), so a keyboard or screen-reader user is placed in the new screen.
items.hint:
Repro: Load the start screen, focus "New document" with Tab and press Enter. The editor loads, but document.activeElement is <body>; the next Tab press goes to the "Skip to writing surface" link at the top of the new screen. Focus is not placed in the editor or on any heading of the new view.
Actual: After Enter activeElement is BODY; the probe's first Tab after the transition reaches the skip link, starting the whole page tab order again.
items.source: explore:keyboard:creating a project from the start screen drops keyboard focus on <body>

items.title: An image inserted inside a heading is re-imported as two literal paragraphs, destroying the heading and its LaTeX
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (functional): expected An inline image in a heading is represented in the exported source in a way the app's own importer accepts, so Apply source preserves one H2 heading 'Drafting with constraints' containing the image.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the demo project. Click the H2 heading 'Drafting with constraints', press Home, then ArrowRight four times so the caret is after 'Draf'. Click Insert > Image and choose a 120x60 PNG (probe uses icon.png): the picture is inserted inline inside the heading. Click View > LaTeX; the heading exports as one line '\subsection{Draf\includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=1.5em,keepaspectratio]{assets/images/icon.png}% Sentence alt: icon.png', with the rest of the heading ('ting with constraints}') on the next line. Add any edit (the probe appends ' % qa') and click Apply source, then switch back to Visual. The H2 heading is gone; the body now has ordinary paragraphs '\subsection{Draf' and 'ting with constraints}', an inline image, and an empty image. Type one character and read View > LaTeX again: the heading is now '\textbackslash{}subsection\{Draf...'.
Actual: The source round trip deletes the heading: headings become ['H1:Introduction'] only, and the two literal paragraphs '\subsection{Draf' and 'ting with constraints}' are created (the probe also finds a second empty image with path null). Re-exporting the corrupted document produces '\textbackslash{}subsection\{Draf\includegraphics...' and no \subsection command (subsectionCount 0), so the heading is lost from both the visual document and the LaTeX. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario 'image-in-heading-roundtrip'.
items.source: explore:insert-media:an image inserted inside a heading is re-imported as two literal paragraphs, destroying the heading and its latex

items.title: A text-block-tall figure with a caption is drawn across the page boundary and the page count drops when the caption is a
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (visual): expected A figure that no longer fits with its caption is moved to the next page (or the image is reduced by the caption's height) so it is never drawn across the page edge, and adding a caption cannot reduce the page count.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the demo, press Ctrl+End, click Insert > Image and choose a 200x3000 PNG. The image is capped at 931 px (the A4 text height) and pagination moves it whole onto page 2: figure padding-top 448 px, image y=1220..2151, status 3 pages. Click the picture, type 'A tall figure with a caption.' into the Figure caption field and press Tab. The figure's padding-top becomes 0 px and the image moves back to y=772..1703, while the caption is at y=1695..1715; the page boundary line is at y=1123. The status bar changes from 3 pages to 2. (Compiling the exported source with the bundled Tectonic gives a 2-page PDF with the figure whole on page 2.)
Actual: With the caption the figure is no longer snapped: figure padding is 0 px, so the 931 px image spans y=772..1703 and crosses the page edge at y=1123, covering page 1's bottom margin and page 2's top margin (probe flags pageLineCrossesImage and imageOutsideContentBox). The reported page count falls from 3 to 2. The exported PDF is 2 pages with the figure on page 2, so the visual page puts the image on a different page than the PDF. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario 'image-tall-caption'.
items.source: explore:insert-media:a text-block-tall figure with a caption is drawn across the page boundary and the page count drops when the caption is a

items.title: A caption typed on an image inside a table cell is silently dropped from the LaTeX
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (content): expected The caption entered in the offered Figure caption field is preserved in the exported document, or the field is not offered (with an explanation) for a picture in a table cell so a caption cannot be entered and lost.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the demo, press Ctrl+End, press Enter, click Insert > Insert table, click the first cell, then click Insert > Image and choose a 120x60 PNG. Click the picture in the cell: the Image toolbar offers the 'Figure caption' field. Type 'CELL CAPTION' and press Tab. The cell shows the caption under the picture (figcaption 'CELL CAPTION', 1 figure in the td), but View > LaTeX contains only '\includegraphics[width=90.00bp]{assets/images/cell\_caption.png}% Sentence alt: cell_caption.png' inside the tabular: 0 \caption commands and no 'CELL CAPTION' in the tabular.
Actual: The caption is visible in the editor but absent from the generated LaTeX (captionCount 0, captionInTabular false); the image exports as an inline \includegraphics inside the tabular with only the alt-text comment. The caption disappears from the PDF with no warning. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario 'image-caption-in-cell'.
items.source: explore:insert-media:a caption typed on an image inside a table cell is silently dropped from the latex

items.title: The TOC preview drops inline math from a heading, so its entry does not match the printed contents
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (content): expected The contents preview shows the entry as the PDF contents will print it from \section{The \(x^2\) model}, e.g. '2 The x^2 model'.
items.hint:
Repro: Open View > LaTeX and insert '\section{The \(x^2\) model}' before \end{document}; click Apply source. Place the caret at the end of the document and click References > Table of contents.
Actual: The preview entry reads '2 The model' (the formula is missing), while the exported source still contains '\section{The \(x^2\) model}', so the visual contents and the PDF contents disagree. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario 'toc-math-heading'.
items.source: explore:insert-media:the toc preview drops inline math from a heading, so its entry does not match the printed contents

items.title: Removing the bullet from a nested item creates a second paragraph that the LaTeX merges into the parent item
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (content): expected The editor shows 'outer' as a bullet and 'inner one' as a separate paragraph below it, so the LaTeX keeps that paragraph break (a blank line between them) and the PDF prints 'inner one' on its own line inside the item.
items.source: explore:lists:removing the bullet from a nested item creates a second paragraph that the latex merges into the parent item

items.title: List item text that starts with a square bracket is written as an \item optional label and loses its brackets
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (content): expected The brackets are literal document text, so they are protected in the LaTeX (for example '\item {[}draft] note') and the PDF keeps the bullet/number and prints '[draft] note' in full.
items.source: explore:lists:list item text that starts with a square bracket is written as an \item optional label and loses its brackets

items.title: Column resizing stops working and throws a TypeError on a table with a caption
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (functional): expected The first column widens, as it does on a table without a caption, and no error is logged.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new project. Insert tab > Insert table. Click a body cell and type 'Captioned table' in the Table toolbar's Caption field. Hover the border between the first and second columns until the resize cursor appears, then drag it 80px to the right.
Actual: The drag changes no column width (200/200/200 before and after) and the page throws 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'width')' from updateColumnsOnResize -> displayColumnWidth -> handleMouseDown. The table's first child is the CAPTION element ahead of COLGROUP, and the resizing code passes that caption where it expects the column group. Repeating the same drag on the same table before the caption is added widens the first column from 200px to 280px with no error.
items.source: explore:tables:column resizing stops working and throws a typeerror on a table with a caption

items.title: Shift+Enter in a table cell exports a row terminator, so the cell is split into two rows in the PDF
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (content): expected The line break stays inside the cell, using a construct that is valid there, or the editor refuses Shift+Enter in a cell. The tabular keeps that content in one row.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new project. Insert tab > Insert table. Click the top-middle header cell, type 'one', press Shift+Enter, type 'two'. Switch to View > LaTeX and read the tabular.
Actual: The header row is exported as ' & one\\two &  \\'. '\\' is a tabular row terminator, so compiling the exported block with the bundled Tectonic binary prints 'one' and 'two' on separate table rows even though the visual editor shows both lines in one cell.
items.source: explore:tables:shift+enter in a table cell exports a row terminator, so the cell is split into two rows in the pdf

items.title: Turning off the header row of a one-row table leaves its first cell as a header
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (functional): expected All three cells of the remaining row become body cells, the button reports unpressed (aria-pressed='false'), and the LaTeX export gains '% Sentence table header: none'.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new project. Insert tab > Insert table. Click the first cell of the second row and press 'Delete row'. Click the first cell of the (now last) second row and press 'Delete row' again. With one 3-column row left, press 'Header row' once.
Actual: Only the second and third cells become TD. The first cell stays TH with the header background and 650 font weight, and 'Header row' still reports aria-pressed='true'. The re-exported tabular is unchanged, so applying it back turns all three cells into headers again.
items.source: explore:tables:turning off the header row of a one-row table leaves its first cell as a header

items.title: An escaped dollar inside $...$ inline math is read as the closing delimiter and corrupts the formula
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (content): expected One inline math node with latex a\$b rendered as a$b, and the exported body Price \(a\$b\) today.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and open View > LaTeX.
2. Replace the body before \end{document} with:
Price $a\$b$ today.
3. Click Apply source: the toast says 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.'
4. Switch to View > Visual: there is one inline math node whose data-latex is 'a\' (a followed by one backslash), and KaTeX shows the red error 'Unexpected character: \' at position 2.
5. Open View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual: the body now reads Price \(a\\)b\$ today.
The same input using the paren form, Price \(a\$b\) today., imports correctly as one math node with latex a\$b.
Actual: The source is reported as synchronized but split at the escaped dollar: the math node holds only 'a\' and renders a KaTeX parse error, the rest ('b$ today.') becomes paragraph text, and the re-exported body is Price \(a\\)b\$ today.
items.source: explore:math:an escaped dollar inside $...$ inline math is read as the closing delimiter and corrupts the formula

items.title: A line break inside $...$ inline math is accepted but the formula is rewritten as literal dollars
items.why:
Exploratory pass on math (content): expected One inline math node with latex 'a
+ b' rendered as a+b, exported as \(a
+ b\), matching the behaviour of the paren-delimited form.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and open View > LaTeX.
2. Replace the body before \end{document} with:
Costs $a
+ b$ total.
(the line break is inside the dollar delimiters; there is no blank line)
3. Click Apply source: the toast says 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.'
4. Switch to View > Visual: the paragraph reads 'Costs $a + b$ total.' and contains no math node.
5. Open View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual: the body is 'Costs \$a
+ b\$ total.'.
For comparison, the same input with the paren form, Costs \(a
+ b\) total., imports as one math node and round-trips as \(a
+ b\).
Actual: No math node is created. The dollar delimiters are kept as ordinary paragraph text and the export escapes them to \$a ... b\$, so the formula is lost and the exported source contains literal dollar signs instead of math.
items.source: explore:math:a line break inside $...$ inline math is accepted but the formula is rewritten as literal dollars

items.title: Unclosed or paragraph-split $$ display math is reported as synchronized and exported as escaped literal dollars
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (content): expected The source is rejected the way other unclosed math is: applying 'Inline \(x and more.' shows 'Invalid LaTeX: unclosed math delimiter "\(".' and leaves the document unchanged.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and open View > LaTeX.
2. Replace the body before \end{document} with:
Before $$F=ma
(there is no closing $$)
3. Click Apply source: the toast says 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.' (no error).
4. Switch to View > Visual: the paragraph reads 'Before $$F=ma' with no math node.
5. Open View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual: the body is 'Before \$\$F=ma'.
The same happens with '$$
a

b
$$' (a blank line inside the display math): Apply reports synchronized, the visual document has two paragraphs, and the export is '\$\$
a

b
\$\$'.
Actual: Both inputs are accepted and silently rewritten with escaped dollar signs; no error is shown and the display equation is lost.
items.source: explore:math:unclosed or paragraph-split $$ display math is reported as synchronized and exported as escaped literal dollars

items.title: Link addresses with ~, ^, $ or \ are text-escaped, corrupting the PDF hyperlink target
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (content): expected The exported \href target and the PDF link annotation keep the address exactly as typed, so the PDF link opens https://tilde.example.org/~user/page, https://caret.example.org/a^b, https://dollar.example.org/a$b and https://back.example.org/a\b.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. Type `TildeLink word0`, select `word0`, press Ctrl+K, enter `https://tilde.example.org/~user/page` and click Insert. Repeat on new words with `https://caret.example.org/a^b`, `https://dollar.example.org/a$b` and `https://back.example.org/a\b`. Open View > LaTeX and read the four \href arguments. Then compile a minimal article+hyperref document containing the exported tilde \href line with the bundled Tectonic engine (`src-tauri/binaries/tectonic-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -X compile`) and read the PDF link annotations (`qpdf --qdf` and grep `/URI`).
Actual: The visual editor keeps the correct hrefs, but the exporter runs the address through the text escaper: the source reads `\href{https://tilde.example.org/\textasciitilde{}user/page}{word0}`, `\href{https://caret.example.org/a\textasciicircum{}b}{word1}`, `\href{https://dollar.example.org/a\$b}{word2}` and `\href{https://back.example.org/a\textbackslash{}b}{word3}`. Compiled with Tectonic, the PDF link annotations become `https://tilde.example.org/~{}user/page`, `https://caret.example.org/a\TU\textasciicircum {}b`, `https://dollar.example.org/a\protect \TU\textdollar b` and `https://back.example.org/a\TU\textbackslash {}b` — none is the URL the user entered. Addresses with #, %, & and _ do export correctly.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:link addresses with ~, ^, $ or \ are text-escaped, corrupting the pdf hyperlink target

items.title: Add/Edit link silently discards addresses with an unsupported scheme (doi:, javascript:)
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (functional): expected The dialog either rejects the unsupported address with an error (as it does for a key containing braces) or accepts it; in both cases the user must not be left believing the address was applied.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. Type `BadScheme word`, select `word`, press Ctrl+K, enter `javascript:alert(1)` and click Insert. Then type `DoiTarget word`, select `word`, press Ctrl+K, enter `doi:10.1000/xyz123` and click Insert. Finally type `EditScheme word`, select `word`, press Ctrl+K, enter `https://good.example.org/one` and click Insert; click the linked word, press Ctrl+K, replace the address with `javascript:alert(1)` and press Insert.
Actual: For both additions the dialog closes with no alert and no toast, the word stays unlinked (`links: []`, no \href in the source) and the next typed character appends to the paragraph. For the edit, the dialog also closes with no error and the old address is silently kept: `afterEditLinks` is still `https://good.example.org/one` and the source still reads `EditScheme \href{https://good.example.org/one}{word}`. Tiptap's setLink returns false for any scheme outside its allow-list, and the app swallows that result.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:add/edit link silently discards addresses with an unsupported scheme (doi:, javascript:)

items.title: A citation key or cross-reference label containing ~ is accepted but makes the exported LaTeX fail to compile
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (content): expected The dialog refuses characters that the generated command cannot carry (it already refuses braces, parentheses, %, #, backslash and spaces with the message "...or LaTeX special characters") or the exporter escapes/encodes the value so \cite{...} and \ref{...} stay valid.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. Type `TildeCite ` at the end, open References > Insert citation > Enter a key manually, enter `a~b` and click Insert: the dialog accepts it and the visual editor shows `[a~b]`. Repeat with References > Cross-reference, label `fig~one`: it is accepted and shows `ref: fig~one`. Open View > LaTeX. Then compile the exported source (or a minimal article+hyperref document containing that line) with the bundled Tectonic engine.
Actual: Both values are accepted and exported verbatim as `TildeCite \cite{a~b}` and `TildeRef \ref{fig~one}`. Tectonic rejects either line with `! Missing \endcsname inserted.` and produces no PDF, because ~ is an active character inside the \csname lookup. The same dialogs do reject `a{b`/`fig}` with the special-characters error, so the validation list is incomplete.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:a citation key or cross-reference label containing ~ is accepted but makes the exported latex fail to compile

items.title: Inserted citations and cross-references cannot be edited in the visual editor; they can only be deleted and reinserted
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (ux): expected Clicking/double-clicking a citation or cross-reference (or pressing Enter on it) opens a small editor for its key/label, as double-clicking a footnote marker opens the note editor, so a typo can be corrected in place.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. Type `NoEditCite ` and insert a citation with key `sentence2026` via References > Insert citation > Enter a key manually. Click the `[sentence2026]` atom, double-click it, then press Enter, then press Ctrl+K. Repeat with a cross-reference inserted with label `fig:noedit`.
Actual: Clicking selects the atom but no editor opens: `afterDoubleClick` and `afterEnter` report `{open:false}` for both atoms, and the nodes keep their old keys/labels. Ctrl+K opens the unrelated `Add link` dialog instead of editing the citation/reference. In the visual editor the only way to change either is Backspace/Delete and insert a new one (editing the LaTeX source also works, but the visual document then has to be re-synchronised).
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:inserted citations and cross-references cannot be edited in the visual editor; they can only be deleted and reinserted

items.title: Rejecting a tracked paragraph merge after deleting its comment corrupts the text and resurrects the deleted highlight
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected Rejecting the change restores the original two blocks: the 'Introduction' heading followed by the untouched paragraph. The deleted comment stays deleted and its highlight does not come back.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Open http://localhost:1420 in a fresh browser profile and click New document. 2. On the Review tab click Track changes. 3. Select the phrase 'A sentence is not ' at the start of the first body paragraph, choose New comment, enter 'ZZSTRUCTCOMMENT' and submit. 4. Click at the very start of that same paragraph (immediately before 'A sentence...') and press Backspace so the paragraph merges into the 'Introduction' heading above it. 5. Wait 2.5 s until History shows one tracked change. 6. Open Review in the sidebar and click Delete comment on 'ZZSTRUCTCOMMENT'. 7. Open History and click Reject on the tracked change.
Actual: The merge is only partly undone. The heading keeps the body text and the paragraph is restored too, so the text is duplicated: the document starts 'IntroductionA sentence is not ' followed by a blank line and the full 'A sentence is not merely a container for information...' paragraph ('A sentence is not ' occurs twice instead of once). The deleted comment's highlight ('A sentence is not ') also reappears in the document with no thread in the Comments panel, and both the duplicated text and the threadless highlight are still present after a reload. At this point there are 0 inline revision decorations and 0 History cards, so the app reports a clean review state.
items.source: explore:review:rejecting a tracked paragraph merge after deleting its comment corrupts the text and resurrects the deleted highlight

items.title: Ctrl+Z after Accept or Reject silently reverses the review decision outside History
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected Ctrl+Z must not put the review state and the document out of sync: rejected text must not return behind an empty History, and accepted text must not disappear without a tracked change. Undoing a review decision should bring the pending change back into History.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. New document; Review tab > Track changes. 2. At the end of the document type 'ZZREJECTUNDO rejected.' and wait 2.5 s. 3. Open History and click Reject; the words disappear. 4. On the Review tab click 'Tracking on' to turn tracking off. 5. Click into the document and press Ctrl+Z. 6. For the accept case, repeat the same steps with 'ZZACCEPTUNDO accepted.' but click Accept in History.
Actual: After Reject + Ctrl+Z the rejected sentence 'ZZREJECTUNDO rejected.' reappears in the document while History still shows 0 tracked changes; after a reload the rejected words are still there and History is still empty. After Accept + Ctrl+Z the accepted sentence 'ZZACCEPTUNDO accepted.' disappears, History shows 0 changes, and it stays gone after a reload.
items.source: explore:review:ctrl+z after accept or reject silently reverses the review decision outside history

items.title: Track changes has no live feedback: no persistent indicator and no insertion marks while typing
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (ux): expected While tracking is on, a persistent indicator (status bar or tab) shows it on every ribbon tab, and newly typed text is visibly marked as a tracked insertion as it is typed.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. New document; Review tab > Track changes. 2. Wait 4.5 s for the 'Tracked changes is on.' toast to clear, then switch to the View (or Home) tab. 3. Inspect the ribbon, status bar and document, then start a new paragraph and type 'ZZIMMEDIATE with tracking on.' and inspect the text immediately, before 1.8 s have passed.
Actual: Outside the Review tab nothing indicates that tracking is on: the status bar has no tracking text, no visible control has an aria-pressed/title mentioning tracking, and the editor looks completely normal. Immediately after typing there are 0 .sentence-revision-insertion elements; the insertion marks appear only after the 1.8 s revision debounce (they are present after 2.4 s).

items.title: A table taller than a page is never paginated: page rules cut through rows and rows sit in the margins
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (visual): expected Every table row stays inside the 96px top and bottom margins of its page, and each page rule falls in the blank gap between rows, exactly as the 3,600-word paragraph/heading document in `stages.layout` does (0 margin lines and 0 rule crossings).
items.hint:
Repro: Run `node qa/probes/long-document.mjs` and read `stages.longTable`, or reproduce by hand at 1280x800: open http://localhost:1420, click 'New document', press Ctrl+A then Backspace, put a 61-row HTML table on the clipboard (`<table><thead><tr><th>Name</th><th>Value</th><th>Notes</th></tr></thead><tbody>` followed by 60 rows whose cells are `Row N alpha`, `Row N beta content`, `Row N gamma content`) and press Ctrl+V. The status bar reads 663 words / 4 pages and the editor contains one 61-row table, but the page audit of its 183 text line boxes finds 15 lines above a page's 96px top margin, 21 lines below the 96px bottom margin, and 3 line boxes crossing a page rule: on page 3 the box 3368-3383px runs through `Row 56 alpha`, `Row 56 beta content` and `Row 56 gamma content` at the rule at y=3369.
Actual: The pagination pass only adjusts top-level P, H1-H3, UL, OL and BLOCKQUOTE blocks. ProseMirror wraps the table in a DIV, which is skipped, so the whole table is left as one continuous flow: 36 lines end up inside page margins and Row 56 is drawn across the page boundary.

items.title: The status-bar page count follows the pane width: Split reports 26 pages and Document properties 23 for the same 13-page
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (functional): expected Opening Split or Document properties must not change the paper width or pagination of the document; the status bar keeps reporting the document's 13 pages, scaling the sheet to fit the narrower pane if necessary.
items.hint:
Repro: Run `node qa/probes/long-document.mjs` and read `stages.pageCountVsPane`, or reproduce by hand at 1280x800: create a new document, clear it, and paste the probe's 50-heading/3,600-word document. The full visual view reports 13 pages with a 794px-wide, 14,599px-tall sheet. Click the 'Split' button in the status bar: the same document now reports 26 pages, the sheet shrinks to 448px wide and grows to 29,198px tall, and the text rewraps. Click 'Visual': 13 pages again. Open Layout > Document properties: it reports 23 pages with a 488px-wide, 25,829px-tall sheet; close the panel: 13 pages again. No document text or page-setup setting changes in any of these steps.
Actual: The sheet is sized to `min(paper width, available pane width)`, so opening a side pane reflows the text at a narrower measure. The reported page count and sheet height inflate from 13/14,599 to 26/29,198 in Split and 23/25,829 with the inspector open, then return to 13 when the pane closes.

items.title: Zooming out while at the end leaves the whole document above the viewport, and the scroll range extends past the end of
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (visual): expected Changing zoom keeps the reading position/content visible, the scroll range ends at the scaled bottom of the sheet, and the whole page can be reached horizontally when it is wider than the pane.
items.hint:
Repro: Run `node qa/probes/long-document.mjs` and read `stages.zoom`, or reproduce by hand at 1280x800 with the 50-heading/3,600-word document: click in the page and press Ctrl+End (the editor scrolls to scrollTop 13,558 of a 14,082 maximum). Click the status-bar 'Zoom out' button three times to reach 70%: scrollTop remains 13,558, but the sheet's bottom edge moves from +1,071px to -3,309px relative to the editor viewport, so the entire page and its last block (at -3,707px) are above the visible area. Wheel to the maximum (14,082): the sheet bottom is -3,833px and the editor is completely blank. At 150% the sheet spans -120px to 1,071px in the 950px-wide viewport while the horizontal scroll range is only 121px, so the left 120px of the page cannot be brought into view.
Actual: The CSS transform scales the sheet but leaves scroll geometry at the 100% layout: zooming out from the end leaves the viewport below the sheet (with 3,833px of blank scroll past it), and at 150% the left edge of the page is clipped with only 121px of horizontal scroll available to recover it.
items.source: explore:long-document:zooming out while at the end leaves the whole document above the viewport, and the scroll range extends past the end of

items.title: A failed Git-author localStorage write blanks the entire app
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (functional): expected The Git author is an auxiliary setting; if its localStorage write fails, the app should report or ignore the failure and keep the editor and the saved document on screen. A blocked write must not unmount the app.
items.hint:
Repro: 1) Open http://localhost:1420 with a fresh profile, click 'New document' and wait for the top bar to read 'Saved locally'. 2) In the devtools console run: const orig = Storage.prototype.setItem; Storage.prototype.setItem = function (key, value) { if (key === 'sentence.gitAuthor') throw new DOMException('The quota has been exceeded.', 'QuotaExceededError'); return orig.call(this, key, value); }; (this simulates a full or blocked localStorage for that one key). 3) Click 'Settings' and type a name into the 'Name' field under Git author. The app instantly goes blank. 4) Reload once: the override is gone, so the editor returns. 5) Re-apply the same override before the document loads (Playwright page.addInitScript, or CDP Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument) and reload: the app is blank again on boot. Probe evidence: qa/probes/persistence.mjs phase 'git-author-storage-crash' (afterEdit bodyLength 0, editor false; afterLoad bodyLength 0, editor false; pageErrors 'The quota has been exceeded.' twice at startup).
Actual: document.body.innerText has length 0, with no editor, start screen or inspector. The console records 'pageerror: The quota has been exceeded.' (twice on startup because the effect runs in StrictMode). The useEffect at src/App.tsx:697 calls localStorage.setItem('sentence.gitAuthor', ...) with no try/catch (unlike saveBrowserWorkspace and rememberProject) and there is no error boundary, so React unmounts the whole tree. The document is still in localStorage but is unreachable through the UI.
items.source: explore:persistence:a failed git-author localstorage write blanks the entire app

items.title: A source draft is deleted before the workspace write succeeds, so a failed save loses the edit on reload
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (functional): expected The recovery copy in sentence.workspace.draft should stay until the workspace snapshot has actually been written, so reloading after a failed save restores the draft (the app already restores drafts on boot and shows 'Restored your unapplied LaTeX draft').
items.hint:
Repro: 1) Open http://localhost:1420, click 'New document' and wait for 'Saved locally'. 2) In the devtools console run: const orig = Storage.prototype.setItem; Storage.prototype.setItem = function (key, value) { if (key === 'sentence.workspace') throw new DOMException('The quota has been exceeded.', 'QuotaExceededError'); return orig.call(this, key, value); }; . 3) Switch to Source, insert a valid sentence such as 'Victim paragraph.' before \end{document}, and wait 1.8 s. The autosave parses the draft and the top bar shows 'Editing' with 'Retry save: The quota has been exceeded.' At this point localStorage['sentence.workspace.draft'] is gone (it was present immediately after the edit). 4) Reload without restoring Storage.prototype.setItem, then read the visual editor and View > LaTeX. Probe evidence: qa/probes/persistence.mjs phase 'draft-lost-on-failed-workspace-write' (draftExistsRightAfterEdit true; after the failed autosave draftExists false and the workspace has no victim text; after reload draftExists false, editor and LaTeX have no victim text, indicator 'Saved locally').
Actual: The draft key is removed at src/App.tsx:932 (saveBrowserDraft(null)) before persistBrowser runs at line 964. When the workspace write then throws, the only recoverable copy of the source edit is already gone. After the reload the edit is absent from the visual editor, the LaTeX textarea and localStorage, and the reloaded app reports 'Saved locally' with a check icon.
items.source: explore:persistence:a source draft is deleted before the workspace write succeeds, so a failed save loses the edit on reload

items.title: The document is reported unsaved when only the recent-projects list write fails
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (ux): expected Once the workspace snapshot has been written, the document should be reported as saved. A failed write of the auxiliary recent-projects list should be reported separately or ignored, not turn the document's saved state into an error.
items.hint:
Repro: 1) Open http://localhost:1420, click 'New document' and wait for 'Saved locally'. 2) In the devtools console run: const orig = Storage.prototype.setItem; Storage.prototype.setItem = function (key, value) { if (key === 'sentence.recent') throw new DOMException('The quota has been exceeded.', 'QuotaExceededError'); return orig.call(this, key, value); }; . 3) Type a unique marker at the end of the document and wait 1.6 s. 4) Read the top bar and localStorage['sentence.workspace'], then reload. Probe evidence: qa/probes/persistence.mjs phase 'recent-write-failure' (storedHasMarker true, editorHasMarker true, indicator label 'Editing', retry 'Retry save: The quota has been exceeded.'; after reload the marker is still present and the label is 'Saved locally').
Actual: persist() treats rememberProject's failure as a save error: saveState becomes 'error' and dirty stays true, so the heading renders 'Editing' with the Retry save control even though localStorage['sentence.workspace'] already contains the typed text and a reload restores it. Clicking Retry cannot clear the state while sentence.recent remains unwritable.
items.source: explore:persistence:the document is reported unsaved when only the recent-projects list write fails

items.title: Add link from the ribbon opens the dialog with focus still in the document, so typing edits the manuscript behind the mo
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (functional): expected The dialog's Address field receives focus when the dialog opens, exactly as it does when the same dialog is opened with Ctrl+K from the already-focused editor, so typed characters go into the address and never into the manuscript.
items.hint:
Repro: Open a project with body text and put the caret inside a word (Ctrl+Home, then ArrowRight). Go to the Home ribbon tab, focus "Add link", press Enter. The "Add link" dialog opens, but document.activeElement remains the ProseMirror "Document editor" behind it (modal count 1, focus inEditor true, sampled 0-1000 ms). Type "example.com": the dialog's Address field stays empty and the word under the caret in the manuscript is replaced with "example.com". Press Tab once and focus jumps into the dialog (on its Close button); Escape closes it and removes the temporary link, but the typed text remains in the document.
Actual: Probe data: dialog open (modal 1, backdrop 1), activeElement = DIV .tiptap.ProseMirror.sentence-editor with aria-label "Document editor", inEditor true, inDialog false. After typing, the modal input value is "" and the document text changes from "alpha beta gamma delta QRS..." to "example.com beta gamma delta QRS..." (the linked word is replaced; inDocument true, and the text is still there after Escape closes the dialog). One Tab moves focus to the dialog Close button, so the modal trap can recover, but the first keystrokes have already modified the document.
items.source: explore:keyboard:add link from the ribbon opens the dialog with focus still in the document, so typing edits the manuscript behind the mo

items.title: Paragraph spacing popover takes no focus on open and drops focus on <body> when Escape closes it
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected Focus moves into the popover when it opens (as with the equation and link dialogs), and Escape returns focus to the Paragraph spacing button (as the Text color palette does), so a keyboard user can type the value and then keep navigating from the ribbon.
items.hint:
Repro: Open a project, go to Home, focus "Paragraph spacing" and press Enter. The popover opens, but focus stays on the ribbon button; the next Tab goes to "Add link" and the Before/After inputs are only reached after tabbing through the rest of the page (the popover is portalled to the end of <body>: 17 Tab presses in the probe; the count grows with sidebar content). Put focus in the Before field and press Escape: the popover closes and document.activeElement becomes BODY instead of the Paragraph spacing button.
Actual: Probe data: after Enter, focus is BUTTON.ribbon-icon-button "Paragraph spacing" with aria-expanded true; after one Tab focus is the "Add link" button; tabsToPanel = 17. After focusing the Before input and pressing Escape the panel count is 0 and activeElement is BODY.

items.title: Split view renders two find bars and always returns find focus to the visual pane
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected A single find bar for the document (one search landmark and one Find field), and Escape returns focus to the pane the find was opened from, so a keyboard user continues exactly where they were.
items.hint:
Repro: Open a project, press Ctrl+Alt+3 for Split, then press Ctrl+F from the visual page. Two identical find bars appear, one in each pane: the probe counts 2 .find-bar elements, 2 role=search landmarks and 2 inputs named "Find"; focus lands in the source pane's copy (barParent source-column). After typing a query and pressing Escape, focus goes to the visual editor. Repeat with the caret in the LaTeX textarea: Ctrl+F focuses the source-pane bar, but Escape still returns focus to the visual editor instead of the textarea.
Actual: Probe data in Split mode: find 2, findInputs 2, searchLandmarks 2; the Ctrl+F ref points at the source-column bar even when the caret was in the visual pane; Escape from a find opened over the LaTeX textarea sets activeElement to DIV .sentence-editor (visual) rather than the LaTeX textarea.
items.source: explore:keyboard:split view renders two find bars and always returns find focus to the visual pane

items.title: Colour palettes never expose the applied text colour to assistive technology
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected The palette exposes the current colour, for example aria-checked on the active swatch or an accessible value on the trigger, so a screen-reader user can tell which colour is applied.
items.hint:
Repro: Select some text, go to Home, focus "Text color", press ArrowDown twice (No color, then Black) and Enter. The selection turns black and focus returns to the editor. Reopen the palette with ArrowDown: inspect the trigger and the swatches. The trigger is still named only "Text color" with no aria-valuetext/value, and none of the ten swatches has aria-checked or aria-selected, including Black. The colour is shown only by the CSS colour bar under the icon.
Actual: Probe data after applying Black: trigger {label: "Text color", value: "Text color", expanded: "true"}; all swatches including Black have checked:null and selected:null.
items.source: explore:keyboard:colour palettes never expose the applied text colour to assistive technology

items.title: Zooming out while at the end leaves the whole document above the viewport, and the scroll range extends past the end of
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (visual): expected Changing zoom keeps the reading position/content visible, the scroll range ends at the scaled bottom of the sheet, and the whole page can be reached horizontally when it is wider than the pane.
items.hint:
Repro: Run `node qa/probes/long-document.mjs` and read `stages.zoom`, or reproduce by hand at 1280x800 with the 50-heading/3,600-word document: click in the page and press Ctrl+End (the editor scrolls to scrollTop 13,558 of a 14,082 maximum). Click the status-bar 'Zoom out' button three times to reach 70%: scrollTop remains 13,558, but the sheet's bottom edge moves from +1,071px to -3,309px relative to the editor viewport, so the entire page and its last block (at -3,707px) are above the visible area. Wheel to the maximum (14,082): the sheet bottom is -3,833px and the editor is completely blank. At 150% the sheet spans -120px to 1,071px in the 950px-wide viewport while the horizontal scroll range is only 121px, so the left 120px of the page cannot be brought into view.
Actual: The CSS transform scales the sheet but leaves scroll geometry at the 100% layout: zooming out from the end leaves the viewport below the sheet (with 3,833px of blank scroll past it), and at 150% the left edge of the page is clipped with only 121px of horizontal scroll available to recover it.
items.source: explore:long-document:zooming out while at the end leaves the whole document above the viewport, and the scroll range extends past the end of

items.title: Page break or table of contents inserted at the end of a blockquote is nested in the quote and becomes literal text afte
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (functional): expected Page furniture placed at the end of a blockquote is inserted after the quote, like it already is when the caret is in the middle of the quote; it renders at the page boundary, exports outside \begin{quote}, and round-trips through Apply source without turning \newpage or \tableofcontents into text.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the demo project. Click the text of the blockquote ('Clarity arrives when the mechanics disappear...'), press End, then click Insert > Page break. The page-break band is drawn inside the quote at y=1621..1685 on a 1123 px page: its centre is 530 px away from the page edge, the quote's own text is pushed to y=1220 (page 2), and the following paragraph is at y=1824, so the break does not separate anything (probe: break node parent BLOCKQUOTE, band 1621..1685, quote first child 1220..1249). View > LaTeX shows the command inside the environment: ' egin{quote} ... 
ewpage \end{quote}'. Make any source edit and click Apply source, then View > Visual: there are 0 [data-page-break] nodes and the quote now shows the literal text '
ewpage'. Type one character in the quote and read View > LaTeX again: the block is '\	extbackslash{}newpageX', so the command is now escaped prose. Repeating the repro with References > Table of contents instead of Page break gives the same result: the TOC is nested in the quote and, after Apply source, becomes the literal text '	ableofcontents' (0 [data-toc] nodes), re-exported as '	extbackslash{}tableofcontents'.
Actual: The page break/TOC node is a child of BLOCKQUOTE. The page-break band sits mid-page (band 1621..1685, page edge 1123), the quote text is moved to page 2, and the exported source puts the command inside  egin{quote}. Apply source then drops the block atom: the visual document contains 0 page-break/0 TOC nodes and shows '
ewpage' or '	ableofcontents' as ordinary quote text (probe quoteText after sync: '... remains. \newpage'), and re-exporting escapes it to '	extbackslash{}newpage'. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenarios 'quote-page-break-roundtrip' and 'quote-toc-roundtrip'.
items.source: explore:insert-media:page break or table of contents inserted at the end of a blockquote is nested in the quote and becomes literal text afte

items.title: The table-of-contents preview numbers sections from 1 in report/book documents while the compiled PDF prints 0.1
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (content): expected The contents preview uses the numbering the chosen document class prints (0.1, 0.1.1 for report/book with no chapters) and reflects that \tableofcontents starts a new page, so the visual contents match the compiled PDF.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the demo project. On the Layout tab set Document class to Report. Press Ctrl+End and click References > Table of contents. The preview entries read '1 Introduction' and '1.1 Drafting with constraints', and the status bar says '1 page'. View > LaTeX contains '\documentclass[11pt,a4paper]{report}', '\section{Introduction}', '\subsection{Drafting with constraints}' and '\tableofcontents'. Compile that exported source with the bundled engine, e.g. 'src-tauri/binaries/tectonic-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --untrusted main.tex'; pdftotext shows the contents as '0.1 Introduction' and '0.1.1 Drafting with constraints', and pdfinfo reports 4 pages (the report class starts a title page and a contents page, which the visual page and status bar do not show).
Actual: The preview numbers the same headings as 1 and 1.1 and keeps the TOC block on the single visual page; the exact exported source, compiled with Tectonic, prints 0.1 and 0.1.1 and is 4 pages (probe entries: ['1 Introduction', '1.1 Drafting with constraints'], documentClass report, tocCount 1, status '1 page'). Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario 'toc-report-class'.
items.source: explore:insert-media:the table-of-contents preview numbers sections from 1 in report/book documents while the compiled pdf prints 0.1

items.title: A wide image inserted into a table cell exports at the full text width, so the compiled table overflows the page margin
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (visual): expected An image placed in a table cell is sized to that cell (as it is displayed in the editor) or the source uses a width that keeps the tabular inside the text block, so the compiled PDF matches the visual table width.
items.hint:
Repro: In the demo project press Ctrl+End, click Insert > Insert table, click the first cell, then Insert > Image and choose a 2400x600 PNG. The picture renders 438x111 px inside the 459 px cell and the table stays 600 px wide, the text width. View > LaTeX exports '\includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=\textheight,keepaspectratio]{assets/images/wide-cell.png}' inside the '\begin{tabular}{lll}' block. Copy that asset to assets/images/wide-cell.png and compile the exported source with the bundled Tectonic; the log reports 'Overfull \hbox (35.96829pt too wide) in paragraph at lines 62--70', so the table extends 35.97 pt beyond the text block.
Actual: The cell is an 'l' column, so 'width=\linewidth' resolves to the full A4 text width, not the cell width. The table is centred with column padding and becomes 35.97 pt wider than the text block in the compiled PDF, while the visual page shows the 438 px image fitting a 459 px cell inside the 600 px table. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario 'wide-image-in-table-cell'.
items.source: explore:insert-media:a wide image inserted into a table cell exports at the full text width, so the compiled table overflows the page margin

items.title: An unreadable image file is inserted as a broken figure with no warning and an unsized \includegraphics
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (functional): expected A file that cannot be decoded is rejected with a visible error, or the editor at least warns that the image could not be read, instead of adding a broken figure and a LaTeX reference with no usable graphic.
items.hint:
Repro: In the demo project press Ctrl+End and click Insert > Image. Choose a file named not-an-image.png whose bytes are plain text ('this is not a PNG file') rather than a PNG. The editor inserts one figure whose img has naturalWidth/naturalHeight 0x0 and displays only the alt text; no toast appears. View > LaTeX contains '\includegraphics{assets/images/not-an-image.png}% Sentence alt: not-an-image.png' with no width or height.
Actual: The picker completes without an error: the visual document gains 1 figure with an undecodable data URL (natural 0x0), toast is null, and the exported source references assets/images/not-an-image.png with no size, which cannot produce the intended picture in the PDF. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario 'corrupt-image-file'.
items.source: explore:insert-media:an unreadable image file is inserted as a broken figure with no warning and an unsized \includegraphics

items.title: Shift+Tab on a nested item in the middle of a sublist reparents every following sibling under it
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (functional): expected Only 'child two' moves out to 'outer' level; 'child one' and 'child three' stay in the same sublist under 'outer', so the document reads: outer, child one, child three nested under outer, child two beside outer. Outdenting 'child one' should likewise leave child two and three under outer.
items.source: explore:lists:shift+tab on a nested item in the middle of a sublist reparents every following sibling under it

items.title: Turning bullets off for a selection that spans a parent and its nested child leaves the selected child bulleted
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (functional): expected Both selected bullet items lose their bullet and become plain paragraphs, as they do when a flat bullet list is fully selected and the same button is clicked.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new document. Type 'outer text', click Home > Bulleted list, press Enter, type 'child text', press Tab. Click at the end of 'outer text', press Home, then Shift+ArrowDown and Shift+End so the selection covers both 'outer text' and 'child text' (the Bulleted list button is shown pressed). Click Home > Bulleted list. Open Source, click Refresh from visual and read the LaTeX. Actual: 'outer text' becomes a paragraph but the selected 'child text' keeps its bullet and is promoted to a top-level list: DOM '

outer text

  • child text

', LaTeX 'outer text egin{itemize} \item child text \end{itemize}'. A selected bullet item is left untouched even though the Bulleted list button reported itself pressed.

items.title: The bullet button stays pressed on a paragraph that has no bullet, and clicking it removes the parent item's bullet
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (ux): expected With the caret on the visually unbulleted paragraph 'inner one', the Bulleted list button is not pressed, and clicking it bullets that paragraph (or does nothing) instead of changing a different item.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new document. Type 'outer', click Home > Bulleted list, press Enter, type 'inner one', press Tab, press Enter, type 'inner two'. Click at the end of 'inner one' and click Home > Bulleted list once ('inner one' becomes a plain paragraph). Read the Bulleted list button's aria-pressed value, then click Home > Bulleted list again.
Actual: The button still reports aria-pressed='true' on the unbulleted paragraph and Numbered list reports 'false'. The second click removes the bullet from 'outer' instead: both 'outer' and 'inner one' become plain paragraphs and 'inner two' is promoted to a top-level list. LaTeX after the second click is 'outer

inner one

 egin{itemize}
\item inner two
\end{itemize}'. There is no way to re-bullet 'inner one' through this button; clicking it again only strips more list structure.
items.source: explore:lists:the bullet button stays pressed on a paragraph that has no bullet, and clicking it removes the parent item's bullet

items.title: A numbered list typed as '0. ' shows 0 in the editor but exports an enumerate starting at 1
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (content): expected The editor and the exported LaTeX agree on the numbering: either the LaTeX preserves the visible 0 start (for example with \setcounter{enumi}{-1}) or the editor starts the list at 1.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a new document and type '0. zero item' (the ordered-list input rule creates the list). Open Source, click Refresh from visual and read the LaTeX textarea.
Actual: The editor DOM is '<ol start="0">' with list-style decimal, so the item is shown as 0, but the LaTeX is '\begin{enumerate}\n\item zero item\n\end{enumerate}' with no \setcounter, so the PDF numbers the same item 1.
items.source: explore:lists:a numbered list typed as '0. ' shows 0 in the editor but exports an enumerate starting at 1

items.title: Zooming out while at the end leaves the whole document above the viewport, and the scroll range extends past the end of
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (visual): expected Changing zoom keeps the reading position/content visible, the scroll range ends at the scaled bottom of the sheet, and the whole page can be reached horizontally when it is wider than the pane.
items.hint:
Repro: Run `node qa/probes/long-document.mjs` and read `stages.zoom`, or reproduce by hand at 1280x800 with the 50-heading/3,600-word document: click in the page and press Ctrl+End (the editor scrolls to scrollTop 13,558 of a 14,082 maximum). Click the status-bar 'Zoom out' button three times to reach 70%: scrollTop remains 13,558, but the sheet's bottom edge moves from +1,071px to -3,309px relative to the editor viewport, so the entire page and its last block (at -3,707px) are above the visible area. Wheel to the maximum (14,082): the sheet bottom is -3,833px and the editor is completely blank. At 150% the sheet spans -120px to 1,071px in the 950px-wide viewport while the horizontal scroll range is only 121px, so the left 120px of the page cannot be brought into view.
Actual: The CSS transform scales the sheet but leaves scroll geometry at the 100% layout: zooming out from the end leaves the viewport below the sheet (with 3,833px of blank scroll past it), and at 150% the left edge of the page is clipped with only 121px of horizontal scroll available to recover it.

items.title: Typing while an equation is selected silently replaces the equation
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (functional): expected The typed text continues after the equation (or is placed in a new paragraph after it); the equation stays in the document and in the exported LaTeX.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and type 'Speed ' in the editor.
2. Open Insert > Equation block, enter E=mc^2 and click Insert.
3. Without clicking anywhere else, type the word 'next'.
4. Open View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual.
The same happens to an existing equation: click it to open the editor, press Escape to dismiss it, then type any character (e.g. inline 'Before [x+1] after' -> Escape -> 'Z').
Actual: The equation is replaced by the typed text. After step 3 the DOM has zero [data-math-block] nodes and two paragraphs 'Speed' and 'next'; the exported body is 'Speed\n\nnext' with no equation. In the Escape case the source becomes 'Before Z after' and the inline math node is gone.
items.source: explore:math:typing while an equation is selected silently replaces the equation

items.title: A bare percent sign in inline math is accepted, but the exported formula never closes because % comments out the delimit
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (content): expected The dialog reports the unescaped % as invalid and blocks Insert (it already rejects the related input \text{50%}), or the export writes \% so the formula compiles.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and type 'Rate '.
2. Open Insert > Inline equation.
3. Enter 100% in the LaTeX source: the preview shows only '100', there is no error message and Insert is enabled.
4. Click Insert, go to View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual: the body reads 'Rate \(100%\)'.
5. Compile that source with the bundled Tectonic.
Actual: The preview silently drops everything from % onward and Insert is allowed. The exported inline math is 'Rate \(100%\)'; the % starts a TeX comment that swallows the closing \), so Tectonic stops with '! Missing $ inserted.' and writes no PDF.
items.source: explore:math:a bare percent sign in inline math is accepted, but the exported formula never closes because % comments out the delimit

items.title: The math preview accepts \textcolor, but the exported preamble omits xcolor so the PDF compile fails
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (content): expected The preamble includes \usepackage{xcolor} when a math formula uses colour commands, or the dialog rejects the command and explains that the package is unavailable.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and type 'Colour '.
2. Open Insert > Inline equation and enter \textcolor{red}{x}: the preview renders a red x with no error and Insert is enabled.
3. Click Insert, then View > LaTeX: the body contains \(\textcolor{red}{x}\) and the preamble lists fontspec, amsmath/amssymb, graphicx, booktabs, ulem, microtype, hyperref, fancyhdr and geometry, but no xcolor.
4. Compile the exported source with the bundled Tectonic.
Actual: Tectonic stops with '! Undefined control sequence.' at \(\textcolor{red}{x}\) and writes no pages, even though the dialog preview showed the formula as valid.
items.source: explore:math:the math preview accepts \textcolor, but the exported preamble omits xcolor so the pdf compile fails

items.title: Valid empty inline math \(\) is imported as literal text and re-exported as \textbackslash{}(\textbackslash{})
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (content): expected The valid empty formula becomes an (empty) inline math node, the way an empty $$ $$ block becomes a math block, or at minimum the source is preserved verbatim.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project, open View > LaTeX and replace the body before \end{document} with: Empty \(\) math.
2. Click Apply source: the toast says 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.'
3. Switch to View > Visual: the paragraph reads literally 'Empty \(\) math.' and contains no math node.
4. Back in View > LaTeX, click Refresh from visual: the body is 'Empty \textbackslash{}(\textbackslash{}) math.'
Actual: No math node is created; the delimiters remain as paragraph text and the next export escapes both backslashes to \textbackslash{}, so the math is gone and the source has changed. The same 'Empty \(\) math.' document compiles without error in Tectonic before the round trip.
items.source: explore:math:valid empty inline math \(\) is imported as literal text and re-exported as \textbackslash{}(\textbackslash{})

items.title: A footnote inserted inside a heading exports as an unprotected \footnote and the document no longer compiles
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (content): expected A footnote in a section title is written with \protect (or moved out of the moving argument), so the exported document still compiles to a PDF.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. Type "Heading footnote" in a new paragraph, click Home > Apply heading, click at the end of the heading text, then Insert > Footnote, enter "Heading note" and click Insert. Open View > LaTeX: the heading is exported as \section{Heading footnote\footnote{Heading note}}. The probe saves this export to qa/probes/links-cites-footnotes-heading.tex and compiles it with the bundled engine: src-tauri/binaries/tectonic-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -X compile qa/probes/links-cites-footnotes-heading.tex --outdir qa/probes/links-cites-footnotes-heading-out.
Actual: Tectonic exits 1 with "! Argument of \@sect has an extra }." at the \section line, reports "No pages of output" and writes no PDF (the probe records compile.exitCode 1, pdf false). A citation (\cite) or cross-reference (\ref) inserted in the same heading compiles normally; the failure is specific to \footnote.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:a footnote inserted inside a heading exports as an unprotected \footnote and the document no longer compiles

items.title: Inserting a footnote, citation or cross-reference over a text selection deletes the selected text
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (functional): expected The selected word is kept and the footnote marker, citation or cross-reference is inserted after it; adding a link to selected text already preserves that text in this app.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project and type "SelectNote alpha beta". Select "beta" (Ctrl+Shift+ArrowLeft), open Insert > Footnote, enter "Selected note" and click Insert. Repeat with "SelectCite alpha beta", References > Insert citation > Enter a key manually, key sentence2026; and with "SelectRef alpha beta", References > Cross-reference, label fig:sel.
Actual: The selected word is deleted. The probe's atomInsertOverSelection scenario records the paragraphs as "SelectNote alpha 1", "SelectCite alpha [sentence2026]" and "SelectRef alpha ref: fig:sel"; "beta" is gone from the document and from the exported LaTeX, with no warning.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:inserting a footnote, citation or cross-reference over a text selection deletes the selected text

items.title: Cancelling a citation, footnote or cross-reference edit immediately after it opens drops the caret to the start of the d
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (functional): expected The caret returns to the edited atom, so "Z" is inserted next to its marker and continues the sentence.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project and leave the first paragraph empty; press Enter and type "QuickNote ", then insert a footnote with text "Note". Double-click the new footnote marker, then press Escape as soon as the Edit footnote dialog appears (the probe presses it immediately, without waiting for the dialog's focus hand-off; the failure window is roughly the first 250 ms). Wait for the dialog to close and type "Z". The probe's atomEditQuickEscape scenario repeats this for a footnote, a citation and a cross-reference.
Actual: The atom's selection is lost. The probe's paragraphs after typing become ["Z", "QuickNote 1"], ["Z", "QuickCite [sentence2026]"] and ["Z", "QuickRef ref: fig:quick"]: the character is inserted at the very start of the document instead of beside the marker. Pressing Escape after the dialog has been open for about 300 ms preserves the caret, so the failure is the fast-cancel path.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:cancelling a citation, footnote or cross-reference edit immediately after it opens drops the caret to the start of the d

items.title: The References panel's Cite and manual-citation controls are enabled in Source view but silently insert nothing
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (functional): expected The citation is inserted at the last visual caret, or the panel's citation controls are disabled and explain that the visual document is not available while the source pane is active.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project and type "SourceCite ". Open References > Insert citation to show the References panel. Switch to View > LaTeX (the panel remains visible). Click the Cite button for sentence2026, then click "Enter a key manually", enter ghost2026 and click Insert. Switch back to Visual.
Actual: Cite and "Enter a key manually" are both enabled, and the manual dialog accepts the key and closes, but the source contains no \cite, the visual document still has no citation, and no toast or alert appears. The probe records citationsInSourceAfterCite [], citationsInSourceAfterManual [], toastBefore/toastAfterCite/toastAfterManual all null, and afterVisual with no citations. The same controls insert normally in Visual and Split views.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:the references panel's cite and manual-citation controls are enabled in source view but silently insert nothing

items.title: A footnote imported with \textit or \textbf formatting is turned into literal escaped commands after the next visual edi
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (content): expected The imported footnote keeps its formatting, or at least the source commands remain intact; re-exporting must not turn them into visible command text.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project. Open View > LaTeX and insert before \end{document}: "Formatted note \footnote{See \textit{Smith} and \textbf{Jones}.} end." Click Apply source and return to Visual. The footnote's data-text reads "See \textit{Smith} and \textbf{Jones}." Type any character at the end of the document, then open View > LaTeX.
Actual: The re-exported line is "Formatted note \footnote{See \textbackslash{}textit\{Smith\} and \textbackslash{}textbf\{Jones\}.} end." The PDF will print the command names as literal text. The same \textit/\textbf input in a normal paragraph imports as italic/bold marks and re-exports unchanged, so the loss is specific to the footnote's plain-text attribute.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:a footnote imported with \textit or \textbf formatting is turned into literal escaped commands after the next visual edi

items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (visual): expected Changing zoom keeps the reading position/content visible, the scroll range ends at the scaled bottom of the sheet, and the whole page can be reached horizontally when it is wider than the pane.
items.hint:
Repro: Run `node qa/probes/long-document.mjs` and read `stages.zoom`, or reproduce by hand at 1280x800 with the 50-heading/3,600-word document: click in the page and press Ctrl+End (the editor scrolls to scrollTop 13,558 of a 14,082 maximum). Click the status-bar 'Zoom out' button three times to reach 70%: scrollTop remains 13,558, but the sheet's bottom edge moves from +1,071px to -3,309px relative to the editor viewport, so the entire page and its last block (at -3,707px) are above the visible area. Wheel to the maximum (14,082): the sheet bottom is -3,833px and the editor is completely blank. At 150% the sheet spans -120px to 1,071px in the 950px-wide viewport while the horizontal scroll range is only 121px, so the left 120px of the page cannot be brought into view.
Actual: The CSS transform scales the sheet but leaves scroll geometry at the 100% layout: zooming out from the end leaves the viewport below the sheet (with 3,833px of blank scroll past it), and at 150% the left edge of the page is clipped with only 121px of horizontal scroll available to recover it.
