items.title: Editing a citation key or an equation with Track changes on is never recorded in History
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected Each atom edit changes the document and the exported LaTeX, so History should list a pending tracked change for the citation-key edit and another for the equation edit (with before/after values and Accept/Reject buttons), just as it does for text edits.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Open http://localhost:1420, create a project, and put the caret at the end of the last paragraph. 2. With tracking off, insert a citation (References tab > Insert citation > Enter a key manually > sentence2026 > Insert) and an inline equation (Insert tab > Inline equation > x^2 > Insert). 3. Open the Review tab and click Track changes. 4. Double-click the [sentence2026] citation, change the key to otherKey2026, click Update and wait 2 s. 5. Click the rendered x^2 equation, change it to y^3, click Update and wait 2 s. 6. Open History in the sidebar.
Actual: History stays at 0 with the empty-state text after both edits: no revision card exists for either change. The document and the LaTeX already show \cite{otherKey2026} and \(y^3\). Both edits therefore bypass review entirely, so they cannot be rejected or even seen.
items.source: explore:review:editing a citation key or an equation with track changes on is never recorded in history

items.title: Rejecting a tracked deletion of commented text permanently drops the comment highlight and leaves a false 'text was dele
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected Rejecting the deletion restores the commented phrase together with its comment highlight, and the thread is anchored again.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Open a new document. 2. Select the leading phrase 'A sentence is not ' of the first body paragraph, click Review > New comment, enter 'PROBEREJECTCOMMENT' and submit. 3. On the Review tab click Track changes. 4. Select the same phrase again and press Backspace. 5. Wait about 2 s until the deleted phrase is struck through and History shows one tracked change. 6. Open History and click Reject on that change. 7. Inspect the Review panel and the paragraph, then reload the page.
Actual: The phrase is restored but the comment stays in the detached state with the note 'The text this comment was attached to was deleted, so it has no highlight in the document.' There is no highlight on the restored phrase, the thread is still detached after a reload, and there is no UI to reattach it. The warning is false because the text exists again.
items.source: explore:review:rejecting a tracked deletion of commented text permanently drops the comment highlight and leaves a false 'text was dele

items.title: Rejecting a tracked change while a newer tracked edit is still uncommitted silently folds that edit into the review base
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (functional): expected Rejecting AAA removes it from the document, while BBB remains a pending tracked change that can still be accepted or rejected on its own.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Open a new document, put the caret at the end, press Enter and type 'BASE' with tracking off. 2. Review tab > Track changes, then type 'AAA' at the end and wait about 2.5 s so History shows one tracked change. 3. Type 'BBB' at the same position and immediately (inside the roughly 1.8 s revision debounce) click Reject on the AAA card. 4. Wait 2.5 s, then type 'CCC' at the end and wait for History to settle.
Actual: The document becomes 'BASEBBB' but History shows 0 tracked changes, so BBB is no longer reviewable. The next tracked edit 'CCC' produces one card whose before preview already contains 'BASEBBB' and whose after preview is 'BASEBBBCCC', proving BBB was absorbed into the revision baseline without ever appearing in History.
items.source: explore:review:rejecting a tracked change while a newer tracked edit is still uncommitted silently folds that edit into the review base

items.title: Tracked insertions of a citation or an equation show a History card with identical before/after text and no mark in the
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (ux): expected Each History card identifies the inserted atom (for example the citation key or the equation source) in its before/after previews, and the new citation/equation is marked as an insertion in the document.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Open a new document and put the caret at the end of the last paragraph. 2. Review tab > Track changes. 3. References tab > Insert citation > Enter a key manually > sentence2026 > Insert; wait about 2.5 s and open History. 4. Back in the document, Insert tab > Inline equation > x^2 > Insert; wait about 2.5 s and open History again.
Actual: Both cards show exactly the same text on both sides (e.g. 'mpactly: meaning = structure + language.' for before and after), and the document contains no .sentence-revision-insertion mark for either atom. The citation and equation are only discoverable by reading the body, so a reviewer cannot see what was inserted or where, even though Reject does remove them.
items.source: explore:review:tracked insertions of a citation or an equation show a history card with identical before/after text and no mark in the

items.title: A tracked deletion is struck through at the start of the paragraph when the deleted text's trailing context repeats earl
items.why: Exploratory pass on review (visual): expected The deleted 'X ' is drawn where it was removed, between the two occurrences of 'tail': 'tail [X ]tail'.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Open a new document. 2. Triple-click the first body paragraph to select it and type 'tail X tail' to replace it. 3. Review tab > Track changes. 4. Click at the start of that paragraph, press ArrowRight five times, then hold Shift and press ArrowRight twice to select 'X '. 5. Press Backspace and wait about 2.5 s; open History to confirm one tracked change.
Actual: The strike-through is rendered before all of the paragraph text: the paragraph reads '[X ]tail tail' and the deletion widget's offset in the paragraph is 0 instead of 5. The review mark therefore points at the start of the paragraph rather than at the deletion point, and a reviewer checking a repeated phrase sees the wrong location.
items.source: explore:review:a tracked deletion is struck through at the start of the paragraph when the deleted text's trailing context repeats earl

items.title: Returning to Source after an autosaved edit wipes the undo history and rewrites the pane
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (functional): expected The typed comment is still in the source pane and Ctrl+Z undoes the last source edit, exactly as it does when Ctrl+Z is pressed before switching views.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the app, click Source in the status bar and place the caret inside the body (before \end{document}). Type a line '% Autosave comment note' plus a new line 'Probe commented body line.', then wait ~2 s until Apply source disables (the autosave committed the draft). Click Visual, then Source. Press Ctrl+Z three times.
Actual: The pane is regenerated from the visual model: the comment disappears and all three Ctrl+Z presses leave the text unchanged (Apply source stays disabled, so the history was reset). The same edit is undone normally if Ctrl+Z is pressed before leaving the pane.
items.source: explore:source-editor:returning to source after an autosaved edit wipes the undo history and rewrites the pane

items.title: 'Refresh from visual' destroys the unsaved draft instantly and it cannot be undone
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (ux): expected A confirmation, or an undoable replacement, so a mistaken Refresh does not destroy the hand-written draft.
items.hint:
Repro: In Source mode add '% Hand-written draft to keep' plus 'Second draft line.' to the body so Apply source is enabled. Click 'Refresh from visual' within the autosave window, then click into the textarea and press Ctrl+Z.
Actual: The draft is replaced with generated LaTeX immediately; no toast or confirmation appears and Ctrl+Z after refocusing the textarea does nothing (the undo history was reset).
items.source: explore:source-editor:'refresh from visual' destroys the unsaved draft instantly and it cannot be undone

items.title: Focus stays on 'Refresh from visual', so typing right after the click is silently dropped
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (ux): expected The source editor regains focus so the keystrokes land in the document, as they do after Apply source (activeElement is the LaTeX textarea).
items.hint:
Repro: Source mode. Edit the text so Apply source is enabled and click 'Refresh from visual'. Without clicking the textarea first, type 'typed-right-after-refresh'.
Actual: document.activeElement remains the 'Refresh from visual' button and the textarea value never receives the typed text.
items.source: explore:source-editor:focus stays on 'refresh from visual', so typing right after the click is silently dropped

items.title: The parse-error toast keeps showing an error after the corrected source saves successfully
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (ux): expected The error notice clears as soon as the corrected draft parses and the autosave succeeds.
items.hint:
Repro: In Source mode add '\section{Unclosed probe' before \end{document} and click Apply source (toast: 'Invalid LaTeX: missing closing brace.'). Change the line to '\section{Repaired probe}' and wait ~1.6 s for the autosave.
Actual: The save-error button disappears, Apply source disables and the visual document shows 'Repaired probe', but the toast still reads 'Invalid LaTeX: missing closing brace.' until its 4 s timeout; it is still on screen after switching to Visual.
items.source: explore:source-editor:the parse-error toast keeps showing an error after the corrected source saves successfully

items.title: LaTeX parse errors are transient and never say which line failed
items.why: Exploratory pass on source-editor (ux): expected The message points at the failing line (for example 'line 58') and remains available beside the source until the draft is fixed.
items.hint:
Repro: In Source mode insert '\section{Unclosed probe' before \end{document}, click Apply source, then read the toast and the line gutter and wait ~4 s.
Actual: The toast says only 'Invalid LaTeX: missing closing brace.', no gutter line is highlighted (0 elements with the active class), and after ~4 s the toast is gone with no 'Invalid LaTeX' text anywhere on the page; only a 'Retry save' button remains, with the reason hidden in its tooltip/aria-label.
items.source: explore:source-editor:latex parse errors are transient and never say which line failed

items.title: Page count, line wrapping and page margins change when the window is resized, so a 13-page document reports 11 pages
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (functional): expected Pagination is a property of the paper settings, not the window: at every pane width the document keeps 13 pages, the same line wrapping, and the same 96px page margins (scaled uniformly with the sheet when the page is too wide to show at 100%).
items.hint:
Repro: Run `node qa/probes/long-document.mjs` and read `stages.windowWidth`. Or by hand at 1280x800: create a project, clear the page, and paste 50 headings each followed by the probe's 69-word paragraph (unique words: 3,600 total). The status bar reads `3,600 words / 13 pages`, the sheet is 14,599px tall, 300 text line boxes are rendered and the 96px page margins measure 97px left and 99px right. Resize the window to 1180x800: the same untouched document now reads `3,600 words / 11 pages`, the sheet is 12,353px tall, only 250 line boxes are rendered, the paragraph after `Heading 2 HDOC2` rewraps from 5 lines to 4, and its text insets from the paper edge fall to 66px left and 68px right. At 1024x768 it stays 11 pages with 53px/55px insets. Resizing back to 1280x800 restores 13 pages, 300 line boxes and 97px/99px insets.
Actual: Once the sheet is fit-scaled (window narrower than about 1200px) the text column grows inside the page: the 96px margins shrink to 66px/68px at 1180 and 53px/55px at 1024, paragraphs rewrap, and the page count drops from 13 to 11. The status bar shows 11 pages and the sheet is drawn 2 pages shorter, while the document text and paper settings are unchanged.
items.source: explore:long-document:page count, line wrapping and page margins change when the window is resized, so a 13-page document reports 11 pages

items.title: Resizing the window mid-document jumps the scroll position about two pages and leaves the caret off-screen
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (functional): expected Resizing the pane keeps the document point under the viewport and the caret visible, the way opening and closing the Document properties panel does.
items.hint:
Repro: Run `node qa/probes/long-document.mjs` and read `stages.resizeScroll`. Or by hand at 1280x800 with the 50-heading/3,600-word document: click `Heading 25` in the outline, scroll `BODY25` into view, click into its text and wait. The scroller is at scrollTop 6,773 with the caret at y=503 (visible; editor viewport y=149-776). Resize the window to 1200x800, which does not change the page count (still 13 pages): scrollTop jumps to 8,817 and the caret moves to y=-1,934, above the viewport. Resize back to 1280x800: scrollTop is 9,333 and the caret is at y=-2,057, still off-screen; the editor is showing a different part of the document from the one being edited.
Actual: A width-only resize fires the pane-rescale path and moves the scroll offset by about 2,044px even though the page count is unchanged; the caret and the paragraph being edited end up far above the viewport and do not return when the window is restored.

items.title: Typing latency grows with document length: about 13ms per character at 3,600 words and 90ms at 37,200 words
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (ux): expected Typing stays responsive in long documents: the per-keystroke cost does not grow with the number of paragraphs/pages, and the character appears within a frame or two as it does on a blank page.
items.hint:
Repro: Run `node qa/probes/long-document.mjs` and read `stages.typing`. At 1280x800 type the same 70-character sample (` Typing latency sample with several ordinary words in a long document.`) at the end of the 3,600-word document, then clear the page and paste 400 copies and 1,200 copies of the probe's 30-word paragraph to reach 12,400 and 37,200 words and type the sample again. Across two runs the median gap between input events is 4.2-4.3ms on a blank page, 12.4-13.1ms at 3,600 words, 25.8-27.7ms at 12,400 words and 89.3-94.8ms at 37,200 words; p90 rises to 24.3-26.0 / 40.3-45.5 / 124.1-185.7ms and typing the 70 characters takes 0.88-0.95s / 1.73s / 6.64-7.59s. Page count also grows to 25 and 72 pages in those two cases.
Actual: The pagination pass runs on every document update, so the input handling cost scales with the document. At 12,400 words each character already takes about 26-28ms (under 40 chars/s) and at 37,200 words about 90-95ms (about 11 chars/s), with observed input gaps up to 225ms.
items.source: explore:long-document:typing latency grows with document length: about 13ms per character at 3,600 words and 90ms at 37,200 words

items.title: Deleting the whole long document leaves the single remaining page scrolled 386px down with its top off-screen
items.why: Exploratory pass on long-document (visual): expected Clearing the document scrolls back to the top of the remaining page, so the page's top edge and the caret are visible, matching a newly created empty document view.
items.hint:
Repro: Run `node qa/probes/long-document.mjs` and read `stages.clearAll`. At 1280x800 with the 50-heading/3,600-word document, press Ctrl+A then Backspace. The status bar correctly drops to `0 words / 1 page`, the outline count goes to 0 and the sheet shrinks to one page (1,123px), but the scroller stays at scrollTop 416 of a 606px range: the page's top edge is at y=-386 relative to the editor viewport (page spans -386 to 737 in the 627px viewport). The top 386px of the page, including the top margin, are off-screen.
Actual: The old scroll offset survives the shrink; the viewport ends up looking at the lower part of the single blank page with no page top edge visible.

items.title: A failed recent-projects write reports a fully saved document as unsaved
items.why: Exploratory pass on persistence (ux): expected The document's saved state should follow the workspace snapshot: once sentence.workspace holds the current text the indicator should read 'Saved locally'. A failure to write the auxiliary recent-projects list should be reported separately or ignored rather than turning a saved document into 'Editing'/'Not saved' with an error toast.
items.hint:
Repro: 1) Open http://localhost:1420 in a fresh browser profile, click 'New document' and wait for the top bar to read 'Saved locally'. 2) In the devtools console run: const orig = Storage.prototype.setItem; Storage.prototype.setItem = function (key, value) { if (key === 'sentence.recent') throw new DOMException('The quota has been exceeded.', 'QuotaExceededError'); return orig.call(this, key, value); }; . 3) Type a unique marker at the end of the document and wait 1.6 s: the top bar shows 'Editing' with a 'Retry save: The quota has been exceeded.' button and an error toast, while localStorage['sentence.workspace'] already contains the marker (check with JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('sentence.workspace'))). 4) Reload: the marker is still in the editor and the bar now reads 'Saved locally'. 5) For the boot variant, apply the same override before the page loads (Playwright page.addInitScript / CDP Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument) and reload: the unchanged, restored document displays 'Not saved' with the same Retry save control and error toast, even though its text is present in the editor and in localStorage. Probe evidence: qa/probes/persistence.mjs phases 'recent-write-failure' (storedHasMarker true, editorHasMarker true, indicator label 'Editing', retry 'Retry save: The quota has been exceeded.') and 'recent-boot-indicator' (label 'Not saved', retry present, hasAlpha true, storedHasAlpha true).
Actual: In persist() the result of rememberProject(current) is assigned to recentError and, if set, saveError is populated and saveState is forced to 'error' (src/App.tsx:999-1002), so the heading renders 'Editing' while dirty is true. On boot the workspace effect calls rememberProject (src/App.tsx:1175-1177); with dirty false the TopBar renders 'Not saved' (src/components/TopBar.tsx:41). The 'Retry save' control cannot clear the state while the recent-list key stays unwritable, even though the document itself is persisted and survives a reload.
items.source: explore:persistence:a failed recent-projects write reports a fully saved document as unsaved

items.title: Deleting a comment drops keyboard focus on <body> and the next keystrokes are silently discarded
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (functional): expected After a comment is deleted, focus moves to the next or previous comment card, the Review rail or the editor, so the keyboard user keeps a usable position and later typing is not thrown away.
items.hint:
Repro: Open a project, select body text, go to Review and activate "New comment"; type a note and press Ctrl+Enter. Click the Review rail to show the panel. Tab to the first "Delete comment" button and press Enter. The thread disappears and document.activeElement becomes BODY. Type "LOST": the document text does not change.
Actual: Probe data: comment cards went 2 -> 1, document.activeElement is BODY (bodyFocused true), and typing "LOST" left the editor text without that word (typed false).
items.source: explore:keyboard:deleting a comment drops keyboard focus on <body> and the next keystrokes are silently discarded

items.title: Paragraph spacing popover has a detached tab order: Shift+Tab jumps to the status-bar Zoom in, and Tab past the last fie
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected The popover keeps its focus order anchored to its trigger and controls: Shift+Tab from the first field returns to the Paragraph spacing button, and leaving the last field either continues to a usable control or closes the popover (as the Text color palette does).
items.hint:
Repro: In a project open the Home ribbon tab, focus "Paragraph spacing" and press Enter (focus lands in the Before field). Press Shift+Tab once: focus goes to the status-bar "Zoom in" button. Focus the Before field again, press Tab (moves to After) and Tab again: document.activeElement is BODY while the .spacing-panel is still open.
Actual: Probe data: after Shift+Tab activeElement = BUTTON "Zoom in"; after two forward Tabs activeElement = BODY; document.querySelectorAll(".spacing-panel").length = 1, so the dialog is still open with focus outside it.
items.source: explore:keyboard:paragraph spacing popover has a detached tab order: shift+tab jumps to the status-bar zoom in, and tab past the last fie

items.title: Comment cards in the Review panel are mouse-only: the ARTICLE is not focusable and has no keyboard path to select a comm
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected Each comment card is reachable with Tab (role/button or tabIndex 0) and Enter/Space selects it, and the selected state is exposed to assistive technology, so selecting a comment is not a mouse-only action.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a comment, open the Review rail, and inspect the .comment-thread cards. Click the second card: its class changes from no "active" to "active" (the comment is selected). Now Tab through the panel: focus visits the other rail buttons and then the Resolve comment, Delete comment and Reply buttons, never the card itself.
Actual: Probe data for the cards: tag ARTICLE, tabIndex -1, role null, hasClick true, hasKey false. A click moves the active flag to the second card, but no focusable control performs the same action.
items.source: explore:keyboard:comment cards in the review panel are mouse-only: the article is not focusable and has no keyboard path to select a comm

items.title: LaTeX source file switcher exposes no selected state, and the textarea is still named "LaTeX source" while editing refer
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected The file switcher is a labelled tablist with aria-selected (or an equivalent pressed state) and the textarea's accessible name identifies the open file, for example "references.bib source", so a screen-reader user knows which file is being edited.
items.hint:
Repro: Press Ctrl+Alt+2 to open the source pane and inspect .source-file-tabs. Both buttons are plain buttons (role null, aria-selected null, aria-pressed null); only the CSS class active marks document.tex. Focus references.bib and press Enter: the textarea shows @article{sentence2026, ... and the active class moves, but the textarea's aria-label is still "LaTeX source".
Actual: Probe data: tabs = [{text:"document.tex", role:null, selected:null, pressed:null, cls:"active"}, {text:"references.bib", role:null, selected:null, pressed:null}]; after switching, the value starts "@article{sentence2026," and the textarea aria-label remains "LaTeX source".
items.source: explore:keyboard:latex source file switcher exposes no selected state, and the textarea is still named "latex source" while editing refer

items.title: Ribbon tablist ignores Home and End, so only the arrow keys move between ribbon tabs
items.why: Exploratory pass on keyboard (ux): expected End moves focus and selection to the last ribbon tab (Git) and Home moves them to the first, matching the workspace tabs and the usual ARIA tabs keyboard model.
items.hint:
Repro: Focus the Home ribbon tab (role=tab) and press End; inspect document.activeElement and the aria-selected tab. Then focus the Git tab and press Home.
Actual: Probe data: after End on Home, document.activeElement is still BUTTON#ribbon-tab-home "Home" and the only tab with aria-selected="true" is Home. After Home on Git, focus and selection remain on Git. ArrowRight/ArrowLeft do move between tabs.
items.source: explore:keyboard:ribbon tablist ignores home and end, so only the arrow keys move between ribbon tabs

items.title: Inserting an image with the caret inside a verbatim block truncates the code and moves the rest of it into prose
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (functional): expected The code block keeps both lines and its monospace/verbatim form, and the picture is inserted as a block before or after the code (as it already is when the caret is at the start of the block, which produces a figure before the verbatim block), or the Image command is disabled inside a code block.
items.source: explore:insert-media:inserting an image with the caret inside a verbatim block truncates the code and moves the rest of it into prose

items.title: An image that fits the page in a two-column document is exported at its natural width and runs across both columns and o
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (visual): expected An image displayed inside the text block is exported at a width that fits the column it is placed in (for example width=\linewidth in twocolumn), so the compiled PDF matches the visual page and stays inside the right margin.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the demo project and set Layout > Columns to Two. Press Ctrl+End, click Insert > Image and choose a 500x100 PNG. The page still shows one 600 px column and draws the picture 502x102 px inside it. View > LaTeX contains '\documentclass[11pt,a4paper,twocolumn]{article}' and '\includegraphics[width=375.00bp]{assets/images/column-probe.png}'. Compile that source with the bundled engine (src-tauri/binaries/tectonic-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --untrusted main.tex, with the asset at assets/images/column-probe.png): the log reports 'Overfull \hbox (154.9223pt too wide) in paragraph at lines 62--63' and the rendered page shows the red picture starting in the left column, crossing the column gap and the right column, and ending at the page edge. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario 'image-two-columns'.
Actual: imageOptions compares the 500 px natural width with the single-column text width (602 px) and writes the image at 375 bp; a twocolumn article's \columnwidth is about 221 pt, so the graphic is 155 pt too wide, overlaps the second column and is clipped by the page edge. The visual page never shows the two-column layout, so the mismatch is invisible before compiling.
items.source: explore:insert-media:an image that fits the page in a two-column document is exported at its natural width and runs across both columns and o

items.title: An image inserted at the end of a blockquote or list item is destroyed by Apply source: the figure becomes accent-mangle
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (functional): expected A block image at the end of a quote or list item either survives Apply source as a figure with its caption, or is inserted after the quote/list rather than inside it (the behavior page breaks and contents already have), so the visual document and the re-exported LaTeX keep the picture and the caption.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the demo project, click the blockquote text ('Clarity arrives when the mechanics disappear...'), press End, then Insert > Image and choose a PNG. Click the image, type 'Quoted caption' in Figure caption and press Tab. View > LaTeX shows the figure inside the quote ('\begin{quote} ... \begin{figure}[htbp] ... \caption{Quoted caption} \end{figure} \end{quote}'). Go back to Visual, then to LaTeX and click Apply source (a space plus Backspace enables it). In Visual the quote now has one paragraph and no figure: its text is 'Clarity arrives when the mechanics disappear and only the thought remains. e̱gin{figure}[htbp] ȩntering a̧ption{Quoted caption} \end{figure}', with the image demoted to an inline img. Type one character in the quote and View > LaTeX: the corrupted text is exported as '\\e̱gin\{figure\}[htbp]' and '\textbackslash{}end\{figure\}'. The same happens with a figure at the end of a list item: the item becomes '... \texttt{meaning = structure + language}. e̱gin{figure}[htbp] ȩntering \end{figure}' with 0 figures. Probe scenarios 'quote-image-roundtrip' and 'list-image-roundtrip' in qa/probes/insert-media.mjs.
Actual: The exported source is valid before the sync, but the importer parses the figure markup inside the quote/list as inline text: \b, \c and \c are read as accent commands ('e̱gin', 'ȩntering', 'a̧ption'), the figure node disappears, the image becomes an inline image, and the caption turns into literal punctuation text. The corrupted text is then re-exported as escaped prose (backslashes written as \textbackslash{}).
items.source: explore:insert-media:an image inserted at the end of a blockquote or list item is destroyed by apply source: the figure becomes accent-mangle

items.title: A page break left as the last block shows a second blank page and '2 pages' while the exported PDF has one page
items.why: Exploratory pass on insert-media (content): expected The page count reflects what the exported document produces: either the trailing break does not add a blank page to the visual sheet/status bar, or the export emits something that really produces the blank page the editor shows.
items.hint:
Repro: Open the demo project, press Ctrl+End and click Insert > Page break. Do not type after it. The editor shows two page sheets (sheetHeight 2246 px for two 1123 px pages) and the status bar reads '92 words 2 pages'; page two contains only two empty paragraphs. View > LaTeX ends with '... language}.

\end{document}'. Compile that exact source with the bundled Tectonic engine: pdfinfo reports Pages: 1, because 
ewpage followed by \end{document} ships no second page. Probe qa/probes/insert-media.mjs scenario 'page-break-at-end'.
Actual: The visual sheet and the status bar count 2 pages, but the compiled PDF is 1 page; the second page the user sees (and the '2 pages' count) never reaches the output.

items.title: A list nested five levels deep exports LaTeX that the bundled engine refuses to compile
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (functional): expected Nesting stops at four levels (the article class defines only enumi-enumiv/itemi-itemiv) or the exporter writes compilable LaTeX for deeper levels (for example an enumitem setlistdepth declaration).
items.hint:
Repro: New document. Click Home > Numbered list. Type L1, press Enter, type L2, press Tab; repeat Enter + type L3 + Tab; L4 + Tab; L5 + Tab. Open View > LaTeX and read the body.
Actual: The editor builds all five levels and View > LaTeX contains five nested \begin{enumerate} environments. Running the bundled Tectonic engine on the exported source (src-tauri/binaries/tectonic-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --untrusted) exits 1 with "LaTeX Error: Too deeply nested." at the fifth environment and produces no PDF; a four-level list compiles. Five-level bullet lists fail the same way ("Too deeply nested." with five nested itemize environments).
items.source: explore:lists:a list nested five levels deep exports latex that the bundled engine refuses to compile

items.title: A bulleted or numbered list inside a table cell is flattened into concatenated text in the exported LaTeX
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (content): expected The cell keeps its two list items (an itemize/enumerate inside a p{} cell or equivalent), or list commands are disabled inside table cells with an explanation.
items.hint:
Repro: New document. Insert > Insert table (3x3). Click the first body cell (row 2, column 1). Home > Bulleted list, type "first item", press Enter, type "second item". View > LaTeX and read the tabular row. Actual: The visual cell shows

  • first item

  • second item

, but the exported row is "first itemsecond item & & \\": there is no \item and the two items are joined without even a space, so the PDF prints one merged run. A numbered list in the same cell exports as "one celltwo cell".

items.title: A numbered list typed as "0. " shows 0 in the editor but exports an enumerate starting at 1
items.why: Exploratory pass on lists (content): expected The editor and the PDF agree: the visible 0 is preserved (for example with \setcounter{enumi}{-1}) or the editor starts the list at 1.
items.hint:

Actual: The editor DOM is <ol start="0"> and shows "0. zero item" / "1. next item", but the exported source is a plain \begin{enumerate} with no \setcounter, so the PDF numbers the same items 1. and 2.

items.title: Source round trip drops empty rows from one-column tables; a 1x1 empty table disappears and its LaTeX becomes body text
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (functional): expected The one-column table keeps all three rows (Head plus two empty body rows), and the single empty cell stays an editable 1x1 table. Empty rows are table structure and must survive the parse.
items.hint:
Repro: New document. Insert tab > Insert table (3x3, header row). Click the first body cell, then Table toolbar > Delete column twice, leaving one column. Click the header cell and type Head. Open the source pane (status-bar Source), append a space to the source so Apply source enables, click Apply source, then Visual. For the 1x1 case: New document > Insert table, click the first body cell, Delete column twice and Delete row twice, leaving a single empty header cell; make the same trivial source edit, Apply source, then Visual.
Actual: The 3x1 table returns as 1x1: only the row containing Head survives, and both empty body rows are dropped. The 1x1 table disappears entirely (0 tables in the editor) and its LaTeX is inserted as paragraph text, rendered as 'egin{table}[htbp] entering egin{tabular}{l} \hline \hline \end{tabular} \end{table}' (the \b and \c sequences are decoded as accent macros); the status bar reports 7 words and the toast says 'Visual document synchronized from LaTeX.' The source pane still shows the original 3-row tabular, so source and visual disagree. Both cases reproduce from the trivial 'append a space + Apply source' edit, not only from a hand-written tabular. Evidence: qa/shots/probe-tables-narrow.png, probe scenarios narrowTableRoundTrip and trivialSourceEdit.
items.source: explore:tables:source round trip drops empty rows from one-column tables; a 1x1 empty table disappears and its latex becomes body text

items.title: Shift+Tab in the first table cell jumps to the sidebar History button and discards the next keystrokes
items.why: Exploratory pass on tables (functional): expected Shift+Tab at the start of the table keeps the caret in the text flow (for example, in the paragraph before the table), mirroring what Tab does after the last cell, so continued typing lands in the document.
items.hint:
Repro: New document. Insert tab > Insert table (3x3). Click the first (header) cell, type first. Click the second body row's middle cell and type mid. Click the first header cell again, press Shift+Tab, then type X without clicking anywhere.
Actual: document.activeElement becomes the sidebar BUTTON labelled History (activeElement.closest('.tiptap, .ProseMirror') is false). The caret is still painted in the first cell, but typing X adds no text anywhere; the editor text remains 'first mid', so the keystroke is silently discarded. Probe scenario tableBoundaries, check 'Shift+Tab in the first cell keeps typing inside the document'.
items.source: explore:tables:shift+tab in the first table cell jumps to the sidebar history button and discards the next keystrokes

items.why: Exploratory pass on math (content): expected The align and gather environments become editable math blocks (with their environment names) inside the quote and list item, as a top-level align does; if the container form is unsupported, Apply source must report it instead of rewriting the environment.

items.title: Equation block dialog accepts a full align environment and exports it nested inside equation*, which amsmath rejects
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (content): expected The dialog stores the input as an align math block (environment 'align') or rejects a complete environment in the single-equation dialog; the export should be one align environment.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and type "Nested " in the editor.
2. Open Insert > Equation block.
3. Enter:
\begin{align}
a &= b \\
c &= d
\end{align}
4. The preview is valid and Insert is enabled; click Insert.
5. Open View > LaTeX, click Refresh from visual, and compile the generated body with the bundled Tectonic.
Actual: Insert creates a mathBlock with data-math-environment absent and data-numbered="false". Refresh from visual wraps the input in an equation* block: the exported body starts with `\begin{equation*}` followed by `\begin{align}` and ends with `\end{align}` then `\end{equation*}`. Tectonic 0.17.0 stops with `! Package amsmath Error: Erroneous nesting of equation structures;` and writes no pages. The same acceptance happens for a pasted `\begin{equation}...\end{equation}` and `\begin{gather}...\end{gather}`.
items.source: explore:math:equation block dialog accepts a full align environment and exports it nested inside equation*, which amsmath rejects

items.title: The math dialog accepts \mathscr, \bm and \cancel but the exported preamble loads none of their packages
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (content): expected Either the preamble loads the packages the preview supports (mathrsfs, bm, cancel) or the dialog rejects those commands with an explanation that the package is unavailable.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and insert an inline equation three times (Insert > Inline equation), using \mathscr{A}, \bm{x} and \cancel{x} in turn. Each preview renders the formula and Insert is enabled.
2. Open View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual.
3. Read the preamble: it lists fontspec, amsmath/amssymb, graphicx, booktabs, ulem, microtype, hyperref, fancyhdr and geometry, but no mathrsfs, bm or cancel.
4. Compile the three formulas with the bundled Tectonic using that package set.
Actual: The exported body contains `\(\mathscr{A}\)\(\bm{x}\)\(\cancel{x}\)` and the preamble has no mathrsfs, bm or cancel. Tectonic fails with `! Undefined control sequence.` for each of the three, while the dialog reported no error, the preview rendered every formula, and the visual page showed all three.
items.source: explore:math:the math dialog accepts \mathscr, \bm and \cancel but the exported preamble loads none of their packages

items.title: Valid empty display math ($$ $$) is re-exported as an equation* with a blank line and no longer compiles
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (content): expected The empty formula round-trips as a valid empty equation (for example \begin{equation*}\end{equation*} with no blank line), or Apply source rejects it; it must not turn a compilable document into an uncompilable one.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and open View > LaTeX.
2. Replace the body before \end{document} with: Before $$ $$ after.
3. Click Apply source (the toast reports success). The visual page contains an empty 600x36 equation block with data-latex="".
4. Open View > LaTeX and click Refresh from visual.
5. Compile the generated body with the bundled Tectonic.
Actual: Refresh from visual emits a blank line between `\begin{equation*}` and `\end{equation*}`. Tectonic stops with `! Missing $ inserted.` and writes no pages. Applying the export again is reported as synchronized and reproduces the same blank-line block. The original `Before $$ $$ after.` compiles without error.
items.source: explore:math:valid empty display math ($$ $$) is re-exported as an equation* with a blank line and no longer compiles

items.title: Valid math containing the literal text "katex-error" is rejected by the dialog as unrenderable
items.why: Exploratory pass on math (functional): expected The formula inserts and exports, because \text{katex-error} is valid amsmath and compiles.
items.hint:
Repro: 1. Create a project and open Insert > Inline equation.
2. Enter \text{katex-error} (or \text{__sentence_katex_error__}).
3. Look at the preview and the Insert button state.
Actual: The preview renders the text, but Insert is disabled and the dialog shows 'This LaTeX could not be rendered. Check the syntax and try again.'; there are zero .katex-error nodes and .math-preview-invalid is present. The validity check scans the rendered HTML for the substrings 'katex-error' and '__sentence_katex_error__', so legitimate formula text matching those strings is marked invalid. Tectonic compiles `\(\text{katex-error}\)` without error, and the same formula inserted from the source pane round-trips fine, so only the dialog blocks it.
items.source: explore:math:valid math containing the literal text "katex-error" is rejected by the dialog as unrenderable

items.title: A footnote inserted in a table cell is silently dropped from the compiled PDF
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (content): expected The footnote body is printed in the PDF, as the same footnote is in a normal paragraph or a list item, or the app refuses or relocates a footnote in a table.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project and clear the demo body (Ctrl+A, Backspace, twice). Insert > Insert table. Click the first cell of the second row, type "Cell text", then Insert > Footnote, enter "Table UI note" and click Insert. View > LaTeX shows the footnote inside the tabular row. Save the exported document, compile it with `src-tauri/binaries/tectonic-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -X compile <file>.tex --outdir <dir>`, and run `pdftotext <file>.pdf -`.
Actual: The PDF contains only "Cell text1" and an empty footnote line ("1"); the string "Table UI note" does not appear anywhere in the extracted PDF text. The footnote marker's link annotation is also empty (pdftohtml reports `<a href="">`). The probe's list-item control, compiled the same way, prints "List note", so the loss is specific to the table cell.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:a footnote inserted in a table cell is silently dropped from the compiled pdf

items.title: A footnote in a heading that the table of contents lists is duplicated and leaves a marker in the contents entry
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (content): expected The contents entry is "Footnote Heading" with no footnote marker, and the note is printed once in the section body.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project and clear the body. Insert > Contents (the Insert tab's Contents button). Press Ctrl+End, Enter, type "Footnote Heading", then Home > Apply heading. Click at the end of the heading and Insert > Footnote with "Toc heading note". Open View > LaTeX, compile the export with the bundled Tectonic, and run `pdftotext` on the PDF.
Actual: The visual contents block becomes "1 Footnote Heading" (the footnote marker is rendered inside the TOC). The exported source is `\section{Footnote Heading\protect\footnote{Toc heading note}}`. The compiled PDF contains "Toc heading note" twice: the contents page shows "1 Footnote Heading" plus a footnote numbered 2, and the section page shows the heading with the note numbered 1. pdftotext reads "Contents 1 Footnote Heading1 1 Footnote Heading2 ... Toc heading note Toc heading note".
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:a footnote in a heading that the table of contents lists is duplicated and leaves a marker in the contents entry

items.title: Optional-argument citations are silently corrupted by Apply source
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (content): expected The optional note is preserved as `\cite[p.~5]{sentence2026}`, or Apply source reports the form as unsupported instead of rewriting the paragraph.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project and clear the body. View > LaTeX, insert `Optional \cite[p.~5]{sentence2026} cite.` before `\end{document}`, and click Apply source. Type one character at the end of the visual document, then open View > LaTeX. Compile the export with Tectonic and run `pdftotext`.
Actual: Apply reports "Visual document synchronized from LaTeX." and creates zero citation nodes. The visual paragraph is "Optional i̧te[p. 5]{sentence2026} cite."; the re-exported line is `Optional i̧te[p.~5]\{sentence2026\} cite.X`, and the PDF prints the same corrupted text instead of a citation (the `\c` in `\cite` is consumed as a cedilla accent). The probe compiles the untouched input separately as `citationOptionalArgumentOriginal` (Tectonic exit 0; its PDF shows `Optional [?, p. 5] cite.`), so the original is valid and the corruption is introduced by Apply source.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:optional-argument citations are silently corrupted by apply source

items.title: Grouping braces in an imported footnote are escaped after a visual edit, so the PDF prints the braces
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (content): expected The grouping braces keep their LaTeX meaning and do not print; the footnote re-exports as `\footnote{The {NASA} study}`, or Apply source rejects the grouping instead of silently changing it.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project and clear the body. View > LaTeX, insert `Braced note \footnote{The {NASA} study} end.` before `\end{document}`, and click Apply source. The visual footnote is "The {NASA} study" and the paragraph is "Braced note 1 end.". Type one character at the end of the document, open View > LaTeX, compile the export and run `pdftotext`.
Actual: The re-exported line is `Braced note \footnote{The \{NASA\} study} end.X`; the compiled PDF prints "The {NASA} study" with the braces visible.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:grouping braces in an imported footnote are escaped after a visual edit, so the pdf prints the braces

items.title: The Add link dialog accepts addresses that produce malformed PDF link targets (space and braces)
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (functional): expected The address is percent-encoded (space to %20, braces to %7B/%7D) or rejected with an error; the clickable PDF target is the address the user entered.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project and clear the body. Type "word0", select it, Home > Add link, enter `https://space.example.org/a b`, Insert. Add "word1", link it to `https://brace.example.org/a{b}` the same way. Open View > LaTeX and compile; dump the PDF link annotations with `pdftohtml -xml -stdout -i -noframes <pdf>`.
Actual: Both links are accepted with no error. The export is `\href{https://space.example.org/a b}{word0}` and `\href{https://brace.example.org/a\{b\}}{word1}`. The PDF annotations are `href="https://space.example.org/a b"` (raw space) and `href="https://brace.example.org/a\{b\}"` (literal backslashes), so the clickable target is not the address.
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:the add link dialog accepts addresses that produce malformed pdf link targets (space and braces)

items.title: The Edit link dialog's confirm button is still labelled Insert
items.why: Exploratory pass on links-cites-footnotes (ux): expected The dialog's confirm button says Update, matching the Edit citation, Edit footnote and Edit cross-reference dialogs.
items.hint:
Repro: Create a project, type "LinkFlow alpha", select "alpha", Home > Add link, enter `https://first.example.org`, click Insert. Click the linked word, then Home > Add link again.
Actual: The dialog title is "Edit link" and the address is prefilled, but its buttons are "Remove link", "Cancel", "Insert"; clicking Insert updates the existing link. The probe records the button list as ["", "Remove link", "Cancel", "Insert"] (the empty entry is the Close icon).
items.source: explore:links-cites-footnotes:the edit link dialog's confirm button is still labelled insert
